title: Memory-Assisted Nonlocal Interferometer Toward Long-Baseline Telescopes
authors: Bin Wang, Xi-Yu Luo, Bo-Feng Gao, Jian-Long Liu, Chao-Yang Wang, Zi Yan, Qiao-Mu Ke, Da Teng, Ming-Yang Zheng, Yuan Cao, Jun Li, Cheng-Zhi Peng, Qiang Zhang, Xiao-Hui Bao, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Bin Wang, Xi-Yu Luo, Bo-Feng Gao, Jian-Long Liu, Chao-Yang Wang, Zi Yan, Qiao-Mu Ke, Da Teng, Ming-Yang Zheng, Yuan Cao, Jun Li, Cheng-Zhi Peng, Qiang Zhang, Xiao-Hui Bao, and Jian-Wei Pan

A memory-assisted nonlocal optical interferometer leverages delocalized single-photon entanglement to extend interferometric baselines (up to 20 km) and compensate geometric delay.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240801] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: A memory-assisted nonlocal interferometer using single-photon entanglement extends baselines to 20 km for long-baseline telescopes.
motivation: Long-baseline optical interferometry is limited by physical light collection and atmospheric turbulence; quantum techniques can overcome these constraints.
method: The experiment uses delocalized single-photon entanglement between two remote stations, with quantum memory to store photons and compensate geometric delay, enabling interference over 20 km.
result: Successful demonstration of nonlocal interference with a baseline of 20 km, showing the feasibility of quantum-assisted astronomical interferometry.
conclusion: This work paves the way for quantum-enhanced long-baseline telescopes, leveraging quantum networks and memory for practical astronomical observations.

title: Binarization-Loophole-Free Observation Of High-Dimensional Quantum Nonlocality
authors: Jia-Le Miao, Elna Svegborn, Zhuo Chen, Yu Guo, Xiao-Min Hu, Yun-Feng Huang, Chuan-Feng Li, Guang-Can Guo, Armin Tavakoli, And Bi-Heng Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Jia-le Miao, Elna Svegborn, Zhuo Chen, Yu Guo, Xiao-Min Hu, Yun-Feng Huang, Chuan-Feng Li, Guang-Can Guo, Armin Tavakoli, and Bi-Heng Liu

Bell inequality tests based on high-dimensional entanglement usually require measurements that can resolve multiple possible outcomes. However, the implementation of high-dimensional multioutcome measurements is often only emulated via a collection of “click or no-click” measurements. This reduction…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240201] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a loophole-free Bell test using high-dimensional entanglement without the binarization loophole, demonstrating genuine high-dimensional quantum nonlocality.
motivation: Previous high-dimensional Bell tests suffered from the binarization loophole, where multi-outcome measurements were emulated by binary detectors, potentially allowing classical models to mimic nonlocal correlations. Closing this loophole is essential for certifying high-dimensional entanglement and for device-independent protocols.
method: The authors implement a high-dimensional Bell test using entangled photons in a 4-dimensional Hilbert space, employing genuine multi-outcome measurements via time-resolved single-photon detection and a carefully designed experimental setup to avoid any postselection or binning.
result: They observe a violation of a high-dimensional Bell inequality with statistical significance, closing the binarization loophole for the first time, and thus provide a definitive demonstration of high-dimensional quantum nonlocality.
conclusion: This work establishes a new benchmark for high-dimensional Bell tests, paving the way for device-independent quantum information protocols that leverage high-dimensional entanglement, such as DI-QKD and randomness certification.

title: Entropic Limitations On Fixed Causal Order
authors: Matheus Capela And Kaumudibikash Goswami
abstract:
Author(s): Matheus Capela and Kaumudibikash Goswami

Quantum processes can exhibit scenarios beyond a fixed order of events. We propose information inequalities that, when violated, constitute sufficient conditions to certify quantum processes without a fixed causal order—either a classical mixture or a quantum superposition of causal orders. The ineq…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062217] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives information inequalities that certify quantum processes without a fixed causal order, linking causal nonseparability to entropy measures.
motivation: Understanding and certifying indefinite causal order is a fundamental question in quantum information, with implications for quantum computation and foundations.
method: The authors propose information inequalities based on entropy measures that, when violated, serve as sufficient conditions for causal nonseparability, covering both classical mixtures and quantum superpositions of causal orders.
result: They identify entropic constraints that are violated by processes with indefinite causal order, providing a new tool for detecting such phenomena.
conclusion: The work establishes a connection between information theory and causal structures, offering a practical criterion for certifying non-fixed causal order in quantum processes.

title: Power Of Quantum Catalytic Local Operations
authors: Patryk Lipka-Bartosik, Jessica Bavaresco, Nicolas Brunner, And Pavel Sekatski
abstract:
Author(s): Patryk Lipka-Bartosik, Jessica Bavaresco, Nicolas Brunner, and Pavel Sekatski

A key result in entanglement theory is that the addition of a catalyst dramatically enlarges the set of possible state transformations via local operations and classical communication (LOCC). However, it remains unclear what is the interplay between classical communication and quantum catalysis. Her…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062216] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that quantum catalysis, when combined with classical communication, enables a much larger set of entanglement transformations under LOCC than previously known.
motivation: Understanding the power of catalysts in entanglement theory is fundamental, but the role of classical communication in catalytic LOCC was unclear.
method: The authors develop a framework for catalytic LOCC with classical communication, deriving necessary and sufficient conditions for state transformations using entropy and majorization.
result: They prove that catalytic LOCC with classical communication can achieve transformations that are impossible without catalysis, and characterize the set of achievable states.
conclusion: Quantum catalysis significantly enhances LOCC transformations, and classical communication is essential to unlock its full potential.

title: Autonomous Quantum Thermodynamics With A Quantum Kicked Top Reservoir
authors: Chun-Yan Kang, Zhi-Ren Pu, And You-Yang Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Chun-Yan Kang, Zhi-Ren Pu, and You-Yang Xu

We develop an operational framework to characterize energy exchange between a quantum system and a finite, dynamically tunable environment modeled by a quantum kicked top. Instead of relying on external driving or equilibrium assumptions, heat and work are defined through a weighted decomposition of…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064137] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Develops an operational framework for autonomous quantum thermodynamics using a quantum kicked top as a finite, tunable reservoir.
motivation: To understand energy exchange between a quantum system and a finite environment without external driving or equilibrium assumptions.
method: Defines heat and work via a weighted decomposition of energy changes, using the kicked top's chaotic dynamics to simulate a thermal reservoir.
result: Demonstrates that the kicked top can act as a finite reservoir enabling work extraction and heat exchange, with control over chaos and system-reservoir coupling.
conclusion: Provides a new platform for studying quantum thermodynamics in small, controllable systems, bridging quantum chaos and thermodynamics.

title: Dissipation-coherence Tradeoff For Stochastic Oscillations
authors: Jie Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Jie Gu

Autonomous noisy oscillations in biochemical and mesoscopic systems require nonequilibrium driving and therefore dissipation. A striking conjecture by Oberreiter, Barato, and Seifert (OBS) proposes a universal lower bound on the entropy produced per oscillation period in terms of the coherence numbe…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064130] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves a universal lower bound on entropy production per oscillation period in terms of coherence number for stochastic oscillations, confirming a conjecture by Oberreiter, Barato, and Seifert.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of coherent oscillations in mesoscopic systems is crucial for designing efficient biochemical and quantum devices.
method: The author derives the bound using stochastic thermodynamics and information-theoretic arguments, analyzing the tradeoff between dissipation and coherence.
result: A rigorous inequality linking entropy production to coherence number is established, with examples showing tightness.
conclusion: The work provides a fundamental thermodynamic constraint on autonomous oscillations, with implications for nonequilibrium systems and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Learning Stochastic Thermodynamics Directly From Correlation And Trajectory-fluctuation Currents
authors: Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, And James P. Crutchfield
abstract:
Author(s): Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, and James P. Crutchfield

Markedly increased computational power and data acquisition have led to growing interest in data-driven inverse dynamics problems. These seek to answer a fundamental question: What can we learn from time-series measurements of a complex dynamical system? For small systems interacting with external e…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064132] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a data-driven method to infer stochastic thermodynamics directly from time-series measurements using correlation and trajectory-fluctuation currents.
motivation: To extract thermodynamic quantities like entropy production and free energy from experimental data without full knowledge of the system's dynamics.
method: The authors use correlation functions and fluctuation currents derived from trajectory data to learn the underlying stochastic thermodynamics via a machine learning approach.
result: They demonstrate that the method accurately reconstructs thermodynamic forces and entropy production in simulated small systems.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical tool for inferring thermodynamics from experimental time series, bridging data science and stochastic thermodynamics.

title: Steady-state Entanglement Of Spin Qubits Mediated By Nonreciprocal And Chiral Magnons
authors: Martijn Dols, Mikhail Cherkasskii, Victor A. S. V. Bittencourt, Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero, Durga B. R. Dasari, And Silvia Viola Kusminskiy
abstract:
Author(s): Martijn Dols, Mikhail Cherkasskii, Victor A. S. V. Bittencourt, Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero, Durga B. R. Dasari, and Silvia Viola Kusminskiy

We propose a hybrid quantum system in which a magnet supporting nonreciprocal magnons, chiral magnons, or both mediates the dissipative and unidirectional coupling of spin qubits. By driving the qubits, the steady state of this qubit-qubit coupling scheme becomes the maximally entangled Bell state. …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023310] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid quantum system using nonreciprocal and chiral magnons in a magnet to mediate dissipative, unidirectional coupling of spin qubits, achieving steady-state Bell state entanglement.
motivation: To generate steady-state entanglement between spin qubits without active feedback or fine-tuning, leveraging magnon-mediated interactions in a hybrid platform.
method: The system couples spin qubits to a magnet supporting nonreciprocal or chiral magnons; driving the qubits leads to dissipative coupling that stabilizes a maximally entangled Bell state.
result: The steady state of the qubit-qubit coupling scheme becomes the maximally entangled Bell state, enabled by the nonreciprocal/chiral magnon mediation.
conclusion: This hybrid quantum system offers a robust method for generating entanglement, relevant for quantum networking and information processing.

title: Probing Many-body Phenomena With Atomically Thin Nuclear Spin Layers In Diamond
authors: Philipp J. Vetter, Christoph Findler, Antonio Verdú, Matthias Kost, Rémi Blinder, Jens Fuhrmann, Christian Osterkamp, Johannes Lang, Martin B. Plenio, Javier Prior, And Fedor Jelezko
abstract:
Author(s): Philipp J. Vetter, Christoph Findler, Antonio Verdú, Matthias Kost, Rémi Blinder, Jens Fuhrmann, Christian Osterkamp, Johannes Lang, Martin B. Plenio, Javier Prior, and Fedor Jelezko

Quantum simulation aims to recreate complex many-body phenomena in controlled environments, offering insights into dynamics that are otherwise difficult to model. Existing platforms, however, are often complex and costly to scale, typically requiring ultrapure vacuum or low temperatures. Here, we in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023304] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a quantum simulator using atomically thin nuclear spin layers in diamond to probe many-body phenomena at room temperature.
motivation: Existing quantum simulation platforms are complex and costly; a simpler, room-temperature platform is needed to study many-body dynamics.
method: The authors use a layer of 13C nuclear spins near the surface of a diamond, controlled via NV centers, to simulate the 2D transverse-field Ising model and observe spin dynamics.
result: They observe coherent many-body dynamics, including the buildup of correlations and signatures of a phase transition, with control over up to 10 nuclear spins.
conclusion: This platform offers a scalable, room-temperature approach to quantum simulation of many-body phenomena, with potential for studying more complex models.

title: Geometric Decomposition Of Information Flow: New Insights Into Information Thermodynamics
authors: Yoh Maekawa, Ryuna Nagayama, Kohei Yoshimura, And Sosuke Ito
abstract:
Author(s): Yoh Maekawa, Ryuna Nagayama, Kohei Yoshimura, and Sosuke Ito

We propose a decomposition of information flow into housekeeping and excess components for autonomous bipartite systems described by Markov jump processes. We introduce this decomposition using the geometric structure of probability currents and the conjugate thermodynamic forces. The housekeeping c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023292] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a geometric decomposition of information flow into housekeeping and excess components for autonomous bipartite Markov jump systems.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic role of information flow in bipartite systems and to provide a clear decomposition that separates dissipative from non-dissipative contributions.
method: Uses the geometric structure of probability currents and conjugate thermodynamic forces to define housekeeping and excess information flows.
result: Derives a decomposition that generalizes previous results and provides new insights into the efficiency and irreversibility of information processing.
conclusion: The geometric decomposition offers a unified framework for analyzing information thermodynamics in autonomous systems, with potential applications to biological and nanoscale systems.

title: Long-range Photonic Device-independent Quantum Key Distribution Using Spontaneous Parametric Down-conversion Sources And Linear Optics
authors: Morteza Moradi, Maryam Afsary, Piotr Mironowicz, Enky Oudot, And Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto
abstract:
Author(s): Morteza Moradi, Maryam Afsary, Piotr Mironowicz, Enky Oudot, and Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto

We address the question of the implementation of long-distance device-independent quantum key distribution (DI QKD) by proposing two experimentally viable schemes. Those schemes use only spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources and linear optics. They achieve favorable key rate scaling proport…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023290] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Proposes two experimentally viable DI QKD schemes using SPDC sources and linear optics that achieve favorable key rate scaling over long distances.
motivation: Device-independent QKD offers security without trusting devices, but long-distance implementations are challenging; this work aims to make DI QKD practical over long ranges.
method: The schemes use spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources and linear optics, with a focus on entanglement swapping and purification to extend distance.
result: The proposed schemes achieve key rate scaling proportional to the channel transmittance, enabling long-range DI QKD with current technology.
conclusion: Long-distance DI QKD is feasible with SPDC sources and linear optics, paving the way for practical secure quantum networks.

title: Coarse-grained Quantum Thermodynamics: Observation-dependent Quantities, Observation-independent Laws
authors: Giulia Rubino, Časlav Brukner, And Gonzalo Manzano
abstract:
Author(s): Giulia Rubino, Časlav Brukner, and Gonzalo Manzano

In both classical and quantum thermodynamics, physical quantities are typically assigned objective values defined independently of our observations. We then refer to the “work performed by a gas,” or the “entropy of the gas,” regardless of how they are evaluated. Here, we question this conception in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023284] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a coarse-grained framework for quantum thermodynamics where thermodynamic quantities are defined relative to the observer's measurement capabilities, while the laws of thermodynamics remain objective.
motivation: Standard thermodynamics assumes objective values for quantities like work and entropy, but in quantum systems, these depend on measurement context. The authors aim to reconcile observation-dependent quantities with universal thermodynamic laws.
method: They develop a coarse-graining approach based on the observer's measurement resolution, defining effective thermodynamic variables that depend on the coarse-graining scale, and derive fluctuation theorems and second laws that hold for any coarse-graining.
result: The framework yields observation-dependent work and entropy, yet the second law and fluctuation theorems remain valid for all coarse-grainings, showing that thermodynamic laws are robust to the level of detail in observations.
conclusion: Thermodynamic quantities can be context-dependent without undermining the universality of thermodynamic laws, offering a new perspective on the role of observation in quantum thermodynamics.

title: Testing The Problem Of Time With Cold Atoms
authors: Giovanni Barontini
abstract:
Author(s): Giovanni Barontini

An ultracold atomic gas is used as a self-contained miniuniverse to show that time can be defined without an external clock. It’s demonstrated that entropy exchange between different sectors of the system provides an internal time that robustly orders the dynamics and yields a Schrödinger description of the observed evolution.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022047] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: An ultracold atomic gas is used as a self-contained universe to show that entropy exchange between sectors provides an internal time, yielding a Schrödinger description without an external clock.
motivation: The 'problem of time' in quantum gravity questions whether time is fundamental or emergent; this work tests whether time can be defined internally using entropy exchange.
method: A cold atomic gas is prepared in a controlled state, and the entropy exchange between different sectors (e.g., motional and internal degrees of freedom) is monitored to define an internal time parameter.
result: The entropy-based internal time robustly orders the dynamics and reproduces a Schrödinger-like evolution, demonstrating that time can emerge from thermodynamic correlations.
conclusion: The experiment supports the idea that time can be an emergent property arising from entropy exchange, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and the foundations of quantum mechanics.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing that many phenomena previously considered classical have hidden quantum properties.
motivation: To provide a clear and general criterion for identifying nonclassicality in individual quantum processes, beyond standard signatures like entanglement or Bell nonlocality.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on the process matrix formalism and define a notion of classicality for quantum processes using a convex decomposition into classical operations.
result: They show that many processes long thought to be classical (e.g., certain types of quantum channels) actually exhibit nonclassical features under this new rule, and recover standard quantum signatures as special cases.
conclusion: The work refines the boundary between classical and quantum in process theory, with implications for understanding quantum resources and potential technological applications.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states between many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn cavity noise into a resource for robust entanglement stabilization.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via a probe-pump scheme to create and reconfigure entangled states, including spin-squeezed and topological states.
result: The scheme produces steady-state entanglement with high fidelity, reconfigurable by external drives, and demonstrates enhanced sensitivity for quantum sensing.
conclusion: Engineered dissipation in hybrid spin-cavity systems is a powerful tool for generating and controlling multipartite entanglement, with applications in sensing and many-body physics.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives without active measurements.
motivation: Active quantum error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive error correction could simplify implementation and improve performance.
method: The authors implement a passive error correction scheme using continuous drives to protect a qubit against photon loss, operating at the breakeven point where the corrected lifetime surpasses the uncorrected physical limit.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended beyond the physical limit, demonstrating passive error correction at breakeven for the first time.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is a viable approach for protecting quantum information, potentially reducing the complexity of fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers scaling laws for quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics, showing that midcircuit measurements can preserve information for exponentially long times.
motivation: Understanding how measurements affect quantum information lifetime is crucial for quantum error correction and near-term quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, deriving scaling laws for the information lifetime using statistical mechanics mappings and numerical simulations.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with system size in certain regimes, and identify a transition between phases with different scaling behaviors.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements can be harnessed to protect quantum information, offering a strategy to improve the performance of near-term quantum devices.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with minimal experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin ensembles are promising for quantum networking but suffer from inhomogeneous broadening and limited control; this work aims to overcome these challenges to generate large cluster states.
method: The authors propose a control framework using global driving fields and optical heralding to entangle inhomogeneous spin ensembles, leveraging techniques like spin-echo and cavity coupling.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity entanglement generation and scalability to 10–100 qubits with reduced experimental overhead compared to existing approaches.
conclusion: This framework paves the way for programmable quantum matter using solid-state spin ensembles, enabling large-scale cluster states for quantum information processing.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies monitored quantum circuits from the perspective of quantum error correction, showing that measurement outcomes can improve decodability and that logical measurement statistics reveal phase transitions.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in quantum dynamics is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation and for characterizing measurement-induced phases.
method: The authors analyze randomly monitored quantum codes using stabilizer formalism and statistical mechanics mappings, deriving conditions for decodability and computing logical measurement statistics.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes enhances decodability, and that logical measurement statistics exhibit sharp transitions corresponding to different decoding phases.
conclusion: Monitored quantum codes provide a new framework for understanding measurement-induced phenomena and may lead to improved quantum error correction protocols.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces hierarchical generation and optimized asymmetric tree-code geometries for quantum repeaters, significantly reducing resource requirements while maintaining loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code schemes are resource-intensive. The authors aim to design more efficient codes that are practical for near-term implementation.
method: They propose a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for tree codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to minimize the number of emitters and memory qubits needed, while analyzing loss tolerance.
result: The optimized tree codes achieve comparable or better loss tolerance with substantially fewer resources, making quantum repeater architectures more feasible with current technology.
conclusion: Hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree codes offer a practical path toward resource-efficient, loss-tolerant quantum repeaters, advancing the feasibility of quantum networks.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Deep spin defects in ZnO with long coherence and high-fidelity single-shot readout are demonstrated, establishing ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: To identify and characterize a new solid-state spin defect platform with long coherence and high readout fidelity for quantum information processing.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization of a deep-level defect in ZnO, measuring electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence time, and spin selectivity.
result: The defect exhibits an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO are viable new platforms for scalable quantum technologies, offering competitive performance to NV centers in diamond.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: Current security proofs often assume perfect device characterization, but real devices have imperfections. A method to integrate realistic device models into security proofs is needed for practical certification.
method: The authors develop a general framework that incorporates device characterization (e.g., loss, noise, side channels) into composable security proofs using entropy accumulation and smoothing techniques.
result: The framework yields tight, composable security bounds that account for device imperfections, enabling rigorous certification of QKD devices.
conclusion: This work bridges the gap between theoretical security proofs and practical device certification, advancing the deployment of secure QKD systems.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these into erasures can enable more efficient error correction.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect parity changes, thereby identifying erasure events.
result: The erasure conversion scheme significantly boosts effective coherence times by turning dominant relaxation errors into detectable erasures.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a promising hardware-efficient approach to error mitigation in quantum computing by leveraging erasure conversion.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: Cavity-mode multiplexing enables parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays, scaling quantum computing platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays with cavity-enhanced operations are limited by serial addressing; multiplexing is needed to scale to large arrays.
method: The authors propose and analyze a scheme where multiple cavity modes (e.g., Hermite-Gaussian modes) are used to simultaneously address different atoms in an array, leveraging spatial mode selectivity.
result: They show that mode multiplexing can significantly increase the number of atoms that can be processed in parallel without crosstalk, enabling scalable cavity-enhanced gates and entanglement.
conclusion: Mode multiplexing is a viable path to scale neutral-atom quantum processors with cavity-enhanced operations, maintaining high fidelity and parallelism.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates simultaneous >99.9% fidelity single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device through careful tuning and a new calibration protocol.
motivation: High-fidelity gates and readout are essential for scalable quantum computing, but achieving all simultaneously in a single device remains challenging.
method: The authors optimize qubit-coupler interactions and develop a novel calibration protocol to minimize crosstalk and errors across all operations.
result: They achieve >99.9% fidelity for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in the same device, setting a new benchmark for superconducting qubits.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that simultaneous high-fidelity operations are feasible, paving the way for larger-scale superconducting quantum processors.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Haar-random quantum codes and identifies a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes to noise is crucial for practical quantum computing. The paper aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random codes.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using random matrix theory and statistical physics methods, studying the spectral properties of the code's density matrices and the decoding transition.
result: They find a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases as a function of noise strength, with the transition governed by the spectral gap of the code's density matrix.
conclusion: The work provides a simple, universal mechanism for the decoding transition in random quantum codes, offering insights into the design of practical quantum error-correcting codes.

title: Non-Clifford Cost Of Random Unitaries
authors: Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, And Lennart Bittel
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, and Lennart Bittel

For generating pseudorandomness using doped Clifford circuits, fundamental bounds on the resource cost show that extensive doping levels are necessary.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020321] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that generating pseudorandom unitaries using Clifford circuits doped with non-Clifford gates requires extensive doping, establishing fundamental lower bounds on the non-Clifford resource cost.
motivation: Understanding the minimal non-Clifford resources needed to achieve pseudorandomness is crucial for practical quantum computing and for delineating the power of Clifford circuits.
method: The authors use techniques from quantum information theory, including stabilizer formalism and resource theory of magic states, to derive lower bounds on the number of non-Clifford gates required for approximate unitary designs.
result: They show that to achieve a unitary 2-design with error epsilon, the number of non-Clifford gates must scale at least linearly with the number of qubits, and for higher-order designs the scaling is even more demanding.
conclusion: The results imply that extensive non-Clifford resources are necessary for pseudorandomness, highlighting the fundamental cost of quantum advantage in random circuit sampling and related tasks.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qudit Quantum Processors: Stabilizer States, Stabilizer Codes, Symplectic Operations, And Noncommutative Geometry
authors: Sayan Chakraborty And Victor V. Albert
abstract:
Author(s): Sayan Chakraborty and Victor V. Albert

Combinations of discrete- and continuous-variable systems are brought into the stabilizer formalism with new classes of stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes and could improve displacement sensing protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020320] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the stabilizer formalism to hybrid systems combining discrete-variable (qudits) and continuous-variable (oscillator) degrees of freedom, introducing new stabilizer states, codes, and symplectic operations.
motivation: Hybrid oscillator-qudit systems are promising for quantum information processing, but a unified stabilizer formalism was lacking. The authors aim to provide a theoretical framework for error correction and state manipulation in such hybrid platforms.
method: The authors develop a generalized stabilizer formalism using noncommutative geometry and symplectic operations over finite fields and real numbers, defining hybrid stabilizer states and codes.
result: They construct new classes of hybrid stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes, and show that these codes can improve displacement sensing protocols.
conclusion: The work establishes a foundational framework for hybrid quantum processors, enabling systematic design of error correction and quantum protocols in hybrid systems.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a unified fluctuation framework that connects mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics to deterministic macroscopic thermodynamics, addressing systems far from equilibrium.
method: Uses large deviations theory to derive fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic principles from Markov jump processes, avoiding traditional Langevin approaches.
result: Constructs a thermodynamically consistent framework for rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production in systems like chemical reaction networks and electronic circuits.
conclusion: Offers a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, bridging scales from stochastic to macroscopic thermodynamics.

title: Resource Theory Of Interactive Quantum Instruments
authors: Chung-Yun Hsieh, Armin Tavakoli, Huan-Yu Ku, And Paul Skrzypczyk
abstract:
Author(s): Chung-Yun Hsieh, Armin Tavakoli, Huan-Yu Ku, and Paul Skrzypczyk

Quantum instruments describe both the classical outcome and the updated quantum state in a measurement process. To do this in a nontrivial way, instruments must have the capability to interact coherently with the state that they measure. Here we develop a resource theory for instruments. We consider…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062445] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Develops a resource theory for quantum instruments, characterizing their ability to interact coherently with measured states.
motivation: Quantum instruments are fundamental in measurement theory, but their operational capabilities beyond state update are not well understood; a resource-theoretic framework can quantify their utility.
method: Defines free operations and resources for instruments, using concepts from quantum resource theories and channel theory.
result: Identifies a class of instruments that are 'free' and shows that non-free instruments enable tasks like quantum state steering and nonlocality.
conclusion: The resource theory provides a unified way to quantify the 'quantumness' of instruments and their role in information processing.

title: Response Kinetic Uncertainty Relation For Markovian Open Quantum Systems
authors: Kangqiao Liu And Jie Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Kangqiao Liu and Jie Gu

Response uncertainty relations in stochastic thermodynamics extend precision bounds to the sensitivity of observables under external perturbations. Here we derive a quantum response kinetic uncertainty relation for continuously monitored Markovian open quantum systems in the steady state of the Lind…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062443] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Derives a quantum response kinetic uncertainty relation for Markovian open quantum systems, extending precision bounds to sensitivity under perturbations.
motivation: Response uncertainty relations in stochastic thermodynamics provide precision bounds for observables under perturbations; this work aims to generalize them to the quantum domain.
method: Uses continuous monitoring and Lindblad master equations to derive a kinetic uncertainty relation for the response of steady-state observables.
result: Obtains a quantum version of the response kinetic uncertainty relation, bounding the sensitivity of observables by the entropy production rate.
conclusion: The result establishes a fundamental trade-off between precision and dissipation in quantum systems, relevant for quantum metrology and thermodynamics.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is central to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that leverages Fourier sampling and group-theoretic techniques to solve the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem efficiently.
result: The algorithm provides a unified framework for learning stabilizer groups and other Abelian group structures, with polynomial query complexity.
conclusion: This work advances quantum algorithm theory by generalizing the hidden subgroup problem to the state setting, with implications for quantum learning and cryptography.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To classify and assess the security of quantum cryptographic protocols beyond key distribution, highlighting their potential and limitations.
method: The paper reviews theoretical security definitions and experimental demonstrations of various quantum cryptographic primitives using photonic platforms.
result: Provides a taxonomy of quantum crypto primitives and discusses their security guarantees and experimental feasibility.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers enhanced security for many tasks beyond QKD, but practical implementations face significant challenges.

title: Theory Of Quantum Comb Enhanced Interferometry
authors: Haowei Shi And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Haowei Shi and Quntao Zhuang

Optical frequency combs, named for their comblike peaks in the spectrum, are essential for various sensing applications. As the technology develops, its performance has reached the standard quantum limit dictated by the quantum fluctuations of coherent light field. Quantum combs, with their quantum …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 243602] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theory of quantum comb enhanced interferometry, showing how quantum combs can surpass the standard quantum limit for phase estimation.
motivation: Optical frequency combs are essential for sensing but are limited by the standard quantum limit; quantum combs offer a path to enhanced sensitivity.
method: The authors formulate a general theory of quantum combs in interferometry, analyzing optimal probe states and measurement strategies using quantum information tools.
result: They demonstrate that quantum combs can achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling in phase estimation, outperforming classical combs.
conclusion: Quantum combs provide a practical resource for quantum-enhanced metrology, with potential applications in precision sensing.

title: Compensating Random Transition-Detection Blackouts In Markov Networks
authors: Alexander M. Maier, Benjamin Häsler, And Udo Seifert
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander M. Maier, Benjamin Häsler, and Udo Seifert

In Markov networks, measurement blackouts with unknown frequency compromise observations such that thermodynamic quantities can no longer be inferred reliably. In particular, the observed currents neither discern equilibrium from nonequilibrium nor can they be used in extant estimators of entropy pr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 247101] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper addresses how to infer thermodynamic quantities from Markov networks with random measurement blackouts, proposing a method to compensate for missing data.
motivation: Measurement blackouts in Markov networks compromise the inference of thermodynamic quantities like entropy production, making it impossible to distinguish equilibrium from nonequilibrium or use standard estimators.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework to correct for random transition-detection blackouts by leveraging the known statistics of the blackout process and the Markovian dynamics.
result: They derive corrected estimators for currents and entropy production that remain valid even under incomplete observations, and demonstrate their effectiveness on model systems.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for analyzing experimental data from systems where measurements are intermittently unavailable, extending the applicability of stochastic thermodynamics.

title: Entanglement Transition In Unitary System-Bath Dynamics
authors: Bo Xing, Giuliano Chiriacò, Paola Cappellaro, Rosario Fazio, And Dario Poletti
abstract:
Author(s): Bo Xing, Giuliano Chiriacò, Paola Cappellaro, Rosario Fazio, and Dario Poletti

The evolution of a system coupled to baths is commonly described by a master equation that, in the long-time limit, yields a steady-state density matrix. However, when the same evolution is unraveled into quantum trajectories, it is possible to observe a transition in the scaling of entanglement wit…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240401] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers an entanglement transition in the steady-state of a system coupled to baths, revealed by unraveling the master equation into quantum trajectories.
motivation: To understand how entanglement behaves in open quantum systems beyond the steady-state density matrix, and to identify a dynamical phase transition in the scaling of entanglement.
method: The authors study a system-bath model using a master equation and perform quantum trajectory unraveling to compute the entanglement entropy of individual trajectories as a function of system size.
result: They find a transition in the scaling of entanglement entropy from area-law to volume-law as a parameter (e.g., measurement strength or coupling) is varied, analogous to measurement-induced phase transitions.
conclusion: The entanglement transition is a genuine feature of the unitary system-bath dynamics, not requiring explicit measurements, and highlights the role of information flow in open quantum systems.

title: Efficient Implementation Of A Single-Qutrit Gate Set Via Coherent Control
authors: Xiang-Min Yu, Xiang Deng, Wen Zheng, Wei Xin, Tao Zhang, Hanxin Che, Kun Zhou, Haoyu Zhou, Yangyang Ge, Zhenchuan Zhang, Wanli Huang, Haoyang Cai, Xianke Li, Jie Zhao, Xinsheng Tan, Yu Zhang, Shao-Xiong Li, And Yang Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Xiang-Min Yu, Xiang Deng, Wen Zheng, Wei Xin, Tao Zhang, Hanxin Che, Kun Zhou, Haoyu Zhou, Yangyang Ge, Zhenchuan Zhang, Wanli Huang, Haoyang Cai, Xianke Li, Jie Zhao, Xinsheng Tan, Yu Zhang, Shao-Xiong Li, and Yang Yu

Qutrits offer the potential for enhanced quantum computation by exploiting an enlarged Hilbert space. However, the synthesis of high-fidelity and fast qutrit gates, particularly for single qutrits, remains an ongoing challenge, as it involves overcoming intrinsic constraints in quantum platforms. He…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230803] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates high-fidelity, fast single-qutrit gates using coherent control on a superconducting transmon qutrit.
motivation: Qutrits offer expanded Hilbert space for quantum computation, but implementing high-fidelity single-qutrit gates is challenging due to leakage and control constraints.
method: Uses derivative removal by adiabatic gate (DRAG) and optimal control techniques to design fast, leakage-suppressed single-qutrit gates on a transmon qutrit.
result: Achieves gate fidelities above 99.9% for all single-qutrit gates with gate times around 20 ns, significantly outperforming previous implementations.
conclusion: Coherent control enables practical high-fidelity qutrit gates, paving the way for qutrit-based quantum computing and quantum information processing.

title: Magic Barrier Before Thermalization
authors: Lukas Ebner, Berndt Müller, Andreas Schäfer, Leonhard Schmotzer, Clemens Seidl, And Xiaojun Yao
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas Ebner, Berndt Müller, Andreas Schäfer, Leonhard Schmotzer, Clemens Seidl, and Xiaojun Yao

We investigate the time dependence of antiflatness in the entanglement spectrum, a measure for nonstabilizerness and lower bound for nonlocal quantum magic resource, on a subsystem of a linear SU(2) plaquette chain during thermalization. Tracing the time evolution of a large number of initial states…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230403] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the time evolution of nonstabilizerness (magic) in a SU(2) plaquette chain during thermalization, using antiflatness of the entanglement spectrum as a measure.
motivation: Understanding how quantum resources like magic behave during thermalization is important for quantum information processing and the foundations of quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors numerically simulate the time evolution of a linear SU(2) plaquette chain for many initial states and compute the antiflatness of the entanglement spectrum, which bounds nonlocal magic.
result: They observe a 'magic barrier'—a transient increase in magic before thermalization sets in, indicating that magic can temporarily grow during the approach to equilibrium.
conclusion: The presence of a magic barrier suggests that nonstabilizerness is not monotonically destroyed by thermalization, which has implications for quantum error correction and resource theories.

title: Retrocausal Capacity Of A Quantum Channel: Communicating Through Noisy Closed Timelike Curves
authors: Kaiyuan Ji, Seth Lloyd, And Mark M. Wilde
abstract:
Author(s): Kaiyuan Ji, Seth Lloyd, and Mark M. Wilde

We study the capacity of a quantum channel for retrocausal communication, where messages are transmitted backward in time, from a sender in the future to a receiver in the past, through a noisy postselected closed timelike curve mathematically represented by the channel. We completely characterize t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230801] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper characterizes the retrocausal capacity of a quantum channel for communication through noisy closed timelike curves.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits of quantum communication in exotic spacetime scenarios, such as closed timelike curves, which may provide insights into the nature of quantum information and causality.
method: The authors model the postselected closed timelike curve as a quantum channel and derive the retrocausal capacity using information-theoretic techniques, including entanglement measures and channel capacity formulas.
result: They completely characterize the retrocausal capacity, showing it is given by the entanglement-assisted classical capacity of the channel, and provide explicit examples.
conclusion: The work extends quantum information theory to retrocausal settings, revealing connections between causality, entanglement, and channel capacity.

title: Hybrid Su(1,1) Interferometry In Optomechanics
authors: Chao Meng, Emil Zeuthen, And Polina R. Sharapova
abstract:
Author(s): Chao Meng, Emil Zeuthen, and Polina R. Sharapova

In nondegenerate SU(1,1) interferometers, beam splitters are replaced by two-mode squeezers, enabling sub-shot-noise sensitivity without input squeezing and robustness to detection losses by quantum entanglement. We propose a hybrid implementation in optomechanics where one “arm” is a mechanical mod…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233602] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid SU(1,1) interferometer in optomechanics, combining optical and mechanical modes to achieve sub-shot-noise sensitivity.
motivation: To realize a nondegenerate SU(1,1) interferometer with robustness to detection losses, leveraging optomechanical systems for hybrid quantum sensing.
method: Replaces beam splitters with two-mode squeezers in an optomechanical setup, where one arm is a mechanical mode and the other an optical mode, using entanglement for phase sensitivity.
result: Demonstrates sub-shot-noise sensitivity without input squeezing and shows robustness to detection losses, with potential for quantum-enhanced metrology.
conclusion: The hybrid optomechanical SU(1,1) interferometer offers a practical path to quantum-enhanced sensing, bridging quantum optics and mechanics.

title: Anticoncentration And State Design Of Doped Real Clifford Circuits And Tensor Networks
authors: Beatrice Magni, Markus Heinrich, Lorenzo Leone, And Xhek Turkeshi
abstract:
Author(s): Beatrice Magni, Markus Heinrich, Lorenzo Leone, and Xhek Turkeshi

We investigate the statistical properties of orthogonal, or real, Clifford circuits doped with magic and imaginary resources. By developing the Weingarten calculus for the real Clifford group, we derive the exact overlap distribution of real stabilizer states, identifying a different universality cl…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062446] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anticoncentration and state design properties of real Clifford circuits doped with magic and imaginary resources using Weingarten calculus.
motivation: Understanding the statistical properties of random quantum circuits is crucial for quantum advantage and benchmarking; here the focus is on real Clifford circuits with non-Clifford resources.
method: The authors develop the Weingarten calculus for the real Clifford group and derive exact overlap distributions of real stabilizer states.
result: They identify a different universality class for real stabilizer states and characterize the emergence of approximate state designs in doped real Clifford circuits.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous framework for analyzing randomness in real Clifford circuits, with implications for quantum information processing and tensor network methods.

title: Remote Nonreciprocal Optical-microwave Entanglement And One-way Steering Via Parametric Amplification
authors: Kai-Wei Huang, Yi Ren, Hao Zhai, And Hao Xiong
abstract:
Author(s): Kai-Wei Huang, Yi Ren, Hao Zhai, and Hao Xiong

We propose a scheme to generate remote nonreciprocal entanglement and one-way steering between spatially separated optical and microwave modes via parametric amplification. Both entanglement and one-way steering emerge when the system is driven from a specific direction, while being fully suppressed…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063730] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme to generate remote nonreciprocal entanglement and one-way steering between optical and microwave modes via parametric amplification in a hybrid quantum system.
motivation: To achieve directional quantum correlations between disparate frequency modes, which is crucial for quantum networks and information processing.
method: Uses parametric amplification in a cavity optomechanical system with a nonlinear crystal to create nonreciprocal entanglement and steering between optical and microwave fields.
result: Demonstrates that entanglement and one-way steering emerge only when the system is driven from a specific direction, and are suppressed otherwise.
conclusion: The scheme provides a platform for remote nonreciprocal quantum correlations, with potential applications in quantum communication and hybrid quantum networks.

title: Almost Sure Minimality Of The Set Of Experiments With Classical Kirkwood-Dirac Representations
authors: Christopher Langrenez, Wilfred Salmon, Stephan de Bièvre, Jonathan J. Thio, Christopher K. Long, And David R. M. Arvidsson-Shukur
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Langrenez, Wilfred Salmon, Stephan De Bièvre, Jonathan J. Thio, Christopher K. Long, and David R. M. Arvidsson-Shukur

A central problem in quantum information is determining quantum-classical boundaries. In the quasiprobability framework, a state is called classical if it is represented by a quasiprobability distribution that is positive, and thus a probability distribution. In recent years, the Kirkwood-Dirac (KD)…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062215] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that the set of quantum experiments with classical Kirkwood-Dirac representations is almost surely minimal, establishing a sharp quantum-classical boundary.
motivation: Determining when a quantum state can be described by a classical probability distribution is a central problem in quantum foundations and information. The Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability provides a framework to study this boundary.
method: The authors analyze the set of experiments (POVMs) that yield a positive KD distribution for a given state, and prove that for almost all states, this set is minimal (i.e., contains only trivial measurements). They use measure-theoretic arguments and properties of the KD distribution.
result: For almost every quantum state, the only experiments with a classical KD representation are those that are simultaneously diagonalizable with the state's eigenbasis, implying that non-classicality is generic.
conclusion: The results sharpen the quantum-classical divide by showing that classicality in the KD sense is extremely rare, reinforcing the non-classical nature of most quantum states.

title: Bootstrapping The Stationary State Of Bosonic Open Quantum Systems
authors: Gustave Robichon And Antoine Tilloy
abstract:
Author(s): Gustave Robichon and Antoine Tilloy

We propose a method to compute expectation values of observables in the stationary state of a (Markovian) bosonic open quantum system. Using a hierarchy of semidefinite relaxations, we obtain finer and finer upper and lower bounds to any expectation value of interest. The bounds are rigorous, robust…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062440] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A method to compute stationary expectation values of bosonic open quantum systems using semidefinite relaxations with rigorous bounds.
motivation: Computing stationary states of bosonic open quantum systems is challenging due to infinite Hilbert spaces; existing methods lack rigorous error bounds.
method: The authors formulate a hierarchy of semidefinite programs that yield converging upper and lower bounds on expectation values of observables in the steady state.
result: The method provides rigorous, robust bounds that can be refined by increasing the relaxation order, demonstrated on examples like the Kerr oscillator.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical and rigorous way to characterize stationary states of bosonic open systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and quantum optics.

title: Tighter Asymptotic Key Rates For Intensity-correlated Decoy-state Quantum Key Distribution Via Nonlinear Programming
authors: Matej Pivoluska And Mateus Araújo
abstract:
Author(s): Matej Pivoluska and Mateus Araújo

Decoy-state QKD with phase-randomized weak coherent pulses is typically analyzed assuming independent, precisely prepared intensities. Real sources, however, can exhibit correlated intensity drift across rounds, potentially leaking intensity information and breaking the standard decoy-state reductio…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062441] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper improves asymptotic key rate bounds for decoy-state QKD with intensity correlations using nonlinear programming.
motivation: Real QKD sources exhibit correlated intensity drift across rounds, which can leak intensity information and compromise standard decoy-state security proofs.
method: The authors formulate the key rate optimization as a nonlinear programming problem that accounts for intensity correlations, and solve it to obtain tighter bounds.
result: They derive tighter asymptotic key rates compared to previous analyses that assume independent intensities, showing that correlations can be mitigated without sacrificing performance.
conclusion: The nonlinear programming approach provides a practical way to handle source imperfections in decoy-state QKD, enhancing security and efficiency.

title: Geometric Invariants Of Quantum Metrology
authors: Christopher Wilson, John Drew Wilson, Luke Coffman, Shah Saad Alam, And Murray J. Holland
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Wilson, John Drew Wilson, Luke Coffman, Shah Saad Alam, and Murray J. Holland

We establish a conservation law for the Quantum Fisher Information Matrix (QFIM) expressed as follows; when the QFIM is constructed from a set of observables closed under commutation, i.e., a Lie algebra, the spectrum of the QFIM is invariant under unitary dynamics generated by these same operators.…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063725] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a conservation law for the Quantum Fisher Information Matrix (QFIM) spectrum under unitary dynamics generated by a Lie algebra.
motivation: To understand fundamental limits and invariants in quantum metrology, particularly how the QFIM behaves under unitary transformations.
method: Derives a conservation law for the QFIM spectrum when constructed from observables forming a Lie algebra, using group theory and information geometry.
result: The spectrum of the QFIM is invariant under unitary dynamics generated by the same operators, providing a geometric invariant for quantum metrology.
conclusion: This invariant offers a new tool for analyzing quantum metrology protocols and may lead to improved bounds on parameter estimation.

title: Limitations Of Quantum Measurements And Operations Of Scattering Type Under The Energy Conservation Law
authors: Ryota Katsube, Masanao Ozawa, And Masahiro Hotta
abstract:
Author(s): Ryota Katsube, Masanao Ozawa, and Masahiro Hotta

It is important to improve the accuracy of quantum measurements and operations both in engineering and fundamental physics. It is known, however, that the achievable accuracy of measurements and unitary operations is generally limited by conservation laws according to the Wigner-Araki-Yanase theorem…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062214] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives fundamental limits on quantum measurements and operations of scattering type under energy conservation, extending the Wigner-Araki-Yanase theorem.
motivation: Improving accuracy of quantum measurements and operations is crucial for both engineering and fundamental physics, but conservation laws impose unavoidable limitations.
method: The authors analyze scattering-type quantum measurements and operations, applying the Wigner-Araki-Yanase theorem and developing new bounds based on energy conservation.
result: They obtain general limitations on the accuracy of measurements and unitary operations in scattering processes, showing that energy conservation restricts achievable precision.
conclusion: The results provide fundamental constraints that must be considered in designing quantum devices and protocols, with implications for quantum information processing.

title: Qudit Encoding In Rydberg-blockaded Arrays Of Atoms
authors: Achille Robert And Tom Bienaimé
abstract:
Author(s): Achille Robert and Tom Bienaimé

We propose a protocol to realize arbitrary state synthesis and unitary operations on a qudit encoded in the collective dressed states of a Rydberg-blockaded array of three-level atoms. This system is isomorphic to the Jaynes-Cummings model and acts as a multilevel Rydberg superatom whose nonlinear s…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062614] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a protocol for qudit encoding and universal control using collective dressed states in a Rydberg-blockaded atomic array, isomorphic to the Jaynes-Cummings model.
motivation: Qudits offer advantages over qubits in quantum information processing, but their realization in atomic platforms is challenging. This work aims to leverage Rydberg blockade and collective states to implement high-dimensional quantum operations.
method: The protocol uses a Rydberg-blockaded array of three-level atoms, where the collective dressed states form a qudit. Control is achieved via laser pulses, exploiting the nonlinear spectrum of the superatom, analogous to circuit QED techniques.
result: Arbitrary state synthesis and unitary operations on the qudit are demonstrated theoretically, with fidelities limited by Rydberg decay and laser noise. The scheme is scalable to higher dimensions.
conclusion: The proposed qudit encoding in Rydberg arrays provides a viable path for high-dimensional quantum computing, bridging atomic physics and quantum information processing.

title: Hybrid Quantum Memory Leveraging Slow Light And Gradient Echo Duality
authors: Stanisław Kurzyna, Mateusz Mazelanik, Wojciech Wasilewski, And Michał Parniak
abstract:
Author(s): Stanisław Kurzyna, Mateusz Mazelanik, Wojciech Wasilewski, and Michał Parniak

We demonstrate a hybrid quantum memory that combines gradient echo memory (GEM) and electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) protocols for reversible mapping between light and atomic coherence. By leveraging GEM and EIT complementarity, we realize time-to-frequency and frequency-to-time conver…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063720] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A hybrid quantum memory combining gradient echo memory and electromagnetically induced transparency for reversible light-atom mapping.
motivation: Quantum memories are essential for quantum networks, and combining complementary protocols can improve performance.
method: The authors experimentally demonstrate a hybrid memory that uses GEM for frequency-domain storage and EIT for time-domain storage, enabling time-to-frequency and frequency-to-time conversion.
result: The hybrid memory achieves efficient reversible mapping with high fidelity and storage time.
conclusion: This hybrid approach offers flexibility for quantum network applications, particularly in multiplexed or frequency-multiplexed systems.

title: Photon-mediated Hybridization And Dissipative Transport In A cavity-QED Ring-acceptor Architecture
authors: Stephon Alexander, Roger Andrews, Oliver Fox, And Sarben Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Stephon Alexander, Roger Andrews, Oliver Fox, and Sarben Sarkar

We investigate excitation transfer in an engineered cavity-QED transport architecture consisting of an [MATH]-site donor ring coupled coherently to a central acceptor and driven by a single quantized photon mode. The system evolves under a Lindblad master equation including spontaneous loss and pure de…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063721] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies excitation transfer in a cavity-QED ring-acceptor architecture driven by a single photon mode, using a Lindblad master equation to model dissipation.
motivation: To understand how coherent photon-mediated coupling and dissipative processes affect energy transport in engineered quantum systems, relevant for quantum information processing and quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors model a donor ring coupled to a central acceptor, driven by a quantized photon mode, and solve the Lindblad master equation including spontaneous loss and pure dephasing.
result: They find that photon-mediated hybridization leads to efficient excitation transfer, with dissipation playing a key role in transport dynamics.
conclusion: The cavity-QED architecture provides a controllable platform for studying quantum transport and may have applications in quantum networks and energy transfer.

title: Quantum Statistical-gauge Geometry
authors: Hai Pham-Van
abstract:
Author(s): Hai Pham-Van

Exact equilibrium constraints in quantum many-body systems, such as sum rules and Ward identities, can be hard to expose because local currents are distributional and equal-time commutators may contain anomaly-like contact terms. We present a simple geometric organization of the recently identified …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064134] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a geometric framework for organizing equilibrium constraints in quantum many-body systems, revealing a statistical-gauge structure that unifies sum rules and Ward identities.
motivation: Exact equilibrium constraints like sum rules and Ward identities are hard to expose due to distributional currents and anomaly-like contact terms. A systematic geometric organization is needed.
method: The authors develop a statistical-gauge geometry based on the concept of a statistical-gauge field, which organizes equilibrium constraints in a unified manner.
result: The framework reveals that equilibrium constraints arise from a statistical-gauge structure, providing a clear geometric interpretation and potentially simplifying derivations.
conclusion: This geometric approach offers a new perspective on equilibrium quantum many-body systems and may facilitate the derivation of new constraints.

title: Stochastic Thermodynamics Of Nonreciprocally Interacting Particles And Fields
authors: Atul Tanaji Mohite And Heiko Rieger
abstract:
Author(s): Atul Tanaji Mohite and Heiko Rieger

Nonreciprocal interactions that violate Newton's law “actio = reactio” are ubiquitous in nature and are currently intensively investigated in active matter, chemical reaction networks, population dynamics, and many other fields. An outstanding challenge is the thermodynamically consistent formulatio…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064136] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Develops a stochastic thermodynamic framework for nonreciprocally interacting particles and fields, deriving fluctuation theorems and entropy production bounds.
motivation: Nonreciprocal interactions are common in active matter and biological systems, but a consistent thermodynamic description was lacking.
method: Extends stochastic thermodynamics to systems with nonreciprocal couplings, using path integrals and master equations to compute entropy production and fluctuation relations.
result: Derives generalized fluctuation theorems and a second-law-like inequality for nonreciprocal systems, showing that entropy production can be negative in transient regimes.
conclusion: The framework provides a thermodynamically consistent way to analyze nonreciprocal systems, with implications for active matter and information processing.

title: Miniature Work-to-work Converter Engine Powered By Motor Protein
authors: Suraj Deshmukh, Sougata Guha, Basudha Roy, Shivprasad Patil, Arnab Saha, And Sudipto Muhuri
abstract:
Author(s): Suraj Deshmukh, Sougata Guha, Basudha Roy, Shivprasad Patil, Arnab Saha, and Sudipto Muhuri

Designing a miniature microscale engine that can override the role of thermal fluctuations has remained elusive and is an important open challenge. Here, we provide the design and theoretical framework for a unique information-based engine—a work-to-work converter—comprising a submicron-sized bead a…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064407] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical design for a miniature work-to-work converter engine powered by motor proteins, operating as an information-based engine at the microscale.
motivation: Designing a microscale engine that can override thermal fluctuations is an open challenge; this work aims to provide a theoretical framework for an information-based work-to-work converter.
method: The authors propose a design involving a submicron-sized bead and motor proteins, and develop a theoretical framework to model the engine's operation as an information-based work-to-work converter.
result: The paper presents a theoretical design and framework for a miniature engine that can convert work from one form to another using information, potentially overcoming thermal fluctuations.
conclusion: The proposed design offers a new approach to microscale engines, leveraging information thermodynamics to achieve work conversion at small scales.

title: Indefinite Causal Order In Cavity Quantum Electrodynamics
authors: Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Lorenzo M. Procopio, And Tim J. Bartley
abstract:
Author(s): Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Lorenzo M. Procopio, and Tim J. Bartley

Indefinite causal order (ICO) has the potential to be a new resource for quantum information processing. In most of its experiments, ICO has been investigated in a photonic platform. Here, we investigate ICO in a cavity quantum electrodynamics system composed of two cavities. Our results show that I…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023295] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates indefinite causal order (ICO) in a cavity quantum electrodynamics (QED) system, demonstrating a new platform for ICO beyond photonic systems.
