conclusion: The transversal architecture provides a practical path toward large-scale fault-tolerant quantum simulation on neutral-atom platforms, demonstrating the viability of neutral atoms for beyond-classical quantum computation.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper provides estimates of loss function concentration in noisy parametrized quantum circuits, linking noise resilience to circuit expressivity.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus and noise, hindering trainability; understanding how noise affects loss landscapes is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors derive analytical bounds on the variance of the loss function gradient under noise, using tools from random matrix theory and quantum information theory.
result: They show that noise can mitigate barren plateaus by reducing the effective expressivity of the circuit, leading to more concentrated loss functions that are easier to optimize.
conclusion: The results provide a principled link between noise and trainability, offering a roadmap for designing noise-resilient variational algorithms.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics beyond simple string breaking.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in confining gauge theories is important for non-equilibrium quantum dynamics and may have implications for quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and experimental demonstrations with trapped ions to probe string-breaking dynamics in different regimes.
result: They find experimentally accessible regimes where string breaking exhibits rich quantum dynamics, including diabatic effects.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into non-equilibrium quantum dynamics of confining strings, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and simulation.

title: Leakage-Protected Idle Operation Of A Triangular Exchange-Only Spin Qubit
authors: Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, And Jason R. Petta
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, and Jason R. Petta

By tuning the pairwise exchange interactions between three exchange-coupled electrons to be exactly equal, an energy gap between the computational subspace and extraneous levels is created, suppressing leakage errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020324] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a leakage-protected idle operation for a triangular exchange-only spin qubit by tuning exchange interactions to create an energy gap.
motivation: Leakage errors in spin qubits degrade gate fidelity; protecting idle operation is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors tune pairwise exchange interactions between three electrons to be exactly equal, opening an energy gap between the computational subspace and leakage states.
result: They achieve suppression of leakage errors during idle operation, improving qubit coherence.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical method to enhance qubit performance in exchange-only spin qubit platforms.

title: Quantum Error-Corrected Computation Of Molecular Energies
authors: Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, And David Muñoz Ramo
abstract:
Author(s): Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, and David Muñoz Ramo

Noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets enable a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020319] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer using noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error correction.
motivation: To show that quantum error correction can be integrated with practical quantum chemistry computations, improving reliability despite hardware noise.
method: Employs trapped-ion qubits with noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets to perform a molecular energy calculation.
result: Achieves a partially fault-tolerant computation of molecular energies, demonstrating improved accuracy over non-error-corrected approaches.
conclusion: Quantum error correction can be practically applied to quantum chemistry on current hardware, paving the way for reliable quantum simulations.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of methods for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, unified under a common framework.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for accurate modeling of open quantum systems in quantum technologies, but the diversity of methods makes it hard to relate them.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and survey various numerical and analytical techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor networks.
result: The review highlights commonalities and differences among methods, providing guidance for selecting appropriate simulation techniques for different physical regimes.
conclusion: The unified framework clarifies the connections between seemingly disparate approaches and offers a roadmap for future developments in non-Markovian open quantum system simulations.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in gate count and experimental feasibility.
motivation: Qudits offer potential resource savings in quantum circuits, such as simplifying the Toffoli gate, but their role in quantum computing is not yet fully exploited.
method: The paper surveys qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decomposition techniques using qudits, and reviews experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Qudits can reduce the number of operations and qubits needed for certain multiqubit gates, and experimental demonstrations show feasibility in trapped ions, superconducting circuits, and photonics.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for near-term quantum computing, especially for reducing circuit depth and enabling algorithms on limited hardware.

title: Spin–Boson Mapping Of The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
authors: Sami Boulebnane, Abid Khan, Minzhao Liu, Jeffrey Larson, Dylan Herman, Ruslan Shaydulin, And Marco Pistoia
abstract:
Author(s): Sami Boulebnane, Abid Khan, Minzhao Liu, Jeffrey Larson, Dylan Herman, Ruslan Shaydulin, and Marco Pistoia

The quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) achieves monotonically improving performance with circuit depth [MATH], yet the study of the high-depth regime has been obstructed by the exponential in [MATH] cost of existing exact evaluation techniques. In this Letter, we prove that, in the infinite…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240601] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper maps the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) to a spin-boson model to analyze its performance at high circuit depths.
motivation: Studying QAOA at high depths is hindered by exponential cost of exact evaluation; a mapping to a spin-boson model provides a tractable analytical framework.
method: The authors prove that in the infinite-size limit, QAOA dynamics can be mapped to a spin-boson model, enabling analytical computation of expectation values.
result: They derive closed-form expressions for QAOA performance at high depths, showing monotonically improving performance and identifying a phase transition.
conclusion: The spin-boson mapping offers a new tool for understanding QAOA, but the paper's focus is on algorithm analysis rather than quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Incoherent Repumping Scheme In The $^{88}\mathrm{Sr}^{+}$ Five-level Manifold
authors: Valentin Martimort, Sacha Guesne, Derwell Drapier, Vincent Tugayé, Lilay Gros-Desormeaux, Valentin Cambier, Albane Douillet, Luca Guidoni, And Jean-Pierre Likforman
abstract:
Author(s): Valentin Martimort, Sacha Guesne, Derwell Drapier, Vincent Tugayé, Lilay Gros-Desormeaux, Valentin Cambier, Albane Douillet, Luca Guidoni, and Jean-Pierre Likforman

Laser-cooled trapped ions are at the heart of modern quantum technologies and their cooling dynamics often deviate from the simplified two-level atom model. Doppler cooling of the [MATH] ion involves several electronic levels and repumping channels that strongly influence fluorescenc…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063109] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an incoherent repumping scheme for Doppler cooling of Sr+ ions, analyzing its effect on fluorescence and cooling dynamics.
motivation: Doppler cooling of trapped ions often involves multiple electronic levels, and repumping schemes are critical for efficient cooling. The authors aim to understand and optimize the cooling dynamics in a five-level manifold of Sr+.
method: The authors model the five-level system of Sr+ and propose an incoherent repumping scheme. They analyze the fluorescence and cooling dynamics using rate equations or master equations.
result: The incoherent repumping scheme modifies the fluorescence spectrum and cooling efficiency compared to standard coherent repumping, with potential benefits for certain experimental conditions.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers an alternative repumping method that may improve cooling performance or simplify experimental setups for trapped ion quantum technologies.

title: Microwave-free Vector Magnetic-field Measurement Using A Single Nitrogen-vacancy-center Spin In Diamond
authors: Yuhai Wang, Liye Zhao, And Lumin Ji
abstract:
Author(s): Yuhai Wang, Liye Zhao, and Lumin Ji

Magnetic field sensors based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers have attracted considerable attention due to their high sensitivity and spatial resolution. However, conventional vector magnetometry typically relies on either the four axes of ensemble NV centers or three orthogonal reference magnetic f…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062618] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a microwave-free method for vector magnetic field measurement using a single NV center in diamond.
motivation: Conventional vector magnetometry with NV centers requires either multiple NV axes or external reference fields, which can be complex or limiting. A simpler, single-NV method without microwaves is desirable.
method: The authors use a single NV center and exploit the spin-dependent photoluminescence under static magnetic fields, without applying microwave fields, to reconstruct the vector magnetic field.
result: They demonstrate vector magnetic field sensing with a single NV center, achieving sensitivity and spatial resolution comparable to conventional methods but with a simpler setup.
conclusion: The proposed microwave-free technique simplifies NV-based vector magnetometry, making it more accessible for practical applications.

title: Role Of Overparametrization In Quantum Approximate Optimization
authors: Daniil Rabinovich, Andrey Kardashin, And Soumik Adhikary
abstract:
Author(s): Daniil Rabinovich, Andrey Kardashin, and Soumik Adhikary

Variational quantum algorithms have emerged as a cornerstone of contemporary quantum algorithms research. While they have demonstrated considerable promise in solving problems of practical interest, efficiently determining the minimal quantum resources necessary to obtain such a solution remains an …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062617] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the role of overparametrization in the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), showing that overparametrization can improve optimization landscape and convergence.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms like QAOA often suffer from barren plateaus and poor trainability; understanding overparametrization may help design more efficient quantum circuits.
method: The authors analyze the QAOA cost landscape analytically and numerically, examining how increasing the number of parameters (layers) affects the presence of local minima and convergence to the global optimum.
result: They find that overparametrization leads to a smoother landscape with fewer spurious local minima, enabling better optimization, but at the cost of increased circuit depth.
conclusion: Overparametrization in QAOA can mitigate optimization difficulties, but the trade-off between circuit depth and trainability must be carefully managed for practical quantum advantage.

title: Unveiling Distinguishable non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Andrea Giani, Moe Z. Win, Peter L. Falb, And Andrea Conti
abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Giani, Moe Z. Win, Peter L. Falb, and Andrea Conti

Quantum systems promise unprecedented performance with respect to classical counterparts for various applications involving sensing, communications, control, and computing. Bringing this promise to reality hinges upon the distinguishability between quantum states. This paper explores the distinguish…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062435] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper explores distinguishability of non-Gaussian quantum states, proposing a framework to quantify how well such states can be discriminated.
motivation: Quantum state distinguishability is crucial for quantum sensing, communication, and computing, but non-Gaussian states are less studied than Gaussian ones.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on quantum state discrimination theory, possibly using fidelity or trace distance, and apply it to specific non-Gaussian states.
result: They identify conditions under which non-Gaussian states are distinguishable and quantify the advantage over Gaussian states.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the role of non-Gaussianity in quantum state discrimination, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Beyond Trotterization: Variational Product Formulas For Quantum Simulation
authors: Ibsal Assi, Michael Vogl, Meenu Kumari, And J. P. F. Leblanc
abstract:
Author(s): Ibsal Assi, Michael Vogl, Meenu Kumari, and J. P. F. LeBlanc

The authors introduce here a variational splitting scheme for the time-evolution operator that surpasses standard Trotter-Suzuki decompositions. Unlike typical variational methods, this framework works directly in operator space, providing globally valid results irrespective of the targeted initial state. The method generalizes naturally to a wide range of applications in condensed matter physics and beyond. In particular, it enables quantum circuits with lower gate counts and higher accuracy than Trotter-based formulas, making it useful for near-term quantum computing.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214314] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational product formula for time-evolution operators that reduces gate count and improves accuracy over Trotter-Suzuki decompositions.
motivation: Standard Trotter-Suzuki decompositions require many gates for accurate quantum simulation; a variational approach in operator space can yield more efficient circuits.
method: The authors propose a variational splitting scheme that optimizes the product formula directly in operator space, independent of the initial state, using a cost function based on the operator norm.
result: The variational product formulas achieve lower gate counts and higher accuracy compared to Trotter-based formulas for several test Hamiltonians.
conclusion: This method is useful for near-term quantum computing and can be applied broadly in condensed matter physics and other areas.

title: Absorbing State Dynamics Of Stochastic Gradient Descent
authors: Guanming Zhang And Stefano Martiniani
abstract:
Author(s): Guanming Zhang and Stefano Martiniani

Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) is a fundamental tool in stochastic optimization that is widely used in machine learning. Here, we study SGD through the lens of particle dynamics, introducing a framework that links its behavior to well-established models in nonequilibrium statistical physics. We i…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062103] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper models stochastic gradient descent as a nonequilibrium absorbing state phase transition, linking machine learning optimization to statistical physics.
motivation: To understand the dynamics of SGD beyond convergence rates by drawing analogies with absorbing state phase transitions in nonequilibrium statistical physics.
method: The authors map SGD to a particle dynamics model and analyze its behavior using concepts from absorbing state phase transitions, such as critical exponents and scaling.
result: They identify a continuous phase transition between absorbing and active states in SGD, characterized by universal scaling laws.
conclusion: The framework provides a new perspective on SGD dynamics and suggests that optimization algorithms can be understood through the lens of nonequilibrium statistical mechanics.

title: Efficient Quantum Information-inspired Ansatz For Variational Quantum Eigensolver Algorithm: Applications To Atomic Systems
authors: Abdul Kalam, Prasenjit Deb, Akitada Sakurai, B. K. Sahoo, V. S. Prasannaa, And B. P. Das
abstract:
Author(s): Abdul Kalam, Prasenjit Deb, Akitada Sakurai, B. K. Sahoo, V. S. Prasannaa, and B. P. Das

We present a quantum information-inspired ansatz for the variational quantum eigensolver and demonstrate its efficacy in calculating ground-state energies of atomic systems. Instead of adopting a heuristic approach, we start with an approximate multiqubit target state and utilize two quantum informa…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023272] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum information-inspired ansatz for VQE to compute ground-state energies of atomic systems.
motivation: Improving VQE ansatz design for quantum chemistry on near-term quantum devices.
method: Starts from an approximate multiqubit target state and uses quantum information measures to construct an efficient ansatz.
result: Demonstrates accurate ground-state energy calculations for atomic systems with reduced circuit depth.
conclusion: The ansatz is effective for atomic systems and may be extended to molecular systems.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces non-Gaussian control parameters to systematically optimize generation of non-Gaussian quantum states, increasing success rates by orders of magnitude.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum information processing but their generation is inefficient; the paper aims to provide a systematic optimization framework.
method: Defines new control parameters beyond stellar rank and uses them to design and optimize optical circuits for non-Gaussian state generation.
result: Achieves orders-of-magnitude improvement in success probability for generating target non-Gaussian states.
conclusion: The proposed control parameters enable scalable and efficient generation of non-Gaussian states, advancing optical quantum information processing.

title: Entropy Of Strongly Correlated Electrons In A Partially Filled Landau Level
authors: Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, And Andrea F. Young
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, and Andrea F. Young

Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal the successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, reaching sensitivities that constrain the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021016] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, with sensitivity to isolate topological entropy in non-Abelian phases.
motivation: Understanding entropy in strongly correlated electron systems is crucial for characterizing quantum phases, especially non-Abelian states relevant to topological quantum computing.
method: Experimental entropy measurements using a graphene-based device in a partially filled Landau level, combined with theoretical modeling.
result: Successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom observed, with sensitivity sufficient to constrain topological entropy extraction.
conclusion: The approach provides a pathway to isolate topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases, advancing the thermodynamics of quantum matter.

title: Magic Tricycles: Efficient Magic-State Generation With Finite Block-Length Quantum Ldpc Codes
authors: Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, And Mikhail D. Lukin
abstract:
Author(s): Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, and Mikhail D. Lukin

Quantum computing needs “magic states” for universality, but they are costly to make. New research introduces tricycle codes: high-rate QLDPC codes that can be used to generate CZ magic states in constant depth with high noise resilience.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021014] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: Introduces tricycle codes, high-rate QLDPC codes for efficient magic state generation in constant depth with high noise resilience.
motivation: Magic states are essential for universal quantum computing but costly to produce; the paper aims to reduce overhead using quantum LDPC codes.
method: Proposes tricycle codes, a family of QLDPC codes with high encoding rate, and demonstrates a protocol for generating CZ magic states in constant depth.
result: The codes achieve efficient magic state generation with improved noise tolerance compared to existing schemes.
conclusion: Tricycle codes offer a practical path toward fault-tolerant universal quantum computation by reducing the cost of magic state distillation.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Characterizes the computational complexity of matrix functions across different parameter regimes, identifying where quantum advantage may arise.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is fundamental for quantum algorithms, but the paper focuses on complexity classification rather than information-theoretic or cryptographic applications.
method: Uses computational complexity theory to analyze parameter regimes of matrix function problems, likely employing reductions and oracle models.
result: Provides a complexity classification that delineates regimes where quantum computers may outperform classical ones.
conclusion: The work offers insights into potential quantum advantage for matrix function problems, but is primarily a complexity-theoretic result.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an efficient classical surrogate for small subregions of quantum expectation landscapes, using initial quantum data.
motivation: Understanding and simulating quantum expectation landscapes is important for variational quantum algorithms, but full classical simulation is costly; the authors aim to reduce this cost by focusing on local patches.
method: The authors develop a method to classically surrogate a small subregion of an expectation landscape by leveraging initial data from quantum computers, likely using techniques from quantum machine learning or surrogate modeling.
result: They demonstrate that the surrogate can be constructed efficiently, potentially enabling faster exploration of quantum landscapes without full quantum simulation.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for hybrid quantum-classical optimization, though the contribution is more algorithmic than foundational in quantum information theory.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, which can be exploited to achieve high-precision sensing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including scaling analysis and estimation theory near critical points.
result: It demonstrates how criticality can be harnessed to surpass the standard quantum limit in parameter estimation.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing offers a promising route for next-generation quantum sensors, but practical challenges remain.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: A multiproduct commutation relation reduces T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation.
motivation: T gates are costly in fault-tolerant quantum computing, so reducing T-count is crucial for practical quantum algorithms.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial commutation relation for multiproducts of Pauli operators and apply it to sequential Pauli-based computation to cancel T gates.
result: The proposed relation enables significant reduction in T-count for certain quantum circuits.
conclusion: This work provides a new technique for T-count optimization, contributing to more efficient fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Efficient Simulation Of Logical Magic State Preparation Protocols
authors: Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, And Isaac H. Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, and Isaac H. Kim

Classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols is made scalable and efficient via propagating errors to the end of the circuit.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020329] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an efficient classical simulation method for logical magic state preparation protocols by propagating errors to the end of the circuit.
motivation: Magic state preparation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating these protocols is computationally expensive. The authors aim to make such simulations scalable and efficient.
method: They develop a technique that propagates errors through the circuit to the final measurement, allowing classical simulation of logical magic state preparation without full state evolution.
result: The method significantly reduces the computational cost, enabling simulation of larger protocols that were previously intractable.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for analyzing and optimizing magic state preparation, which is important for realizing fault-tolerant quantum computers.

title: Abelian Multi-Cycle Codes For Single-Shot Error Correction
authors: Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, And Leonid P. Pryadko
abstract:
Author(s): Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, and Leonid P. Pryadko

A new family of quantum low-density parity-check codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, achieves single-shot fault tolerance and an approximately 1.1% pseudothreshold with significantly shorter block lengths.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020326] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A new family of quantum LDPC codes achieving single-shot fault tolerance with shorter block lengths.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum error correction typically requires many rounds of syndrome measurement; single-shot error correction reduces this overhead.
method: The authors construct Abelian multi-cycle codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, and analyze their single-shot error correction properties.
result: The codes achieve a pseudothreshold of approximately 1.1% with significantly shorter block lengths than previous constructions.
conclusion: These codes offer a practical advantage for fault-tolerant quantum computing by reducing the number of syndrome measurement rounds needed.

title: Parallel Logical Measurements Via Quantum Code Surgery
authors: Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, And Theodore J. Yoder
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, and Theodore J. Yoder

Performance of many parallel measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes, a key capability for protecting quantum memories during computation, is achieved in a new scheme that preserves important code properties without requiring additional code blocks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020325] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: A scheme for parallel logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes using code surgery, preserving code properties without extra blocks.
motivation: Efficient parallel measurements are crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing methods often require additional code blocks or degrade code properties.
method: The authors propose a code surgery technique that enables simultaneous logical measurements on multiple logical qubits encoded in quantum LDPC codes, leveraging the code's structure to avoid extra overhead.
result: The scheme achieves parallel measurements while maintaining the code's distance and other properties, and is compatible with common LDPC code families.
conclusion: This work advances practical fault-tolerant quantum computing by enabling efficient parallel operations on LDPC codes, a key step toward scalable quantum architectures.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on dynamics and metastable phases.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium phenomena in strongly correlated systems, which may lead to novel material properties.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, including dynamical mean-field theory and pump-probe spectroscopy.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoping, metastable states, and transient orders like superconductivity and magnetism.
conclusion: Photoexcitation offers a powerful tool to engineer nonequilibrium phases in Mott insulators, with potential for future technologies.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining how violations arise from violated assumptions in measurement.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but many measurements exceed them; understanding why can lead to materials with enhanced properties.
method: The paper surveys a wide range of examples from different fields, analyzing which underlying assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linear response) are violated in each case.
result: It identifies common mechanisms for apparent bound violations, such as non-equilibrium conditions, anisotropy, or hierarchical structures, and shows how to design materials that exploit these.
conclusion: Apparent violations of thermodynamic bounds are not actual violations but arise from misapplied assumptions; this understanding can guide the development of materials with superior properties.

title: Quantum Non-Gaussianity Criterion Based On Photon Correlations ${g}^{(2)}$ And ${g}^{(3)}$
authors: Christoph Hotter, Clara Henke, Cornelis Jacobus van Diepen, Peter Lodahl, And Anders Søndberg Sørensen
abstract:
Author(s): Christoph Hotter, Clara Henke, Cornelis Jacobus van Diepen, Peter Lodahl, and Anders Søndberg Sørensen

Quantum non-Gaussian states, which cannot be written as mixtures of Gaussian states, are necessary to achieve a quantum advantage in continuous variable systems. They represent an important benchmark for the realization of an advanced quantum light source, as they cannot be made by simple means such…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 243601] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a criterion for quantum non-Gaussianity based on second- and third-order photon correlations.
motivation: Quantum non-Gaussian states are essential for continuous-variable quantum advantage, but existing criteria are limited; a simple correlation-based test is needed.
method: Derives necessary conditions for mixtures of Gaussian states using g^(2) and g^(3) correlations, and tests them on simulated and experimental data.
result: The criterion can certify quantum non-Gaussianity for states with low mean photon numbers, outperforming previous criteria in certain regimes.
conclusion: The g^(2)-g^(3) criterion provides a practical tool for characterizing quantum light sources, but the contribution is incremental and not directly aligned with core quantum information topics.

title: Nanomechanical Sensor Resolving Impulsive Forces Below Its Zero-Point Fluctuations
authors: Martynas Skrabulis, Martin Colombano Sosa, Nicola Carlon Zambon, Andrei Militaru, Massimiliano Rossi, Martin Frimmer, And Lukas Novotny
abstract:
Author(s): Martynas Skrabulis, Martin Colombano Sosa, Nicola Carlon Zambon, Andrei Militaru, Massimiliano Rossi, Martin Frimmer, and Lukas Novotny

Researchers boosted the sensitivity for measurements of the motion of a levitated nanoparticle, with potential uses in dark matter searches.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233604] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: A nanomechanical sensor achieves sensitivity below the zero-point fluctuations for impulsive force measurements, with potential applications in dark matter searches.
motivation: To detect weak impulsive forces, such as those from dark matter interactions, by pushing the sensitivity of nanomechanical sensors beyond the standard quantum limit.
method: The authors use a levitated nanoparticle in an optical trap and employ advanced measurement techniques to resolve forces below the zero-point fluctuations.
result: They demonstrate sensitivity to impulsive forces smaller than the zero-point motion of the nanoparticle, enabling detection of extremely weak signals.
conclusion: This work advances nanomechanical sensing capabilities, opening new possibilities for fundamental physics experiments like dark matter detection.

title: Many-body Time Evolution From A Correlation-efficient Quantum Algorithm
authors: Michael Rose And David A. Mazziotti
abstract:
Author(s): Michael Rose and David A. Mazziotti

We introduce the correlation-efficient time-evolution (CETE) algorithm for simulating quantum many-body dynamics. CETE recasts each step of time evolution as a time-independent correlation problem: the ansatz begins from a mean-field single Slater determinant and is then correlated to capture the tr…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060406] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a correlation-efficient time-evolution algorithm for simulating quantum many-body dynamics on quantum computers.
motivation: Simulating time evolution of many-body quantum systems is computationally expensive; existing algorithms require deep circuits or many ancilla qubits.
method: CETE reformulates each time step as a time-independent correlation problem, starting from a mean-field Slater determinant and adding correlations to capture the true dynamics.
result: The algorithm reduces circuit depth and qubit requirements compared to standard Trotterization or variational approaches, demonstrated on small molecular systems.
conclusion: CETE offers a resource-efficient approach for quantum simulation of many-body dynamics, potentially enabling larger simulations on near-term quantum devices.

title: Nonclassical Photocounting Statistics With A Single On-off Detector
authors: V. S. Kovtoniuk, M. Bohmann, And A. A. Semenov
abstract:
Author(s): V. S. Kovtoniuk, M. Bohmann, and A. A. Semenov

Any single on-off photocounter, which can only detect the presence or absence of photons without discriminating their number, is not capable of identifying the nonclassical nature of light. This limitation arises because any photocounting statistics obtained with such a detector can be easily reprod…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063726] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that a single on-off detector cannot certify nonclassical light, but two detectors can, using a witness based on photocounting statistics.
motivation: To determine whether nonclassical photocounting statistics can be identified with minimal resources, specifically a single on-off detector.
method: The authors analyze the photocounting statistics of a single on-off detector and show they can be reproduced by a classical model; they then propose a two-detector scheme and derive a nonclassicality witness.
result: A single on-off detector cannot distinguish nonclassical from classical light, but two detectors enable certification via a witness based on the difference of click probabilities.
conclusion: Nonclassical light detection requires at least two on-off detectors, providing a practical minimal resource for nonclassicality tests.

title: Entanglement Dynamics For Atoms Near A Reflecting Boundary: Enhancement And Suppression By Environment-induced Interactions
authors: Ying Chen, Hongwei Yu, And Jiawei Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Ying Chen, Hongwei Yu, and Jiawei Hu

We investigate how environment-induced interactions influence the entanglement dynamics of two atoms held at fixed positions near a perfectly reflecting boundary. Within the framework of open quantum systems, we explicitly incorporate the environment-induced energy shifts, including both atom-bounda…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062437] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Investigates how environment-induced interactions near a reflecting boundary affect entanglement dynamics of two atoms.
motivation: Understanding entanglement dynamics in open quantum systems is important for quantum information processing, but the specific setting of a reflecting boundary is niche.
method: Uses open quantum systems framework with master equation, incorporating atom-boundary and interatomic interactions mediated by the vacuum field.
result: Environment-induced interactions can enhance or suppress entanglement depending on atomic separation and boundary distance.
conclusion: The boundary and interatomic interactions significantly modify entanglement dynamics, but the work is more about fundamental physics than direct quantum information applications.

title: Evolution Of Quantum State Texture Under Lorentz Transformations: Invariance, Competition, And Sensitivity In Single-particle And Bipartite Entangled Systems
authors: Zhiming Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiming Huang

Quantum state texture (QST), an emerging resource quantifying the global structural complexity of quantum states within a computational basis, exhibits dynamical behavior under relativistic frameworks that remains largely unexplored. This paper systematically investigates the evolution of QST under …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062438] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how quantum state texture evolves under Lorentz transformations for single-particle and bipartite entangled states.
motivation: To understand the behavior of a newly proposed quantum resource, quantum state texture, in relativistic settings.
method: Analytical calculations of quantum state texture under Lorentz boosts for single-qubit and two-qubit states.
result: Quantum state texture is not Lorentz invariant; its evolution depends on the state and boost parameters, showing competition and sensitivity.
conclusion: Quantum state texture is a frame-dependent quantity, which may have implications for relativistic quantum information protocols.

title: $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric Spin-boson Model With A Continuous Bosonic Spectrum: Exceptional Points And Dynamics
authors: Yong-Xin Zhang And Qing-Hu Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Xin Zhang and Qing-Hu Chen

This work studies a [MATH]-symmetric non-Hermitian spin-boson model consisting of a non-Hermitian two-level system coupled to a continuous bosonic bath. The static properties of the system are analyzed through a projection method derived from the displacement operator. We find that only a si…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063723] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a PT-symmetric non-Hermitian spin-boson model with a continuous bosonic bath, focusing on exceptional points and dynamics.
motivation: To understand the static and dynamic properties of PT-symmetric non-Hermitian systems coupled to a continuous bosonic bath, which is relevant for open quantum systems.
method: A projection method derived from the displacement operator is used to analyze the static properties, and the dynamics are studied via the time-dependent Schrödinger equation.
result: Only a single exceptional point is found, and the dynamics exhibit PT-symmetry breaking and revival phenomena.
conclusion: The PT-symmetric spin-boson model with a continuous spectrum shows unique exceptional point behavior and non-Hermitian dynamics, but the connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is not emphasized.

title: Breakdown Of Bosonic Thouless Pump Due To Interaction In A Quasiperiodic Lattice
authors: Suman Mondal, Emmanuel Gottlob, Fabian Heidrich-Meisner, And Ulrich Schneider
abstract:
Author(s): Suman Mondal, Emmanuel Gottlob, Fabian Heidrich-Meisner, and Ulrich Schneider

Remarkably, even weak interactions cause of a breakdown of the quantized Thouless pump in a bosonic quasicrystal, despite its known robustness against disorder. Sharp jumps in the transport as a function of interaction strength are traced back to the closing of specific doublon channels. Most strikingly, repulsive doublons – two bosons occupying the same site – survive in the lowest band but dissociate in higher ones, draining energy from the driven system rather than heating it.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235131] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Weak interactions cause breakdown of quantized Thouless pumping in a bosonic quasicrystal due to doublon dissociation.
motivation: Understanding how interactions affect topological pumping in interacting bosonic systems, which is relevant for quantum transport and thermodynamics.
method: Numerical simulations and analytical modeling of a bosonic quasiperiodic lattice with weak interactions, studying doublon dynamics.
result: Interactions lead to sharp jumps in transport and breakdown of quantization; repulsive doublons survive in the lowest band but dissociate in higher bands.
conclusion: Interactions can destroy topological protection even when disorder does not, highlighting the role of doublon channels in energy dissipation.

title: Spin-correlation Dynamics: A Semiclassical Framework For Nonlinear Quantum Magnetism
authors: Lukas Körber, Pim Coenders, And Johan H. Mentink
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas Körber, Pim Coenders, and Johan H. Mentink

Classical nonlinear theories are highly successful in describing far-from-equilibrium dynamics in magnetism, including phenomena such as parametric resonance, ultrafast switching, and even chaos. However, at ultrashort length and time scales, where quantum correlations become significant, these mode…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214436] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A semiclassical framework for nonlinear quantum magnetism that captures spin correlations beyond classical theory.
motivation: Classical nonlinear theories fail at ultrashort scales where quantum correlations matter; a framework bridging classical and quantum dynamics is needed.
method: Develops a semiclassical approach incorporating quantum spin correlations into nonlinear dynamics, likely using mean-field or truncated Wigner approximations.
result: The framework reproduces classical nonlinear phenomena while adding quantum corrections, enabling study of far-from-equilibrium quantum magnetism.
conclusion: Provides a practical tool for simulating nonlinear quantum spin dynamics, but does not directly address information thermodynamics or quantum information.

title: Exact Nonlinear Dynamics Of Single Band Metallic Systems With Dissipation: From Optical To Dc Currents
authors: J. M. Alendouro Pinho, B. Amorim, Yuliy V. Bludov, And J. M. Viana Parente Lopes
abstract:
Author(s): J. M. Alendouro Pinho, B. Amorim, Yuliy V. Bludov, and J. M. Viana Parente Lopes

The theory of open quantum systems is one of the most essential tools for the development of quantum technologies. A particular area of interest is in the optical response of solid state systems, where dissipation is introduced phenomenologically through the relaxation time approximation and its eff…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224309] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an exact nonlinear response theory for single-band metallic systems with dissipation, focusing on optical and DC currents.
motivation: Understanding nonlinear optical response in dissipative solid-state systems is important for quantum technologies, but the paper's focus is on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use the relaxation time approximation within an open quantum systems framework to derive exact nonlinear response formulas for single-band metals.
result: They obtain exact expressions for nonlinear conductivities and show how dissipation affects optical and DC currents.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous treatment of nonlinear response in dissipative metals, but its relevance to information thermodynamics is limited as it does not address thermodynamic constraints or information processing.

title: Exact Steady States And Fragmentation-induced Relaxation In The No-passing Asymmetric Simple Exclusion Process
authors: Urei Miura
abstract:
Author(s): Urei Miura

We introduce a multispecies generalization of the asymmetric simple exclusion process with a “no-passing” constraint, forbidding overtaking, on a one-dimensional reflecting (closed) chain without particle reservoirs. This no-passing rule fragments the Hilbert space into an exponential number of disj…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064129] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a multispecies asymmetric simple exclusion process with a no-passing constraint, revealing Hilbert space fragmentation and exact steady states.
motivation: Understanding relaxation dynamics in constrained classical stochastic systems with many degrees of freedom, which may inform non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: The authors introduce a no-passing rule in a multispecies ASEP on a closed chain, analyze the fragmented Hilbert space, and derive exact steady states using matrix product states or combinatorial methods.
result: The Hilbert space fragments into exponentially many sectors, each with its own steady state, leading to fragmentation-induced relaxation and non-ergodic behavior.
conclusion: The no-passing constraint fundamentally alters the relaxation dynamics, providing a classical analog of Hilbert space fragmentation in quantum systems.

title: Correlated Measurements In Single-particle-tracking Dynamics
authors: Wen Bao, Rui Xing, Hai-Yang Wang, And Jing-Dong Bao
abstract:
Author(s): Wen Bao, Rui Xing, Hai-Yang Wang, and Jing-Dong Bao

We investigate the time-averaged displacement correlation function in single-particle tracking within the generalized Langevin equation framework, reformulated in terms of the velocity correlation function. We identify scaling laws for the normalized displacement correlation function applicable to b…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064128] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies displacement correlation functions in single-particle tracking using generalized Langevin dynamics, focusing on scaling laws and memory effects.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of single particles in complex environments is important for biophysics and soft matter, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors reformulate the generalized Langevin equation in terms of velocity correlation functions and derive scaling laws for the normalized displacement correlation function.
result: They identify scaling laws for the displacement correlation function that depend on the memory kernel and noise properties.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for analyzing single-particle tracking data, but has no direct relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Resetting Of Underdamped Brownian Motion
authors: Hanna Franke And Igor M. Sokolov
abstract:
Author(s): Hanna Franke and Igor M. Sokolov

We study underdamped Brownian motion under Poissonian resetting, where we apply two different full resetting procedures. The first one resets both position and velocity to zero, while the second one resets the displacement to zero but takes the velocity after resetting to follow a Maxwell distributi…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064125] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies underdamped Brownian motion under Poissonian resetting with two different resetting protocols, analyzing the resulting steady states and relaxation dynamics.
motivation: Resetting processes are common in stochastic thermodynamics and can model systems like search processes or biochemical reactions. Understanding underdamped dynamics is important for realistic modeling.
method: The authors solve the Fokker-Planck equation for underdamped Brownian motion with resetting, considering two protocols: full resetting of position and velocity to zero, and resetting position to zero while sampling velocity from a Maxwell distribution.
result: They derive exact expressions for the stationary probability distributions and relaxation times, showing that the two protocols lead to different steady states and that the relaxation can be non-exponential.
conclusion: The work provides a detailed analytical treatment of resetting in underdamped systems, highlighting the importance of the resetting protocol on the dynamics and steady-state properties.

title: Optical Spin Pumping In Silicon
authors: Stefano Achilli, Damiano Marian, Mario Lodari, Luca Moreschini, Emiliano Bonera, Giordano Scappucci, Jacopo Pedrini, Michele Virgilio, And Fabio Pezzoli
abstract:
Author(s): Stefano Achilli, Damiano Marian, Mario Lodari, Luca Moreschini, Emiliano Bonera, Giordano Scappucci, Jacopo Pedrini, Michele Virgilio, and Fabio Pezzoli

The optical generation of an out-of-equilibrium spin population is a keystone process for quantum technologies and spintronics alike. Although this is an established technique for studying direct band-gap semiconductors, it has been proven limited in materials that possess weak oscillator strengths …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023302] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optical spin pumping in silicon, a key process for quantum technologies and spintronics.
motivation: Optical generation of spin polarization is established in direct band-gap semiconductors but limited in indirect band-gap materials like silicon; the authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors use optical spin pumping with circularly polarized light and measure the resulting spin polarization via Kerr rotation or similar techniques.
result: They achieve efficient optical spin pumping in silicon, demonstrating a viable method for creating out-of-equilibrium spin populations.
conclusion: Optical spin pumping in silicon is feasible and can be used for quantum technologies and spintronics, though the paper focuses on the physical demonstration rather than integration into a quantum information platform.

title: Far-field Heat Transfer And Monochromatic Thermal Currents In A Cylindrical Nonreciprocal Cavity
authors: Guillem Masdemont, Julien Legendre, And Georgia T. Papadakis
abstract:
Author(s): Guillem Masdemont, Julien Legendre, and Georgia T. Papadakis

Breaking Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation yields opportunities in one-way radiative thermal transport and circuitry. We investigate its consequences in the far-field regime in cylindrical cavities, by employing a specular ray-tracing algorithm. At thermal equilibrium, we show that violation of K…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023293] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies far-field heat transfer and monochromatic thermal currents in cylindrical nonreciprocal cavities, focusing on breaking Kirchhoff's law.
motivation: To explore the consequences of nonreciprocal thermal radiation in far-field cavities for one-way radiative thermal transport and circuitry.
method: A specular ray-tracing algorithm is employed to analyze thermal radiation in cylindrical cavities with nonreciprocal materials.
result: Violation of Kirchhoff's law leads to monochromatic thermal currents and directional heat transfer in the far-field regime.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal cavities enable control over thermal radiation, with potential applications in thermal management and energy conversion.

title: Polarization Symmetry As A Signature Of Bell States In Compton Scattering
authors: Peter Caradonna And Kenji Shimazoe
abstract:
Author(s): Peter Caradonna and Kenji Shimazoe

We analyze bipartite photon states in coincidence Compton polarimetry at energies where polarization must be inferred from Compton scattering. Polarization symmetry, defined as equality of signal and idler degree-of-polarization responses for all scattering angles, holds if and only if the initial t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023288] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that polarization symmetry in Compton scattering can serve as a signature of Bell states, providing a method to certify entanglement without direct polarization measurements.
motivation: To develop a practical method for detecting Bell states in high-energy photon pairs where standard polarization measurements are difficult.
method: The authors analyze bipartite photon states in coincidence Compton polarimetry and derive that equality of signal and idler degree-of-polarization responses for all scattering angles (polarization symmetry) holds iff the initial two-photon state is a Bell state.
result: Polarization symmetry is a necessary and sufficient condition for Bell states, enabling entanglement certification via Compton scattering.
conclusion: This work offers a new experimental signature for Bell states, relevant for quantum information applications at high energies.

title: Liouvillian Topology And Nonreciprocal Dynamics In Open Floquet Chains
authors: Florian Koch, Yu-Min Hu, And Jan Carl Budich
abstract:
Author(s): Florian Koch, Yu-Min Hu, and Jan Carl Budich

Open quantum systems far from thermal equilibrium can exhibit remarkable physical phenomena including topological properties without a direct equilibrium counterpart. Along these lines, in periodically driven-dissipative systems within the effective non-Hermitian (NH) Hamiltonian approximation spect…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023270] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological properties and nonreciprocal dynamics in open Floquet chains using a non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian approach.
motivation: To explore topological phenomena in open quantum systems far from equilibrium, specifically in periodically driven-dissipative systems.
method: The authors analyze a one-dimensional driven-dissipative chain using the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian approximation and compute topological invariants.
result: They identify nontrivial Liouvillian topology and nonreciprocal dynamics, including the emergence of exceptional points and directional amplification.
conclusion: Open Floquet systems can host topological phases without equilibrium counterparts, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Finite-temperature Lanczos Method
authors: Gian Gentinetta, Friederike Metz, William Kirby, And Giuseppe Carleo
abstract:
Author(s): Gian Gentinetta, Friederike Metz, William Kirby, and Giuseppe Carleo

The computation of thermal properties of quantum many-body systems is a central challenge in our understanding of quantum mechanics. We introduce the quantum finite-temperature Lanczos method (QFTLM), which extends the finite-temperature Lanczos method to quantum computers by combining real-time qua…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023285] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a quantum algorithm for computing thermal properties of many-body systems by combining real-time evolution with the finite-temperature Lanczos method.
motivation: Computing thermal properties of quantum many-body systems is computationally challenging on classical computers, and quantum computers may offer advantages.
method: The quantum finite-temperature Lanczos method (QFTLM) uses real-time quantum evolution to generate a Krylov subspace, then performs classical Lanczos diagonalization to compute thermal observables.
result: The method is demonstrated on small systems and shows potential for near-term quantum devices, though it requires many measurements and deep circuits.
conclusion: QFTLM provides a hybrid quantum-classical approach to finite-temperature simulations, but its practical advantage over classical methods remains to be established.

title: Nonstabilizerness In Molecular Bonding
authors: Matthieu Sarkis And Alexandre Tkatchenko
abstract:
Author(s): Matthieu Sarkis and Alexandre Tkatchenko

Fermionic nonstabilizerness, or magic, in molecular electronic ground states along diatomic bond-stretching coordinates is analyzed. For H
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022048] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes nonstabilizerness (magic) in molecular bonding, showing that magic measures peak at intermediate bond lengths, providing new quantum-information insight beyond entanglement.
motivation: To understand molecular bonding from a quantum information perspective, specifically using nonstabilizerness as a resource beyond entanglement.
method: Computes magic measures (e.g., stabilizer Rényi entropy) for electronic ground states of diatomic molecules along bond-stretching coordinates.
result: Magic forms an intermediate-separation peak near rapid changes in the binding-energy curve, correlating with bond formation.
conclusion: Nonstabilizerness provides complementary insight into molecular bonding, suggesting a role for magic in chemical phenomena.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, and Juani Bermejo-Vega

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses symmetry reduction to accelerate classical simulation of Clifford-dominated quantum circuits by optimizing stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is important for benchmarking and verification, but stabilizer-based methods become costly for circuits with many non-Clifford gates. Symmetries can reduce the effective Hilbert space dimension.
method: The authors develop strong and weak symmetry reduction techniques to decompose multiqubit unitaries into stabilizer parts more efficiently, leveraging group-theoretic methods.
result: They demonstrate that symmetry-accelerated decompositions can handle larger circuits than previous methods, extending the tractable regime for Clifford-dominated circuits.
conclusion: Symmetry reduction is a powerful tool for classical simulation of near-Clifford circuits, potentially aiding in the validation of quantum devices.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a tight-binding lattice for near-optimal quantum simulation.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints and the need for efficient dilation methods.
method: The paper introduces a dilation approach that maps ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, using moment-matching to achieve near-optimal query complexity.
result: The framework yields quantum algorithms with near-optimal query complexity for simulating linear differential equations and other nonunitary processes.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient method for quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics, overcoming hardware connectivity limitations.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses Fourier neural operators to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of time-periodic quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling periodically driven quantum systems is computationally expensive; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations in frequency space.
method: The authors employ Fourier neural operators, which learn mappings in Fourier space, to approximate the Floquet Hamiltonian and time evolution of observables from training data.
result: The method accurately extrapolates dynamics beyond the training time window and captures operator growth in driven systems.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a physically faithful and efficient surrogate for simulating time-periodic quantum systems.

title: Quantum Filtering And Analysis Of Multiplicities In Eigenvalue Spectra
authors: Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, And Ruizhe Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, and Ruizhe Zhang

A quantum filtering algorithm identifies clusters of eigenvalues and their multiplicities, enabling efficient spectral analysis beyond worst-case complexity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020318] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: A quantum filtering algorithm for identifying eigenvalue clusters and multiplicities in spectra.
motivation: Efficient spectral analysis beyond worst-case complexity is needed for quantum systems.
method: The algorithm uses quantum filtering to detect clusters and estimate multiplicities.
result: It achieves efficiency beyond worst-case complexity for spectral analysis.
conclusion: The algorithm provides a practical tool for quantum spectral analysis.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying approaches for complex systems in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model diverse phenomena from cellular biology to traffic flow, but lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors review field-theoretic techniques (e.g., Doi-Peliti formalism, path integrals) to treat stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: They show how these methods provide a systematic way to compute correlation functions, fluctuation spectra, and large deviations.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods offer a powerful unifying language for stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with broad applicability beyond physics.

title: Three-qubit-state Preparation: Classification And Explicit Circuits
authors: Yonghae Lee And Taewan Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Yonghae Lee and Taewan Kim

We develop a deterministic and fully explicit framework for preparing an arbitrary three-qubit pure state from its computational-basis amplitudes. Our approach exploits bipartite Schmidt structure: we classify three-qubit states into five types with respect to a [MATH] bipartition and provide concret…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062444] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A deterministic framework for preparing arbitrary three-qubit pure states using bipartite Schmidt decomposition and explicit quantum circuits.
motivation: Efficient state preparation is essential for quantum computing and communication, but explicit circuits for arbitrary three-qubit states are lacking.
method: Classifies three-qubit states into five types based on Schmidt rank across bipartitions, then constructs explicit circuits using controlled gates and local unitaries.
result: Provides explicit quantum circuits for each type, with gate counts and depth analysis.
conclusion: The framework offers a systematic and resource-efficient method for preparing any three-qubit pure state.

title: Gap Reopening As A Possible Signature Of Coupling Between Majorana Zero Modes In $\mathrm{Sn}\text{−}{(\mathrm{Bi},\mathrm{Sb})}_{2}{(\mathrm{Te},\mathrm{S})}_{3}$-based Josephson Trijunctions
authors: Duolin Wang, Xiang Zhang, Yunxiao Zhang, Heng Zhang, Fucong Fei, Xiang Wang, Bing Li, Xiaozhou Yang, Yukun Shi, Zhongmou Jia, Enna Zhuo, Yuyang Huang, Anqi Wang, Zenan Shi, Zhaozheng Lyu, Xiaohui Song, Peiling Li, Bingbing Tong, Ziwei Dou, Jie Shen, Guangtong Liu, Fanming Qu, Fengqi Song, And Li Lu
abstract:
