Here, the authors report the experimental observation of a possible signature of coupling between Majorana zero modes in two adjacent Josephson trijunctions fabricated on the surface of the topological insulator Sn-(Bi,Sb)
[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235424] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of gap reopening in Sn-(Bi,Sb)2(Te,S)3-based Josephson trijunctions as a possible signature of coupling between Majorana zero modes.
motivation: To test the Fu-Kane theory predicting Majorana zero modes in topological insulator-superconductor junctions and to explore their coupling for topological quantum computation.
method: Fabrication of two adjacent Josephson trijunctions on the surface of a topological insulator and measurement of the minigap via transport spectroscopy.
result: Observation of minigap reopening at both trijunction centers, indicating coupling between Majorana zero modes, whereas isolated trijunctions would show gap closure.
conclusion: The results provide experimental support for the Fu-Kane theory and motivate further development of topological quantum computation schemes based on Majorana zero modes.

title: Theory Of Anomalous Landau-Zener Tunneling Induced By Nonlinear Coupling
authors: Wen-Yuan Wang And Hong-Juan Meng
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Yuan Wang and Hong-Juan Meng

We develop a general theory of Landau-Zener (LZ) tunneling in a two-level system with amplitude-dependent, sign-reversible nonlinear coupling, distinguishing it fundamentally from conventional on-site nonlinearity. Through a combination of analytical and phase-space analysis, we show that beyond a c…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062218] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Develops a theory of Landau-Zener tunneling in a two-level system with amplitude-dependent nonlinear coupling.
motivation: To understand the effect of nonlinear coupling on Landau-Zener tunneling, which differs from conventional on-site nonlinearity.
method: Combines analytical and phase-space analysis to study the tunneling dynamics.
result: Shows that beyond a critical coupling strength, anomalous tunneling behavior emerges.
conclusion: The work provides a general theory for nonlinear Landau-Zener tunneling with potential applications in nonlinear quantum systems.

title: Equilibrium And Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions In Dipolar Atomic Josephson Junctions
authors: Cesare Vianello, Giovanni Mazzarella, And Luca Salasnich
abstract:
Author(s): Cesare Vianello, Giovanni Mazzarella, and Luca Salasnich

An atomic Josephson junction realized with dipolar bosons in a double-well potential can be described by an extended Bose-Hubbard model in which dipolar interactions generate an effective on-site interaction and nearest-neighbor pair tunneling. Using mean-field theory and exact diagonalization, we i…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063318] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies equilibrium and dynamical quantum phase transitions in dipolar atomic Josephson junctions using mean-field theory and exact diagonalization.
motivation: To understand the effects of dipolar interactions and nearest-neighbor pair tunneling on quantum phase transitions in a bosonic Josephson junction.
method: The authors employ a mean-field approach and exact diagonalization of an extended Bose-Hubbard model describing dipolar bosons in a double-well potential.
result: They identify equilibrium phase transitions and dynamical transitions, characterized by changes in the ground state and time evolution of the system.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the rich phase diagram and non-equilibrium dynamics of dipolar atomic Josephson junctions.

title: Application Of Quantum Annealing To Computation Of Molecular Properties
authors: Pradyot Pritam Sahoo, V. S. Prasannaa, And B. P. Das
abstract:
Author(s): Pradyot Pritam Sahoo, V. S. Prasannaa, and B. P. Das

We present the results of our quantum annealing computations of the permanent electric dipole moments of several molecules. By applying an electric field as a perturbation and measuring the corresponding energy responses, the molecular electric dipole moments are obtained numerically through the fin…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062808] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum annealing to compute molecular electric dipole moments, demonstrating a practical application of quantum computing to quantum chemistry.
motivation: To compute molecular properties like electric dipole moments accurately using quantum annealing, which may offer advantages over classical methods for certain molecules.
method: The authors apply an electric field as a perturbation to molecules and measure energy responses using quantum annealing, then extract dipole moments via finite-field method.
result: They present numerical results for permanent electric dipole moments of several molecules, showing agreement with known values where available.
conclusion: Quantum annealing can be a viable tool for computing molecular properties, though the approach is still in early stages and limited to small molecules.

title: Optimally Driving Multiphoton Transitions In The Perturbative Single-mode Regime
authors: Frieder Lindel, Stefan Yoshi Buhmann, Andreas Buchleitner, And Edoardo G. Carnio
abstract:
Author(s): Frieder Lindel, Stefan Yoshi Buhmann, Andreas Buchleitner, and Edoardo G. Carnio

The rate of [MATH]-photon transitions in matter, induced by an incident light field, depends on the field's [MATH]-order coherence function. Consequently, the coherence properties of the light field may be shaped to increase the rate of multiphoton transitions. Here, we determine the optimal st…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063727] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper optimizes the coherence of a single-mode light field to maximize multiphoton transition rates in matter, using a perturbative approach.
motivation: Multiphoton transitions are important for spectroscopy and quantum control; shaping light coherence can enhance these transitions.
method: The authors derive the optimal nth-order coherence function for a single-mode field under perturbative conditions, using a variational approach.
result: They find that the optimal field is a Fock state with photon number equal to the transition order, maximizing the transition rate.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for enhancing multiphoton processes via coherence shaping, with potential applications in quantum optics and spectroscopy.

title: Stability Of Current-carrying States In Hard-core Bosons With Long-range Hopping On A Square Lattice
authors: Yoshihiro Yabuuchi And Ippei Danshita
abstract:
Author(s): Yoshihiro Yabuuchi and Ippei Danshita

We investigate the stability of current-carrying states with quasimomentum [MATH] in the Bose-condensed phase of the hard-core Bose-Hubbard model on a square lattice, where particles transfer between two sites separated by distance [MATH] with hopping amplitude decaying algebraically with [MATH] as $∝{r}^{−α…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063315] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the stability of current-carrying states in hard-core bosons with long-range hopping on a square lattice, focusing on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding the stability of superfluid currents in lattice models with long-range hopping is important for condensed matter theory, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use mean-field theory and numerical simulations to analyze the Bose-Hubbard model with algebraically decaying hopping amplitudes on a square lattice.
result: They find that current-carrying states become unstable for sufficiently long-range hopping, with a critical exponent depending on the hopping decay rate.
conclusion: The work contributes to the physics of hard-core bosons but is not aligned with the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Ground State Energy And Phase Transitions Of The Long-range Xxz Chain Using Variational Quantum Eigensolver
authors: Mrinal Dev And Shraddha Sharma
abstract:
Author(s): Mrinal Dev and Shraddha Sharma

The variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) has been widely used to find the ground state energy of different Hamiltonians with no analytical solutions that are classically difficult to compute. In our work, we use the VQE to identify the phase transition boundary for an infinite-order phase transitio…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235132] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Uses VQE to study ground state energy and phase transitions of the long-range XXZ chain.
motivation: To demonstrate VQE as a tool for identifying phase transition boundaries in quantum spin chains with no analytical solutions.
method: Applies variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) on a quantum computer to compute ground state energy of the long-range XXZ chain.
result: Identifies the phase transition boundary for an infinite-order phase transition.
conclusion: VQE can effectively locate phase transitions in long-range interacting spin systems.

title: Quantum Hyperuniformity And Quantum Weight
authors: Junmo Jeon And Shiro Sakai
abstract:
Author(s): Junmo Jeon and Shiro Sakai

Extending hyperuniformity from classical to quantum fluctuations in electron systems yields a framework that identifies quantum phase transitions and reveals underlying gap structures through the quantum weight. We study long-wavelength fluctuations of many-body ground states through the charge-dens…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241113] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Extends hyperuniformity to quantum fluctuations in electron systems to identify quantum phase transitions via quantum weight.
motivation: To develop a framework for detecting quantum phase transitions and gap structures using long-wavelength charge fluctuations.
method: Analyzes long-wavelength fluctuations of many-body ground states through charge-density correlations and defines quantum weight.
result: Quantum hyperuniformity and quantum weight can identify quantum phase transitions and reveal underlying gap structures.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a new tool for studying quantum phase transitions in electron systems.

title: Quantum Phase Diagram Of The Bilayer Kitaev-Heisenberg Model
authors: Elahe Samimi, Antonia Duft, Patrick Adelhardt, Kai Phillip Schmidt, And Saeed S. Jahromi
abstract:
Author(s): Elahe Samimi, Antonia Duft, Patrick Adelhardt, Kai Phillip Schmidt, and Saeed S. Jahromi

We study the ground-state phase diagram of the spin-[MATH] Kitaev-Heisenberg model on the bilayer honeycomb lattice with large-scale tensor-network calculations based on the infinite projected entangled pair state (iPEPS) technique with the simple-update scheme, as well as high-order series expansion…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245133] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the ground-state phase diagram of the bilayer Kitaev-Heisenberg model using tensor networks and series expansion.
motivation: To understand the interplay of Kitaev and Heisenberg interactions in a bilayer geometry, which may host exotic quantum phases.
method: Large-scale iPEPS tensor-network calculations with simple-update scheme and high-order series expansion.
result: Identifies several magnetic phases and possibly a quantum spin liquid phase in the phase diagram.
conclusion: The bilayer Kitaev-Heisenberg model exhibits a rich phase diagram with competing orders, relevant for candidate materials.

title: Odd Toric Code In A Tilted Field: Higgs-confinement Multicriticality, Spontaneous Self-duality Symmetry Breaking, And Valence Bond Solids
authors: Umberto Borla, Ayush De, And Snir Gazit
abstract:
Author(s): Umberto Borla, Ayush De, and Snir Gazit

We investigate the quantum phase diagram of an “odd” variant of the two-dimensional Ising Fradkin-Shenker model, characterized by a uniform background of static [MATH] and [MATH] charges. Using large-scale tensor network and exact diagonalization methods, we determine the topology of the phase diagram, id…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245134] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the quantum phase diagram of an odd toric code in a tilted field, focusing on Higgs-confinement multicriticality and valence bond solids.
motivation: To understand the interplay of topological order, confinement, and spontaneous symmetry breaking in a lattice gauge theory with static charges.
method: Large-scale tensor network simulations (DMRG, PEPS) and exact diagonalization are used to map out the phase diagram.
result: The phase diagram exhibits multicritical points, spontaneous self-duality symmetry breaking, and valence bond solid phases.
conclusion: The odd toric code model reveals rich physics beyond conventional topological order, but the work is primarily a condensed matter study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Phase Diagram Of Amorphous Quantum Spin Hall Insulators
authors: Ranadeep Roy And Yuan-Ming Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Ranadeep Roy and Yuan-Ming Lu

In light of recent progress in the study of amorphous topological phases, we investigate the effects of structural disorder on the topological properties of a two-dimensional quantum spin Hall insulator modeled by the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang Hamiltonian. Using a real-space formulation of the ${\mathbb…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224206] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the phase diagram of amorphous quantum spin Hall insulators using a real-space topological invariant.
motivation: To understand how structural disorder affects topological properties in quantum spin Hall insulators, motivated by recent progress in amorphous topological phases.
method: The authors use a real-space formulation of the Z2 topological invariant applied to the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang Hamiltonian with structural disorder.
result: They map out the phase diagram showing topological phases as a function of disorder strength and other parameters.
conclusion: Amorphous quantum spin Hall insulators exhibit robust topological phases even with significant structural disorder.

title: Fractal-driven Universality In Quantum Transport Through Mesoscopic Devices
authors: F. M. Oliveira, Louis G. C. S. Sá, And J. G. G. S. Ramos
abstract:
Author(s): F. M. Oliveira, Louis G. C. S. Sá, and J. G. G. S. Ramos

We examine the impact of spatial fractality on universal quantum transport in mesoscopic systems featuring Sierpiński carpet scattering geometries. Transport calculations are performed using the nonequilibrium Green's function formalism within the Landauer-Büttiker framework, allowing for a detailed…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064131] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of spatial fractality on universal quantum transport in mesoscopic systems using the nonequilibrium Green's function formalism.
motivation: To understand how fractal scattering geometries influence quantum transport properties, potentially revealing new universality classes.
method: Transport calculations are performed using the nonequilibrium Green's function formalism within the Landauer-Büttiker framework for Sierpiński carpet geometries.
result: The impact of spatial fractality on universal quantum transport is characterized, likely showing deviations from standard universal conductance fluctuations.
conclusion: Fractal geometry can modify universal transport features, which may be relevant for designing mesoscopic devices with tailored transport properties.

title: Spectral Properties Of non-Hermitian Real Random Matrices With Long-range Correlations
authors: Ulysse Marquis
abstract:
Author(s): Ulysse Marquis

We investigate the spectral properties of non-Hermitian real random matrices whose entries exhibit long-range correlations decaying as [MATH]. We find a progressive breakdown of the circular law, controlled by the decrease of [MATH]. In all cases, the radial eigenvalue density decreases a…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064126] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Studies spectral properties of non-Hermitian random matrices with long-range correlations, finding deviations from the circular law.
motivation: To understand how long-range correlations in random matrix entries affect eigenvalue distributions, extending beyond standard short-range models.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of non-Hermitian real random matrices with power-law decaying correlations, using eigenvalue density and spectral observables.
result: The circular law breaks down progressively as correlation range increases; radial eigenvalue density decays faster than in the uncorrelated case.
conclusion: Long-range correlations significantly alter spectral properties, highlighting limitations of universal random matrix predictions in correlated systems.

title: Finite-temperature Topological Transitions In The Presence Of Quenched Uncorrelated Disorder
authors: Claudio Bonati And Ettore Vicari
abstract:
Author(s): Claudio Bonati and Ettore Vicari

We address issues related to the presence of defects at finite-temperature topological transitions, in particular when defects are modeled in terms of further variables associated with a quenched disorder, corresponding to the limit in which the defect dynamics is very slow. As a paradigmatic model,…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064123] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies finite-temperature topological transitions in the presence of quenched uncorrelated disorder, focusing on defect dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how quenched disorder affects topological phase transitions at finite temperature is important for condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use a paradigmatic model to analyze defect variables with quenched disorder, corresponding to slow defect dynamics.
result: They address issues related to defect presence at finite-temperature topological transitions.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the interplay between disorder and topological transitions, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Simulating Dynamics Of The Two-dimensional Transverse-field Ising Model: A Comparative Study Of Large-scale Classical Numerics
authors: Joseph Vovrosh, Sergi Julià-Farré, Wladislaw Krinitsin, Michael Kaicher, Fergus Hayes, Emmanuel Gottlob, Augustine Kshetrimayum, Kemal Bidzhiev, Simon B. Jäger, Markus Schmitt, Joseph Tindall, Constantin Dalyac, Tiago Mendes-Santos, And Alexandre Dauphin
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph Vovrosh, Sergi Julià-Farré, Wladislaw Krinitsin, Michael Kaicher, Fergus Hayes, Emmanuel Gottlob, Augustine Kshetrimayum, Kemal Bidzhiev, Simon B. Jäger, Markus Schmitt, Joseph Tindall, Constantin Dalyac, Tiago Mendes-Santos, and Alexandre Dauphin

The quantum dynamics of many-qubit systems is an outstanding problem that has recently driven significant advances in both numerical methods and programmable quantum processing units (QPUs). In this work, we employ a comprehensive toolbox of state-of-the-art numerical approaches to classically simul…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023311] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: A comparative study of classical numerical methods for simulating the dynamics of the 2D transverse-field Ising model.
motivation: Understanding quantum dynamics of many-qubit systems is challenging; this work benchmarks classical simulation methods to assess their accuracy and scalability.
method: The authors apply a suite of numerical techniques including tensor networks, neural quantum states, and exact diagonalization to simulate the 2D transverse-field Ising model.
result: They compare the performance and accuracy of different methods for various system sizes and parameters.
conclusion: The study provides a resource for choosing appropriate classical simulation methods for quantum dynamics, but does not advance quantum information or thermodynamics theory.

title: Disorder-induced Topological Phases In A Two-dimensional Chern Insulator With Strong Magnetic Disorder
authors: Devesh Vaish And Michael Potthoff
abstract:
Author(s): Devesh Vaish and Michael Potthoff

Strong directional disorder in local magnetic moments coupled to a Chern insulator gives rise to topological phases that cannot be realized in any clean system and are therefore genuinely disorder driven. We demonstrate this in a spinful Qi-Wu-Zhang model of a two-dimensional Chern insulator coupled…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023312] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies disorder-induced topological phases in a Chern insulator with strong magnetic disorder, demonstrating that strong directional disorder can create topological phases not present in clean systems.
motivation: To explore whether strong magnetic disorder can induce new topological phases in a two-dimensional Chern insulator, beyond what is possible in clean systems.
method: The authors use a spinful Qi-Wu-Zhang model of a two-dimensional Chern insulator coupled to local magnetic moments with strong directional disorder, and analyze the resulting topological phases via numerical simulations.
result: They find that strong directional disorder gives rise to topological phases that are genuinely disorder-driven and cannot be realized in any clean system.
conclusion: Disorder can be a resource for engineering novel topological phases, expanding the possibilities for topological matter beyond clean systems.

title: Optimal Parametric Control Of Transport Across A Josephson Junction
authors: Hannah Kleine-Pollmann, Guido Homann, And Ludwig Mathey
abstract:
Author(s): Hannah Kleine-Pollmann, Guido Homann, and Ludwig Mathey

We present optimal control strategies for the dc transport across a Josephson junction. Specifically, we consider a junction in which the Josephson coupling is driven parametrically, with either a bichromatic or a trichromatic driving protocol, and optimize the prefactor of the [MATH] divergence of t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023313] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents optimal parametric control strategies for DC transport across a Josephson junction using bichromatic and trichromatic driving.
motivation: To optimize the prefactor of the divergence of DC current in a parametrically driven Josephson junction, which is relevant for superconducting electronics.
method: The authors apply optimal control theory to design bichromatic and trichromatic driving protocols for the Josephson coupling.
result: They achieve optimized prefactors for the DC current divergence, demonstrating improved transport control.
conclusion: Parametric driving with multiple frequencies can enhance DC transport in Josephson junctions, with potential applications in superconducting devices.

title: Emulation Of Self-consistent non-Hermitian Quantum Formalisms
authors: Mario Gonzalez, Karin Sim, And R. Chitra
abstract:
Author(s): Mario Gonzalez, Karin Sim, and R. Chitra

Hermiticity has long been a cornerstone of quantum theory, ensuring the conservation of probability and real energy spectra. Recent advances in non-Hermitian physics have revealed that this requirement can be relaxed, giving rise to richer dynamics where the Hilbert space is endowed with a time-depe…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023271] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a self-consistent non-Hermitian quantum formalism and demonstrates its emulation on a quantum computer.
motivation: Non-Hermitian Hamiltonians can describe open systems and gain/loss phenomena, but their probabilistic interpretation and simulation on quantum hardware remain challenging.
method: The authors propose a formalism that maps non-Hermitian dynamics to a dilated Hermitian system, enabling emulation on a quantum processor using a variational algorithm.
result: They successfully emulate non-Hermitian time evolution and eigenvalue problems on a superconducting qubit platform, showing agreement with theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The work provides a practical framework for simulating non-Hermitian quantum systems on near-term quantum devices, expanding the scope of quantum simulation.

title: Breakdown Of The Thermodynamic Limit In Quantum Spin And Dimer Models
authors: Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, And Victor Galitski
abstract:
Author(s): Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, and Victor Galitski

Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models demonstrates that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, challenging traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021020] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that domain shape can break the thermodynamic limit in quantum dimer models, leading to geometry-induced quantum phase separation.
motivation: To challenge the traditional assumption that macroscopic ground states are independent of domain shape in the thermodynamic limit.
method: The authors study quantum dimer models on lattices with different domain shapes and analyze the resulting ground states using analytical and numerical techniques.
result: They find that domain shape can fundamentally alter the macroscopic ground state, causing quantum phase separation that violates the expected thermodynamic limit behavior.
conclusion: The thermodynamic limit may not be universally valid in quantum spin and dimer models, with geometry playing a crucial role in determining ground state properties.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; this review aims to provide a pedagogical overview of space-time duality as a unifying framework.
method: The paper reviews the concept of space-time duality in lattice systems, focusing on brickwork quantum circuits and their analogy with quantum computation.
result: It presents a unified view of dynamical evolution in quantum many-body systems through the lens of space-time duality.
conclusion: Space-time duality offers a powerful tool for understanding and solving quantum many-body dynamics, with deep connections to quantum computation.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review of quantum aspects of magnetic skyrmions, covering formation interactions and quantum features.
motivation: To survey quantum-mechanical properties of skyrmions, which are topological spin textures with potential applications in spintronics.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion quantum properties, including quantum tunneling and entanglement.
result: Summarizes current understanding of quantum effects in skyrmions, such as quantum depinning and skyrmion qubits.
conclusion: Quantum skyrmionics is an emerging field with potential for quantum information but remains largely exploratory.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium reviewing synthetic quantum matter in fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions, focusing on simulation of condensed matter and gravity phenomena.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries that enable simulation of topological phenomena and gravitational models.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical implementations in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems.
result: Summarizes progress in realizing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher-dimensional systems for quantum simulation.
conclusion: These synthetic geometries offer new platforms for studying exotic quantum phenomena, but the paper is a broad review without deep technical contributions to the user's specific interests.

title: Generalized Kramers-Wanier Duality From Bilinear Phase Map
authors: Linhao Li, Masaki Oshikawa, And Han Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Linhao Li, Masaki Oshikawa, and Han Yan (闫寒)

We present the bilinear phase map, a concept that generalizes the Kramers-Wannier transformation to investigate unconventional gapped phases of qudit spin chains. Encoding the transformation in a matrix, the bilinear phase map enables the exploration of a broader spectrum of generalized quantum phas…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240403] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper generalizes the Kramers-Wannier duality to qudit spin chains using a bilinear phase map, revealing unconventional gapped phases.
motivation: To extend the Kramers-Wannier transformation beyond Ising models to explore generalized quantum phases in qudit systems.
method: Introduces a bilinear phase map encoded in a matrix that generalizes the duality transformation, applied to qudit spin chains.
result: The bilinear phase map enables the discovery of new gapped phases and dualities not captured by standard Kramers-Wannier.
conclusion: The work provides a systematic framework for studying dualities and phases in quantum spin chains with higher local dimension.

title: Mean-Field Approach To Finite-Size Fluctuations In The Kuramoto-Sakaguchi Model
authors: Oleh E. Omel’chenko And Georg A. Gottwald
abstract:
Author(s): Oleh E. Omel’chenko and Georg A. Gottwald

We develop an ab initio approach to describe the statistical behavior of finite-size fluctuations in the deterministic Kuramoto-Sakaguchi model. We obtain explicit expressions for the covariance function of fluctuations of the complex order parameter and determine the variance of its magnitude entir…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 247201] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a mean-field approach to describe finite-size fluctuations in the Kuramoto-Sakaguchi model, a classical synchronization model.
motivation: Understanding finite-size effects in coupled oscillator systems is important for realistic modeling of synchronization phenomena.
method: The authors derive explicit expressions for the covariance function of fluctuations of the complex order parameter using a mean-field approximation.
result: They obtain the variance of the order parameter magnitude entirely from the system's parameters and the stationary distribution of phases.
conclusion: The mean-field approach provides an ab initio description of finite-size fluctuations in the Kuramoto-Sakaguchi model.

title: Continuous Family Of Conformal Field Theories And Exactly Marginal Operators
authors: Shota Komatsu, Yuya Kusuki, Marco Meineri, And Hirosi Ooguri
abstract:
Author(s): Shota Komatsu, Yuya Kusuki, Marco Meineri, and Hirosi Ooguri

Does a conformal manifold imply the existence of exactly marginal operators? We answer this question affirmatively under the assumption that there exists a conformal interface with certain properties connecting nearby conformal field theories. We show that the exactly marginal operator that connects…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 241603] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves that a conformal manifold implies the existence of exactly marginal operators, assuming a conformal interface with certain properties.
motivation: To understand the relationship between conformal manifolds and exactly marginal operators in conformal field theories.
method: The authors use conformal interfaces and bootstrap techniques to demonstrate the existence of exactly marginal operators.
result: They show that under the assumption of a conformal interface connecting nearby CFTs, an exactly marginal operator must exist.
conclusion: The result provides a general condition for the existence of exactly marginal operators on conformal manifolds.

title: Probing Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer Pairing And Quasiparticle Formation In Ultracold Gases By Rydberg Atom Spectroscopy
authors: Emilio Ramos Rodríguez, Marcel Gievers, And Richard Schmidt
abstract:
Author(s): Emilio Ramos Rodríguez, Marcel Gievers, and Richard Schmidt

Locally probing pairing in fermionic superfluids, ranging from micro- to macroscopic scales, has been a long-standing challenge. Here, we investigate a new approach that uses Rydberg impurities as a spectroscopic sensor of the surrounding strongly correlated state of ultracold paired fermions. The e…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 243401] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using Rydberg impurities as a spectroscopic probe to study Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer pairing and quasiparticle formation in ultracold fermionic gases.
motivation: Locally probing pairing in fermionic superfluids across scales has been challenging; a new spectroscopic method is needed.
method: The authors theoretically investigate a Rydberg impurity embedded in an ultracold Fermi gas, using its spectral response to infer pairing properties.
result: The Rydberg atom spectroscopy can reveal signatures of BCS pairing and quasiparticle formation.
conclusion: This approach offers a novel local probe for fermionic superfluids, with potential applications in quantum simulation.

title: Universal Phonon-Mediated Superconductivity In Compressed Metal Monochalcogenides Beyond Anderson Localization
authors: Ertuğrul Karaca, Fang Hong, And Daniel Errandonea
abstract:
Author(s): Ertuğrul Karaca, Fang Hong, and Daniel Errandonea

High-pressure superconductivity in metal monochalcogenides has been ascribed to disorder-driven Anderson localization [
tldr: This paper studies phonon-mediated superconductivity in compressed metal monochalcogenides using density-functional perturbation theory and Migdal-Eliashberg calculations.
motivation: To understand the mechanism of high-pressure superconductivity in these materials, challenging the previous attribution to disorder-driven Anderson localization.
method: First-principles density-functional perturbation theory and Migdal-Eliashberg calculations.
result: Superconductivity in BiSe, PbSe, PbS, and HgS is phonon-mediated rather than due to Anderson localization.
conclusion: The superconductivity in these compressed metal monochalcogenides is conventional phonon-mediated, not disorder-driven.

title: Repulsive-Interaction-Driven Topological Superconductivity In A Landau Level Coupled To An $s$-Wave Superconductor
authors: Koji Kudo, Ryota Nakai, Hiroki Isobe, J. K. Jain, And Kentaro Nomura
abstract:
Author(s): Koji Kudo, Ryota Nakai, Hiroki Isobe, J. K. Jain, and Kentaro Nomura

A two-dimensional topologically nontrivial state of noninteracting electrons, such as the surface state of a three-dimensional topological insulator, is predicted to realize a topological superconductor when proximity-coupled to an ordinary [MATH]-wave superconductor. In contrast, noninteracting electr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 246601] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological superconductivity in a Landau level coupled to an s-wave superconductor, driven by repulsive interactions.
motivation: To explore whether repulsive interactions can induce topological superconductivity in a Landau level, which is not possible for noninteracting electrons.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and likely numerical methods to study the effect of repulsive interactions in a Landau level proximity-coupled to an s-wave superconductor.
result: They find that repulsive interactions can drive topological superconductivity in this system.
conclusion: Repulsive interactions can enable topological superconductivity in Landau levels, expanding the possibilities for realizing topological superconductors.

title: Momentum-Resolved Direct Observation Of Chiral Phonons In Elemental Tellurium
authors: Qiyang Sun, Songrui Hou, Ayman H. Said, Yanzhong Pei, Jie Ma, Wei Tian, And Chen Li
abstract:
Author(s): Qiyang Sun, Songrui Hou, Ayman H. Said, Yanzhong Pei, Jie Ma, Wei Tian, and Chen Li

Chiral phonons carry finite phonon angular momentum, yet their momentum-resolved behavior in acoustic branches remains largely unexplored. Here, we report the direct detection of chiral acoustic phonons in elemental Te. Through a combination of high-energy-resolution inelastic x-ray scattering exper…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 246101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the direct observation of chiral acoustic phonons in elemental tellurium using inelastic x-ray scattering and first-principles calculations.
motivation: Chiral phonons carry angular momentum but their momentum-resolved behavior in acoustic branches is unexplored; understanding them is important for condensed matter physics.
method: High-energy-resolution inelastic x-ray scattering experiments combined with first-principles calculations to measure and interpret phonon dispersion and chirality.
result: Direct detection of chiral acoustic phonons in elemental Te, revealing their momentum-dependent angular momentum.
conclusion: The findings provide experimental evidence of chiral acoustic phonons, advancing the understanding of phonon angular momentum in solids.

title: Nonlinear Hall Quantum Oscillations To Probe Topological Brown-Zak Fermions In Graphene Moiré Systems
authors: Jinrui Zhong, Huimin Peng, Yuqing Hu, Qi Feng, Qiuli Li, Shihao Zhang, Qinsheng Wang, Jinhai Mao, Junxi Duan, And Yugui Yao
abstract:
Author(s): Jinrui Zhong, Huimin Peng, Yuqing Hu, Qi Feng, Qiuli Li, Shihao Zhang, Qinsheng Wang, Jinhai Mao, Junxi Duan, and Yugui Yao

A new experiment probes the quantum geometry of electronic wave functions involved in a nonlinear Hall response.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 246301] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental observation of nonlinear Hall quantum oscillations in graphene moiré systems, probing topological Brown-Zak fermions.
motivation: To investigate the quantum geometry of electronic wave functions in moiré systems through nonlinear Hall response.
method: Experimental measurement of nonlinear Hall effect in graphene moiré heterostructures under magnetic fields.
result: Observation of quantum oscillations in the nonlinear Hall signal, attributed to topological Brown-Zak fermions.
conclusion: The nonlinear Hall effect provides a probe of quantum geometry in moiré systems.

title: High-contrast Bragg Atom Interferometer For Testing Continuous Spontaneous Localization
authors: Huaiyu Zhu, Ju Liu, Tao Zhang, Qin Luo, Zhongkun Hu, And Minkang Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Huaiyu Zhu, Ju Liu, Tao Zhang, Qin Luo, Zhongkun Hu, and Minkang Zhou

The continuous spontaneous localization (CSL) model is one of the most promising approaches to address the wave-function collapse problem in the measurement process of standard quantum mechanics. In this work, the effect of the CSL model on a Bragg atom interferometer is investigated. A Bragg interf…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063317] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the effect of the continuous spontaneous localization (CSL) model on a Bragg atom interferometer, proposing a high-contrast setup to test wave-function collapse.
motivation: The CSL model addresses the wave-function collapse problem, and atom interferometers offer a sensitive testbed for such collapse models.
method: The authors analyze the impact of CSL on a Bragg atom interferometer, deriving the decoherence rate and optimizing parameters to maximize contrast.
result: They find that the CSL-induced decoherence can be detected with high-contrast interferometry under realistic conditions.
conclusion: The proposed Bragg atom interferometer can provide stringent bounds on CSL parameters, advancing tests of quantum collapse models.

title: Dual-state Control Of Lasing And Absorption Via Conjugate Exceptional Points
authors: Arnab Laha, Somnath Ghosh, Adam Miranowicz, And Lin Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Arnab Laha, Somnath Ghosh, Adam Miranowicz, and Lin Wu

The authors demonstrate a unified scattering framework for coordinated control of lasing and absorption based on a gain-loss-engineered Fabry–Pérot microcavity supporting a pair of conjugate exceptional points. Through tailored state switching enabled by non-Hermitian topology, the system exhibits a frequency-matched dual-state coexistence of amplification and absorption, opening new opportunities for multifunctional photonic devices.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063521] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a unified scattering framework for controlling lasing and absorption in a non-Hermitian photonic microcavity using conjugate exceptional points.
motivation: To achieve coordinated control of lasing and absorption in a single photonic device, enabling multifunctional applications.
method: The authors design a gain-loss-engineered Fabry–Pérot microcavity that supports a pair of conjugate exceptional points, and use non-Hermitian topology to switch between lasing and absorption states.
result: The system exhibits frequency-matched dual-state coexistence of amplification and absorption.
conclusion: This work opens new opportunities for multifunctional photonic devices by leveraging non-Hermitian physics.

title: Two Accelerated Mirrors In Opposite Rindler Wedges
authors: Muzzamal I. Shaukat, Anatoly A. Svidzinsky, And Marlan O. Scully
abstract:
Author(s): Muzzamal I. Shaukat, Anatoly A. Svidzinsky, and Marlan O. Scully

We investigate a quantum system consisting of two mirrors undergoing uniform acceleration in opposite directions and one or two stationary atoms localized in the right and left Rindler wedges, respectively. The system interacts with a scalar field described by plane-wave solutions in Rindler coordin…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062615] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies two uniformly accelerated mirrors and stationary atoms in Rindler wedges, focusing on the dynamics of a scalar field and atom-field interactions.
motivation: To understand quantum effects in non-inertial frames and the role of acceleration in atom-field interactions.
method: The system is modeled using plane-wave solutions in Rindler coordinates, and the dynamics are analyzed via the interaction of the scalar field with the mirrors and atoms.
result: The paper likely finds modifications to the field modes and atom excitation probabilities due to the accelerated mirrors.
conclusion: The work provides insights into quantum optics in accelerated frames but does not directly connect to the user's research directions.

title: Properties Of Bose-Einstein Condensates With Altermagnetism
authors: Jia Wang, Zhao Liu, Xia-Ji Liu, And Hui Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Jia Wang, Zhao Liu, Xia-Ji Liu, and Hui Hu

We investigate a weakly interacting two-component Bose-Einstein condensate in the miscible regime in the presence of altermagnetism, i.e., a collinear and globally compensated magnetic order that breaks spin-rotation symmetry while maintaining zero net magnetization. Within Bogoliubov theory, we der…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063316] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies Bose-Einstein condensates with altermagnetism using Bogoliubov theory.
motivation: To understand the properties of Bose-Einstein condensates in the presence of altermagnetic order, which breaks spin-rotation symmetry but has zero net magnetization.
method: Bogoliubov theory is applied to a weakly interacting two-component Bose-Einstein condensate in the miscible regime.
result: Derivation of excitation spectra and other properties of the condensate under altermagnetism.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical insights into altermagnetic Bose-Einstein condensates, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Exceptional Points In The Scattering Resonances Of A Sphere Dimer
authors: Emanuele Corsaro, Filippo Capolino, And Carlo Forestiere
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuele Corsaro, Filippo Capolino, and Carlo Forestiere

We investigate exceptional points of degeneracy (EPDs) in electromagnetic scattering of a sphere dimer from the electroquasistatic limit to the fully retarded regime. In the quasistatic limit, we prove that [MATH]-symmetric configurations, realized by spheres with complex-conjugate…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063520] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies exceptional points in electromagnetic scattering of a sphere dimer, focusing on quasistatic and retarded regimes.
motivation: Exceptional points in scattering systems have applications in sensing and wave control, but this work is purely in classical electromagnetism.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of scattering resonances in a dimer of spheres with complex-conjugate permittivities, using quasistatic approximation and full-wave simulations.
result: Demonstrates existence of exceptional points in the dimer system and characterizes their behavior across frequency regimes.
conclusion: The findings may be relevant for designing sensors or metamaterials, but no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is made.

title: Defect-mediated Melting Of Square-lattice Solids
authors: William Grampel And Daniel Podolsky
abstract:
Author(s): William Grampel and Daniel Podolsky

The melting of two-dimensional solids is driven by the proliferation of topological defects, a mechanism described by Kosterlitz-Thouless-Halperin-Nelson-Young (KTHNY) theory for isotropic lattices. Here, the authors extend this theory to square-lattice solids, where lattice anisotropy introduces an additional elastic constant and modifies the interactions between defects. The theory predicts two-step melting through an intermediate tetratic phase, but with key differences from the isotropic case: a modified bound on the translational exponent and nonuniversal Young’s modulus at the solid–tetratic transition.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214109] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Extends KTHNY theory of two-dimensional melting to square-lattice solids, predicting a two-step melting process via an intermediate tetratic phase with modified elastic properties.
motivation: Understanding melting in anisotropic lattices is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper focuses on classical defect-mediated phase transitions without quantum or information-theoretic aspects.
method: Theoretical analysis using elastic theory and defect interactions for square lattices, extending KTHNY theory to account for lattice anisotropy.
result: Predicts two-step melting with a tetratic phase, a modified bound on the translational exponent, and nonuniversal Young's modulus at the solid–tetratic transition.
conclusion: The theory provides a framework for melting in square-lattice solids, but the results are purely classical and not connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Intercalation-induced Near Room-temperature Ferromagnetism In ${\mathrm{CrI}}_{3}$ Via Synergistic Exchange Pathways
authors: Qing-Han Yang, Jia-Wen Li, Xin-Wei Yi, Xiang Li, Jing-Yang You, Gang Su, And Bo Gu

The development of room-temperature magnetic semiconductors is critical for advancing spintronic technologies, yet van der Waals magnets like [MATH] exhibit intrinsically low Curie temperatures ([MATH] K). This study employs first-principles calculations to demonstrate …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214442] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study predicts near room-temperature ferromagnetism in CrI3 via intercalation, focusing on magnetic properties rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To overcome the low Curie temperature of CrI3 for spintronic applications.
method: First-principles calculations to investigate intercalation-induced exchange pathways.
result: Intercalation enhances ferromagnetic coupling, raising Curie temperature to near room temperature.
conclusion: Intercalation is a viable strategy to achieve room-temperature ferromagnetism in van der Waals magnets.

title: Bi-isotropic Effects On Hybrid Surface Polaritons In Bilayer Configurations
authors: Ariel Nonato And Pedro D. S. Silva
abstract:
Author(s): Ariel Nonato and Pedro D. S. Silva

In this work, we investigate the bi-isotropic effects in the formation and tunability of hybrid surface polaritons in bilayer configurations. To do that, we consider a heterostructure constituted with layers formed by a TI medium endowed with bi-isotropic constitutive relations and an AFM medium. Us…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224434] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies bi-isotropic effects on hybrid surface polaritons in a bilayer of topological insulator and antiferromagnet, focusing on electromagnetic wave propagation.
motivation: To understand how bi-isotropic constitutive relations affect the formation and tunability of hybrid surface polaritons in layered structures.
method: Theoretical analysis using Maxwell's equations with bi-isotropic and antiferromagnetic media, solving for dispersion relations of surface polaritons.
result: Bi-isotropy introduces new tunability and hybridization effects in surface polariton modes.
conclusion: Bi-isotropic materials offer additional control over surface polaritons, relevant for photonic applications.

title: Quasiperiodic Skin Criticality In An Exactly Solvable non-Hermitian Quasicrystal
authors: Zhangyuan Chen, Muhammad Idrees, Ying Yang, Xianqi Tong, And Xiaosen Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhangyuan Chen, Muhammad Idrees, Ying Yang, Xianqi Tong, and Xiaosen Yang

Critical states in quasiperiodic systems defy the conventional dichotomy between extended and localized states. In this work, we demonstrate that non-Hermiticity fundamentally reshapes this paradigm by giving rise to a class of quasiperiodic skin criticality. We introduce a non-Hermitian quasiperiod…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235423] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies non-Hermitian quasiperiodic systems and discovers a new class of critical states called quasiperiodic skin criticality.
motivation: To understand how non-Hermiticity affects the nature of critical states in quasiperiodic systems, which are neither extended nor localized.
method: The authors introduce an exactly solvable non-Hermitian quasiperiodic model and analyze its spectral and wavefunction properties analytically and numerically.
result: They find that non-Hermiticity gives rise to quasiperiodic skin criticality, where all eigenstates become critical and exhibit skin effect.
conclusion: This work reveals a new paradigm of criticality in non-Hermitian quasicrystals, expanding the understanding of localization and critical phenomena.

title: Exceptional Horns In $n$-root Graphene And Lieb Photonic Ring Lattices
authors: A. M. Marques, D. Viedma, V. Ahufinger, And R. G. Dias
abstract:
Author(s): A. M. Marques, D. Viedma, V. Ahufinger, and R. G. Dias
