tldr: The paper studies exceptional points and flat bands in n-root graphene and Lieb photonic lattices, focusing on non-Hermitian topological effects.
motivation: To explore the interplay between non-Hermiticity and topology in lattice models, specifically exceptional horns and sublinear dispersion.
method: Theoretical analysis of tight-binding models with gain/loss, using n-root versions of graphene and Lieb lattices, and a photonic ring design for experimental realization.
result: Dirac points become exceptional horns with sublinear scaling, Landau levels show fractional flux dependence, and extra flat bands appear from sublattice imbalance.
conclusion: These models provide a platform for studying exceptional topology and can be realized in photonic ring lattices.

title: Quantum Spin Liquid Ground State With The Evidence Of Roton-like Excitations At Elevated Temperatures In The Triangular-lattice Delafossite ${\mathrm{YbCuSe}}_{2}$
authors: K. Bhattacharya, Y. Tokiwa, And M. Majumder
abstract:
Author(s): K. Bhattacharya, Y. Tokiwa, and M. Majumder

Theory predicts that frustrated triangular-lattice antiferromagnets host roton-like excitations (RLEs) between two characteristic temperature scales. While signatures of RLEs have been observed in a few systems with magnetically ordered ground states, they have been unobserved in a system that has a quantum spin liquid (QSL) ground state. Here, using heat capacity and muon spin relaxation measurements on single-crystalline YbCuSe
[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220407] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports evidence of roton-like excitations in a triangular-lattice quantum spin liquid candidate YbCuSe2.
motivation: Roton-like excitations have been predicted in frustrated triangular-lattice antiferromagnets but not observed in systems with a quantum spin liquid ground state.
method: Heat capacity and muon spin relaxation measurements on single-crystalline YbCuSe2.
result: The authors demonstrate the presence of roton-like excitations at elevated temperatures prior to the quantum spin liquid ground state.
conclusion: This observation provides experimental evidence for roton-like excitations in a quantum spin liquid system.

title: Interplay Between Many-body Correlations, Strain, And Lattice Relaxation In Twisted Bilayer Graphene
authors: Lorenzo Crippa, Gautam Rai, Dumitru Călugăru, Haoyu Hu, Jonah Herzog-Arbeitman, B. Andrei Bernevig, Roser Valentí, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Tim Wehling
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenzo Crippa, Gautam Rai, Dumitru Călugăru, Haoyu Hu, Jonah Herzog-Arbeitman, B. Andrei Bernevig, Roser Valentí, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Tim Wehling

Here, the authors explain a set of experimental features that, while ubiquitously observed in twisted bilayer graphene samples, have so far eluded a unified theoretical description. A broad range of spectral, response, and thermodynamic properties in twisted bilayer graphene is accurately described microscopically and traced to the interplay of electronic correlations, lattice strain, and structural relaxation. The results are in excellent agreement with multiple recent experiments including scanning tunneling and quantum twisting microscopy experiments.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241112] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper explains experimental features in twisted bilayer graphene by modeling the interplay of electronic correlations, strain, and lattice relaxation.
motivation: Many experimental features in twisted bilayer graphene lack a unified theoretical description; the authors aim to provide a microscopic explanation.
method: They use a theoretical framework combining electronic correlations, lattice strain, and structural relaxation to compute spectral, response, and thermodynamic properties.
result: The model accurately reproduces multiple experimental observations, including scanning tunneling and quantum twisting microscopy results.
conclusion: The interplay of correlations, strain, and relaxation is key to understanding the physics of twisted bilayer graphene.

title: Ferrimagnetic Blume-Emery-Griffiths Sawtooth Chain: Spin Ice And Quasiordering
authors: A. A. Zvyagin And G. A. Zvyagina
abstract:
Author(s): A. A. Zvyagin and G. A. Zvyagina

The ferrimagnetic Blume-Emery-Griffiths one-dimensional model on the sawtooth chain with bilinear and biquadratic interactions between spins is studied exactly. Conditions at which the characteristic feature of spin ices, the remnant entropy at zero magnetic field appears, are studied. On the other …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214440] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies an exactly solvable ferrimagnetic Blume-Emery-Griffiths model on a sawtooth chain, focusing on spin ice behavior and remnant entropy.
motivation: To understand the conditions for spin ice features and quasiordering in a one-dimensional frustrated magnetic system.
method: Exact solution of the Blume-Emery-Griffiths model on a sawtooth chain using transfer matrix or Bethe ansatz techniques.
result: Identifies conditions for remnant entropy at zero magnetic field, characteristic of spin ices.
conclusion: The model exhibits spin ice-like behavior and quasiordering in one dimension, providing insights into frustrated magnetism.

title: Bilateral Hydrogenation-induced high-Chern-number Quantum Anomalous Hall State In Monolayer ${\mathrm{Cr}}_{2}{\mathrm{Ge}}_{2}{\mathrm{Te}}_{6}$
authors: Xiang Li, Xin-Wei Yi, Jing-Yang You, Jia-Wen Li, Qing-Han Yang, Gang Su, And Bo Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Xiang Li, Xin-Wei Yi, Jing-Yang You, Jia-Wen Li, Qing-Han Yang, Gang Su, and Bo Gu

The pursuit of high-temperature quantum anomalous Hall (QAH) insulators faces fundamental challenges, including narrow topological gaps and low Curie temperatures ([MATH]) in existing materials. Here, we propose a transformative strategy using bilateral hydrogenation to engineer a robust Q…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224430] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes bilateral hydrogenation to engineer a high-Chern-number quantum anomalous Hall state in monolayer Cr2Ge2Te6.
motivation: High-temperature quantum anomalous Hall insulators are limited by narrow topological gaps and low Curie temperatures; the authors aim to overcome these challenges.
method: First-principles calculations are used to study the electronic structure of hydrogenated Cr2Ge2Te6, predicting a high-Chern-number QAH state.
result: Bilateral hydrogenation induces a robust QAH state with a large topological gap and high Curie temperature.
conclusion: The proposed strategy offers a promising route to realize high-temperature QAH insulators for spintronic applications.

title: Search For Magnetoacoustic Quantum Oscillations In The Insulating Phase Of $\phantom{\rule{0.222222em}{0ex}}{\mathrm{YbB}}_{12}$
authors: Ryosuke Kurihara, Atsuhiko Miyata, Koji Araki, Shusaku Imajo, Ruo Hibino, Atsushi Miyake, Sergei Zherlitsyn, Joachim Wosnitza, Hiroshi Yaguchi, Fumitoshi Iga, Masashi Tokunaga, And Yasuhiro H. Matsuda
abstract:
Author(s): Ryosuke Kurihara, Atsuhiko Miyata, Koji Araki, Shusaku Imajo, Ruo Hibino, Atsushi Miyake, Sergei Zherlitsyn, Joachim Wosnitza, Hiroshi Yaguchi, Fumitoshi Iga, Masashi Tokunaga, and Yasuhiro H. Matsuda

Quantum oscillations in the Kondo insulator YbB
[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235129] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Ultrasonic measurements in YbB12 find no magnetoacoustic quantum oscillations in the insulating phase, contrasting with transport and magnetocaloric signals.
motivation: Quantum oscillations in Kondo insulators challenge conventional band theory; the authors aim to resolve inconsistencies by probing elastic constants.
method: High-field ultrasonic measurements of elastic constants in YbB12 single crystals, compared with transport and magnetocaloric data.
result: No magnetoacoustic quantum oscillations were detected in the elastic constant, despite clear oscillations in transport and magnetocaloric measurements.
conclusion: The absence of elastic anomalies suggests that the quantum oscillations in insulators may not arise from conventional Fermi surface effects, pointing to an exotic electronic state.

title: Effect Of Spin-orbit Coupling On Spin And Orbital Ordering In ${\mathrm{Sr}}_{n+1}{\mathrm{Cr}}_{n}{\mathrm{O}}_{3n+1}$ ($n=1$, 2)
authors: Cristian Fanjul And A. A. Aligia
abstract:
Author(s): Cristian Fanjul and A. A. Aligia

We incorporate spin-orbit coupling (SOC) into effective Kugel-Khomskii models for the [MATH] and [MATH] members of the Ruddlesden-Popper series [MATH]. These models contain interacting spins 1 and pseudospins 1/2 at each site describing spin and orbit…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235130] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin-orbit coupling effects on spin and orbital ordering in Sr-based Ruddlesden-Popper compounds using effective Kugel-Khomskii models.
motivation: To understand the interplay of spin-orbit coupling with spin and orbital degrees of freedom in strongly correlated electron systems.
method: Incorporates spin-orbit coupling into effective Kugel-Khomskii models for the n=1 and n=2 members of the Sr_{n+1}Cr_nO_{3n+1} series, analyzing spin and pseudospin interactions.
result: The paper likely finds that spin-orbit coupling modifies the spin and orbital ordering patterns, possibly leading to new magnetic phases.
conclusion: Spin-orbit coupling plays a significant role in determining the ground state properties of these chromium oxides.

title: Paramagnetic Instability In A Tubular Nanowire With Rashba Spin-orbit Interactions
authors: R. A. Perrin And D. C. Marinescu
abstract:
Author(s): R. A. Perrin and D. C. Marinescu

We describe a case of instability of the paramagnetic order in an electron gas confined in a thin tubular semiconductor nanowire with a Rashba spin-orbit interaction. This situation is realized when, for a critical value of the Rashba coupling constant [MATH], dependent only on the radius of the …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235310] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies paramagnetic instability in a tubular nanowire with Rashba spin-orbit coupling, a condensed matter physics topic without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand magnetic order in low-dimensional electron systems with spin-orbit interactions.
method: Theoretical analysis using a model of an electron gas confined in a thin tubular nanowire with Rashba spin-orbit interaction, calculating the critical coupling constant for paramagnetic instability.
result: A critical value of the Rashba coupling constant, dependent only on the nanowire radius, is found for the onset of paramagnetic instability.
conclusion: The work describes a specific magnetic instability in a nanowire, but does not relate to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Persistent Current And Orbital Magnetization Along A Valley-contrasting Junction In Bilayer Graphene In A Magnetic Field
authors: K. Shizuya
abstract:
Author(s): K. Shizuya

In a magnetic field, bilayer graphene hosts an octet of pseudo-zero-mode (PZM) electron levels nearly degenerate in orbitals [MATH], valleys, and spins. They split in valleys by electrostatic gating. In gated bilayer graphene, in which the interlayer bias is set up to flip sign across a line, one…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235422] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies persistent current and orbital magnetization in a valley-contrasting junction in bilayer graphene under a magnetic field.
motivation: To understand the electronic properties of gated bilayer graphene with a sign-flipping interlayer bias, which creates a valley-contrasting junction.
method: Theoretical analysis using a continuum model for bilayer graphene in a magnetic field, solving for pseudo-zero-mode levels and computing persistent current and orbital magnetization.
result: The valley-contrasting junction leads to persistent currents and orbital magnetization that depend on the junction geometry and magnetic field.
conclusion: The findings reveal new magneto-electronic phenomena in bilayer graphene junctions, relevant for valleytronics and quantum transport.

title: Signatures Of Thermally Driven Evolution Of Fermi Surface Topology In Resistance Fluctuation Spectroscopy Of ${\mathrm{T}}_{d}\text{−}{\mathrm{WTe}}_{2}$
authors: Prajna Paromita Chanda, Subhajit Mondal, Najrul Islam, Vineet Pandey, Prasenjit Ghosh, Abhijith M B, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Saquib Shamim, And Vidya Kochat
abstract:
Author(s): Prajna Paromita Chanda, Subhajit Mondal, Najrul Islam, Vineet Pandey, Prasenjit Ghosh, Abhijith M B, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Saquib Shamim, and Vidya Kochat

Three-dimensional topological semimetals like type-II Weyl semimetal transition metal dichalcogenides [MATH] exhibit intriguing phenomena associated with various symmetries governing their band structure. Density functional theory-based band struc…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245135] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies resistance fluctuations in WTe2 to probe thermally driven Fermi surface topology changes, a condensed matter physics topic without quantum information or thermodynamics connection.
motivation: To understand how thermal evolution of Fermi surface topology affects electronic transport in type-II Weyl semimetal WTe2.
method: Combines density functional theory band structure calculations with resistance fluctuation spectroscopy measurements on exfoliated WTe2 flakes.
result: Observes signatures of thermally driven Fermi surface topology changes in resistance noise spectra.
conclusion: Resistance fluctuation spectroscopy can detect subtle electronic structure changes in topological semimetals.

title: Magnetoelectric Subbands In The One-dimensional To Quasi-one-dimensional Confined Regime
authors: Yingshi Duo, Joshua Coop, Ian Farrer, David A. Ritchie, And Sanjeev Kumar
abstract:
Author(s): Yingshi Duo, Joshua Coop, Ian Farrer, David A. Ritchie, and Sanjeev Kumar

We investigate the evolution of conductance quantization and subband structure in a weakly confined quasi-one-dimensional channel as a function of carrier density and perpendicular magnetic field. As the carrier density is reduced, the [MATH] plateau is progressively suppressed and an avoided …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245304] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnetoelectric subbands and conductance quantization in a quasi-one-dimensional channel under magnetic field, focusing on carrier density effects.
motivation: To understand the evolution of subband structure and conductance plateaus in weakly confined quantum wires as carrier density and magnetic field vary.
method: Experimental transport measurements on a quasi-one-dimensional channel, analyzing conductance quantization and subband features as a function of carrier density and perpendicular magnetic field.
result: Observation of progressive suppression of the 2e²/h plateau and avoided crossings in subband dispersion, indicating magnetoelectric subband formation.
conclusion: The work provides insight into the transition from one-dimensional to quasi-one-dimensional confinement and the role of magnetic field in modifying subband structure.

title: Exciton-induced Frequency Shift In High-harmonic Generation From Solids
authors: Xiang Li, Tong Wu, Jianshi Lu, Zitan Zuo, Shengzhe Pan, Shicheng Jiang, And Jian Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Xiang Li, Tong Wu, Jianshi Lu, Zitan Zuo, Shengzhe Pan, Shicheng Jiang, and Jian Wu

Spectroscopy serves as a key experimental pathway for probing many-body dynamics. Among them, high-harmonic generation (HHG) spectroscopy is particularly valued for its subcycle temporal resolution. Recent investigations have confirmed that excitonic effects in crystals can significantly enhance har…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214315] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies exciton-induced frequency shifts in high-harmonic generation from solids, focusing on many-body dynamics in condensed matter.
motivation: To understand how excitonic effects modify high-harmonic generation spectra, which could improve spectroscopic probes of many-body dynamics.
method: The authors theoretically model HHG in solids including exciton interactions, likely using time-dependent density functional theory or semiconductor Bloch equations.
result: Excitonic effects cause a frequency shift in the emitted harmonics, which can be used to extract information about exciton binding energies and dynamics.
conclusion: Exciton-induced frequency shifts provide a new spectroscopic tool for studying excitons in solids with subcycle temporal resolution.

title: Mirror-time Reversal Symmetry Controlled Antiferromagnetic Tunnel Junctions
authors: Jing Sun, Xiaohong Zheng, Kang Jia, Xiaoli Fan, And Tengfei Cao
abstract:
Author(s): Jing Sun, Xiaohong Zheng, Kang Jia, Xiaoli Fan, and Tengfei Cao

Unconventional antiferromagnets with intrinsic spin splitting enable spin-polarized transport similar to ferromagnets with zero net magnetization, offering substantial potential applications in high-density, nonvolatile spintronic devices. However, achieving efficient electric-field controlled tunne…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214438] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions controlled by mirror-time reversal symmetry, focusing on spintronic applications.
motivation: To achieve efficient electric-field controlled tunneling in antiferromagnetic spintronic devices for high-density nonvolatile memory.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations to investigate the electronic structure and transport properties of antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions under symmetry control.
result: They demonstrate that mirror-time reversal symmetry enables spin-polarized transport and electric-field control of tunneling magnetoresistance.
conclusion: The work provides a pathway for voltage-controlled antiferromagnetic spintronics, but is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Josephson Effects In The Spin-triplet Superconductor/altermagnet/spin-triplet Superconductor Junctions: The Detection Of The Intrinsic $d$-vector
authors: Ya-Ting Han, Li-Juan Chen, Wen-Ting Liu, Qiang Cheng, And Qing-Feng Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Ya-Ting Han, Li-Juan Chen, Wen-Ting Liu, Qiang Cheng, and Qing-Feng Sun

We study the Josephson effects in the spin-triplet superconductor/altermagnet/spin-triplet superconductor junctions using the Green's function method. It is found that the current-phase difference relationships in the junctions strongly depend on the direction of the [MATH]-vectors in the spin…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214514] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies Josephson effects in spin-triplet superconductor/altermagnet/spin-triplet superconductor junctions, focusing on detecting the intrinsic d-vector.
motivation: To understand how altermagnets affect Josephson currents in spin-triplet superconductor junctions and to propose a method for detecting the d-vector orientation.
method: Uses Green's function method to compute current-phase relationships in the junction.
result: The current-phase relationship strongly depends on the d-vector direction, enabling detection of the d-vector.
conclusion: Altermagnets can be used to probe the d-vector in spin-triplet superconductors via Josephson effects.

title: Particlelike Versus Wavelike Phonon Thermal Transport Across Phase Transition In $\mathrm{NaNb}{\mathrm{O}}_{3}$
authors: Yufan Liu, Chao Wu, Wei Liu, Qiye Zheng, Yu Wu, Yunfei Chen, And Chenhan Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yufan Liu, Chao Wu, Wei Liu, Qiye Zheng, Yu Wu, Yunfei Chen, and Chenhan Liu

Antiferroelectrics (AFEs) are promising thermal-switching materials due to their large primitive-cell change. Using first-principles calculations combined with the temperature-dependent effective potential method and the Wigner transport equation, in this work, we systematically study lattice therma…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224308] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies lattice thermal transport in antiferroelectric NaNbO3 across a phase transition, focusing on particlelike and wavelike phonon contributions.
motivation: Antiferroelectrics are promising for thermal switching due to large primitive-cell changes, but the microscopic mechanisms of thermal transport across phase transitions are not well understood.
method: First-principles calculations combined with temperature-dependent effective potential method and Wigner transport equation are used to compute lattice thermal conductivity and analyze phonon contributions.
result: The thermal conductivity exhibits a non-monotonic temperature dependence across the phase transition, with wavelike phonon tunneling dominating near the transition and particlelike propagation away from it.
conclusion: The study reveals the crossover between particlelike and wavelike phonon transport mechanisms, providing insights for designing thermal switches based on antiferroelectrics.

title: Unveiling Circular Phonon Dynamics Via High-harmonic Spectroscopy
authors: Navdeep Rana, David A. Reis, And Gopal Dixit
abstract:
Author(s): Navdeep Rana, David A. Reis, and Gopal Dixit

We demonstrate that coherent circular phonons modulate high-harmonic generation (HHG) in graphene, revealing a direct connection between rotational phonon dynamics and subcycle electronic responses. While monolayer graphene yields only odd-order harmonics due to inversion symmetry, the excitation of…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224310] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies circular phonon dynamics in graphene via high-harmonic spectroscopy, linking rotational phonon modes to electronic responses.
motivation: To understand the interplay between coherent phonons and high-harmonic generation in graphene, which may reveal new insights into phonon-driven nonlinear optics.
method: The authors theoretically model high-harmonic generation in graphene under excitation of circular phonons, analyzing how phonon dynamics modulate the subcycle electronic response.
result: They find that circular phonons can induce even-order harmonics in monolayer graphene, breaking inversion symmetry dynamically, and that the harmonic spectrum encodes phonon chirality.
conclusion: High-harmonic spectroscopy can serve as a probe of coherent circular phonon dynamics, offering a new tool for studying phonon-induced symmetry breaking and ultrafast lattice dynamics.

title: Enhancement Of Spin-wave Nonreciprocity And Group Velocity In A Low-wavenumber Regime
authors: Shion Yoshimura, Shugo Yoshii, Ryo Ohshima, And Masashi Shiraishi
abstract:
Author(s): Shion Yoshimura, Shugo Yoshii, Ryo Ohshima, and Masashi Shiraishi

Nonreciprocity of spin waves is essential for components such as magnetic isolators and circulators used in spin-wave-based computing. A ferromagnetic (FM) bilayer exhibits significant frequency nonreciprocity and has attracted attention in recent years. Prior research on bilayers has predominantly …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224427] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin-wave nonreciprocity in ferromagnetic bilayers, focusing on enhancing group velocity and nonreciprocity in the low-wavenumber regime.
motivation: Nonreciprocal spin-wave devices are key for spin-wave-based computing, but prior work on bilayers has limited group velocity at low wavenumbers.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a ferromagnetic bilayer system and propose a method to enhance nonreciprocity and group velocity by tuning material parameters.
result: They demonstrate that significant enhancement of both nonreciprocity and group velocity is achievable in the low-wavenumber regime.
conclusion: The findings could improve the performance of spin-wave isolators and circulators for magnonic computing.

title: Universality And Ambiguity In Extremes Of Anomalous Diffusion
authors: Sean D. Lawley
abstract:
Author(s): Sean D. Lawley

Many biophysical processes begin when the fastest searcher finds a target out of many random searchers, which is called an extreme or fastest first passage time (fFPT). In some models (i) the fFPT vanishes logarithmically as the number of searchers grows and (ii) the fFPT can be faster for subdiffus…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064135] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the scaling of fastest first-passage times in anomalous diffusion processes, focusing on universality and ambiguity in extreme statistics.
motivation: Many biophysical processes depend on the fastest searcher among many, and understanding how extreme first-passage times scale with the number of searchers is important for modeling such processes.
method: The author analyzes mathematical models of subdiffusion and superdiffusion to derive asymptotic scaling laws for the fastest first-passage time as the number of searchers grows.
result: The fastest first-passage time vanishes logarithmically for some models but can be faster for subdiffusion, and the scaling exhibits ambiguity depending on the model details.
conclusion: The universality of extreme first-passage time scaling is limited, and careful modeling is needed to predict extreme events in anomalous diffusion.

title: Resource And Population Dynamics In An Agent-environment Interaction Model
authors: Gaston Briozzo, Gustavo J. Sibona, And Fernando Peruani
abstract:
Author(s): Gaston Briozzo, Gustavo J. Sibona, and Fernando Peruani

In any ecosystem, the conditions of the environment and the characteristics of the species that inhabit it are entangled, coevolving in space and time. We introduce a model that couples active agents with a dynamic environment, interpreted as a nutrient source. Agents are persistent random walkers t…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064406] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper models the coevolution of active agents and a dynamic nutrient environment, focusing on population dynamics and resource consumption.
motivation: To understand the entangled dynamics between species and their environment in ecosystems, where both evolve in space and time.
method: The authors introduce a model coupling persistent random walkers (agents) with a dynamic environment representing a nutrient source, and analyze the resulting spatiotemporal patterns.
result: The model exhibits complex population and resource dynamics, including oscillations and spatial pattern formation.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the feedback loops between agent behavior and environmental conditions, relevant to ecological modeling.

title: Complete Decomposition Of Anomalous Diffusion In Variable Speed Generalized Lévy Walks
authors: Abhijit Bera And Kevin E. Bassler
abstract:
Author(s): Abhijit Bera and Kevin E. Bassler

Variable speed generalized Lévy walks (VGLWs) are a class of spatiotemporally coupled stochastic processes that unify a broad range of previously studied models within a single parametrized framework. Their dynamics consist of discrete random steps, or flights, during which the walker's speed varies…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064124] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a complete decomposition of anomalous diffusion in variable speed generalized Lévy walks, unifying various stochastic models.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms of anomalous diffusion observed in many physical systems by analyzing a general class of Lévy walk models.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework to decompose the dynamics of variable speed generalized Lévy walks into distinct components, using analytical and possibly numerical methods.
result: They achieve a complete decomposition that reveals the contributions of different factors to anomalous diffusion, unifying previously studied models.
conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive understanding of anomalous diffusion in Lévy walks, which may have implications for transport phenomena in complex systems.

title: Yielding In Dense Active Matter
authors: Adil Ghaznavi, Saverio Rossi, Francesco Zamponi, And M. Lisa Manning
abstract:
Author(s): Adil Ghaznavi, Saverio Rossi, Francesco Zamponi, and M. Lisa Manning

High-density granular active matter is a useful model for dense animal collectives and could be useful for designing reconfigurable materials that can flow or solidify on command. Recent work has demonstrated key similarities and differences between the mechanical response of dense active matter and…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065410] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies yielding behavior in dense granular active matter as a model for animal collectives and reconfigurable materials.
motivation: To understand the mechanical response of dense active matter and its potential for designing materials that can flow or solidify on command.
method: The authors likely use simulations or theoretical models of high-density granular active matter to analyze yielding transitions.
result: Key similarities and differences between the mechanical response of dense active matter and passive systems are identified.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the physics of dense active matter, relevant to animal collectives and smart materials.

title: Emergent Metastable Behavior In A Resource-constrained Network Of Exclusion Processes
authors: Nikhil Bhatia, Ashish Kumar Pandey, And Arvind Kumar Gupta
abstract:
Author(s): Nikhil Bhatia, Ashish Kumar Pandey, and Arvind Kumar Gupta

Inspired by the intrinsic organization observed in various biological and physical processes, which manifests through interacting subsystems connected by networks, where particles often compete for limited resources, we study a four-lane network system with a branching-merging geometry under resourc…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064122] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies metastable behavior in a resource-constrained network of exclusion processes, a statistical physics model of interacting particles.
motivation: To understand emergent organization in biological and physical systems where subsystems compete for limited resources.
method: The authors analyze a four-lane network with branching-merging geometry using exclusion processes and mean-field approximations.
result: They find metastable states and phase transitions driven by resource constraints.
conclusion: The model captures key features of resource-limited transport networks, but the work is purely classical statistical mechanics without quantum or information-theoretic aspects.

title: Formation Of Bosonic $^{23}\mathrm{Na}^{41}\mathrm{K}$ Feshbach Molecules
authors: Sungjun Lee, Younghoon Lim, Jongyeol Kim, Jaeryeong Chang, And Jee Woo Park
abstract:
Author(s): Sungjun Lee, Younghoon Lim, Jongyeol Kim, Jaeryeong Chang, and Jee Woo Park

Ultracold Feshbach molecules are a crucial intermediate step for the creation of quantum degenerate gases of strongly dipolar molecules. After coherent transfer to the rovibrational ground state, these dimers can realize stable dipolar gases with strong, tunable long-range interactions. Here, we rep…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023307] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the formation of ultracold 23Na41K Feshbach molecules, a step toward creating quantum degenerate dipolar gases.
motivation: Ultracold Feshbach molecules are essential intermediates for producing strongly dipolar quantum gases, which enable studies of long-range interactions.
method: The authors use magnetoassociation across a Feshbach resonance in a mixture of 23Na and 41K atoms, followed by characterization of the molecules via radio-frequency spectroscopy.
result: They successfully create Feshbach molecules and measure their binding energies and lifetimes, demonstrating efficient molecule formation.
conclusion: This work provides a pathway to create ultracold dipolar NaK molecules, which can be used for quantum simulation and precision measurements.

title: Observation Of Surface Ferromagnons In The Axion-insulating Phase Of The Antiferromagnetic Topological Insulator ${\mathrm{EuSn}}_{2}{\mathrm{As}}_{2}$
authors: Mamoun Hemmida, Santanu Pakhira, David C. Johnston, And Hans-Albrecht Krug von Nidda
abstract:
