We report the study of spin dynamics of [MATH] in the antiferromagnetic axion topological insulator [MATH] by means of antiferromagnetic resonance at 9.34 GHz. Below the Néel temperature ([MATH]), two types of resonance modes, the conventiona…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023309] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin dynamics in an antiferromagnetic topological insulator using antiferromagnetic resonance, focusing on surface magnon modes in the axion-insulating phase.
motivation: To understand the spin dynamics and magnon modes in the antiferromagnetic topological insulator EuSn2As2, particularly in its axion-insulating phase.
method: Antiferromagnetic resonance measurements at 9.34 GHz were performed on single crystals of EuSn2As2 below the Néel temperature.
result: Two types of resonance modes were observed: conventional antiferromagnetic resonance and surface ferromagnon modes, indicating surface spin excitations.
conclusion: The observation of surface ferromagnons provides insight into the magnetic properties of topological insulators and their axion-insulating phase.

title: Macroscopic Localization And Collective Memory In Poisson Renewal Resetting
authors: Ohad Vilk
abstract:
Author(s): Ohad Vilk

Stochastic renewal processes are ubiquitous across physics, biology, and the social sciences. Here, we show that continuous-time renewal dynamics can naturally produce a mixed discrete-continuous structure, with a macroscopic fraction of particles occupying a discrete state. For ensembles of continu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023305] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies macroscopic localization and collective memory in Poisson renewal resetting processes, a stochastic dynamics model.
motivation: To understand how renewal processes can produce a mixed discrete-continuous structure with macroscopic occupation of a discrete state.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of continuous-time renewal dynamics with resetting.
result: Discovery of a macroscopic localization phenomenon and collective memory effects in the ensemble.
conclusion: Renewal resetting can lead to emergent collective behavior and memory, relevant to statistical physics.

title: Manifold-based Transformation Of Probability Distributions: Application To The Inverse Problem Of Reconstructing Distributions From Experimental Data
authors: Tomotaka Oroguchi, Rintaro Inoue, And Masaaki Sugiyama
abstract:
Author(s): Tomotaka Oroguchi, Rintaro Inoue, and Masaaki Sugiyama

Information geometry is a mathematical framework that elucidates the manifold structure of the probability distribution space (p space), providing a systematic approach to transforming probability distributions (PDs). In this study, we utilized information geometry to address the inverse problems as…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023291] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses information geometry to transform probability distributions for solving inverse problems in experimental data reconstruction.
motivation: The authors aim to address the inverse problem of reconstructing probability distributions from experimental data, which is common in fields like structural biology.
method: They apply information geometry, specifically the manifold structure of probability distribution spaces, to systematically transform distributions and solve the inverse problem.
result: The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of the manifold-based transformation approach for reconstructing distributions from limited or noisy experimental data.
conclusion: Information geometry provides a powerful framework for inverse problems involving probability distributions, with potential applications in various experimental sciences.

title: Dynamical Phase Transitions Across Slow And Fast Regimes In A Two-tone Driven Duffing Resonator
authors: Soumya S. Kumar, Javier Del Pino, Letizia Catalini, Alexander Eichler, And Oded Zilberberg
abstract:
Author(s): Soumya S. Kumar, Javier del Pino, Letizia Catalini, Alexander Eichler, and Oded Zilberberg

The dynamical phase transitions of a Duffing resonator subjected to a bichromatic drive across the slow- and fast-beating regimes are mapped. An analytical threshold to observe these transitions based on an effective nonlinear response theory is provided, explaining the mechanism behind these processes. Complementary analytical treatments for the slow and fast regimes are supplied.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023298] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical phase transitions in a driven Duffing resonator, focusing on classical nonlinear dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the transition between slow and fast beating regimes in a nonlinear resonator under bichromatic drive.
method: Analytical effective nonlinear response theory combined with complementary treatments for slow and fast regimes.
result: An analytical threshold for dynamical phase transitions is derived and mapped across the two regimes.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for predicting and explaining dynamical phase transitions in driven nonlinear resonators.

title: Complete Inelastic Transparency Of Time-modulated Resonant Photonic Circuits
authors: M. Sumetsky
abstract:
Author(s): M. Sumetsky

Photonic circuits modulated in time can convert the input light frequency [MATH], shifting it by multiples of the modulation frequency [MATH] and, in certain cases, amplify the total input light power. Of special interest are photonic circuits employing microwave capacitors, which instantaneou…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023299] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies time-modulated resonant photonic circuits that achieve complete inelastic transparency, enabling frequency conversion and amplification.
motivation: To understand and exploit the effects of time modulation in photonic circuits for frequency conversion and power amplification.
method: The author theoretically analyzes a resonant photonic circuit with time-varying parameters, deriving conditions for complete inelastic transparency where input light is fully converted to a different frequency.
result: Complete inelastic transparency is achieved under specific modulation conditions, allowing efficient frequency conversion and amplification.
conclusion: Time-modulated photonic circuits can serve as efficient frequency converters and amplifiers, with potential applications in classical and quantum photonics.

title: General Spin Models From Noncollinear Spin Density Functional Theory And Spin-cluster Expansion
authors: Tomonori Tanaka And Yoshihiro Gohda
abstract:
Author(s): Tomonori Tanaka and Yoshihiro Gohda

We present a data-efficient framework for constructing general classical spin Hamiltonians by combining the spin-cluster expansion (SCE) with fully self-consistent noncollinear spin density functional theory (DFT). The key idea is to fit the SCE model to magnetic torques rather than to total energie…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023300] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A data-efficient framework combining spin-cluster expansion with noncollinear spin DFT to construct classical spin Hamiltonians from magnetic torques.
motivation: To efficiently derive accurate spin models for complex magnetic materials without relying on total energy calculations.
method: Uses spin-cluster expansion fitted to magnetic torques computed from self-consistent noncollinear spin DFT.
result: Demonstrates that fitting to torques yields accurate spin Hamiltonians with fewer DFT calculations than energy-based methods.
conclusion: The torque-based SCE approach is a practical and efficient tool for constructing spin models for large-scale magnetic simulations.

title: Visualizing Phonon Edge States On Molybdenum Disulfide
authors: Patrick Giese, Mathias Stokkebye Nissen, Stig Helveg, And Jakob Schiøtz
abstract:
Author(s): Patrick Giese, Mathias Stokkebye Nissen, Stig Helveg, and Jakob Schiøtz

Enhanced atomic vibrations have previously been observed near edges of two-dimensional materials with high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM). Here this observation is accounted for by localized phonon edge modes by including correlated atom vibrations in HR-TEM image simulations.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022049] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses HR-TEM image simulations to show that enhanced atomic vibrations near edges of MoS2 are due to localized phonon edge modes.
motivation: Enhanced atomic vibrations observed near edges of 2D materials in HR-TEM were not well understood; the authors aimed to explain this phenomenon.
method: The authors performed HR-TEM image simulations that included correlated atom vibrations to model the observed contrast.
result: The simulations reproduced the enhanced vibrations, attributing them to localized phonon edge modes.
conclusion: Localized phonon edge modes account for the enhanced atomic vibrations seen at edges of MoS2 in HR-TEM.

title: Emergent Self-attention From Astrocyte-gated Associative Memory Dynamics
authors: Arnau Vivet And Alex Arenas
abstract:
Author(s): Arnau Vivet and Alex Arenas

We introduce a Hopfield-type associative memory in which effective connectivity is multiplicatively modulated by astrocytic gains evolving under an entropy-regularized replicator equation. The coupled neuron-astrocyte dynamics admit a Lyapunov function, ensuring global convergence. At fixed points, …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023276] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A Hopfield-type associative memory model with astrocyte-gated multiplicative modulation and entropy-regularized replicator dynamics, showing global convergence and emergent self-attention.
motivation: To incorporate astrocytic modulation into neural network models to achieve more biologically plausible associative memory and attention mechanisms.
method: The authors introduce a coupled neuron-astrocyte system where astrocytic gains evolve via an entropy-regularized replicator equation, and prove global convergence using a Lyapunov function.
result: The model exhibits emergent self-attention-like behavior at fixed points, with astrocytic gains modulating effective connectivity.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework linking astrocyte dynamics to attention mechanisms in neural networks, but is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Tensor Network Approach To Momentum-resolved Spectroscopy In Nonperiodic Super-moiré Systems
authors: Anouar Moustaj, Yitao Sun, Tiago V. C. Antão, And Jose L. Lado
abstract:
Author(s): Anouar Moustaj, Yitao Sun, Tiago V. C. Antão, and Jose L. Lado

Computing spectral functions in large, nonperiodic super-moiré systems remains an open problem due to the exceptionally large system size that must be considered. Here, we establish a tensor network methodology that allows computing momentum-resolved spectral functions of noninteracting and interact…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023282] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A tensor network method for computing momentum-resolved spectral functions in large nonperiodic super-moiré systems.
motivation: Computing spectral functions in large nonperiodic super-moiré systems is challenging due to the huge system sizes required.
method: The authors develop a tensor network approach that efficiently computes momentum-resolved spectral functions for noninteracting and interacting systems.
result: The method enables spectral calculations in systems with millions of atoms, demonstrated on twisted trilayer graphene and other moiré systems.
conclusion: Tensor networks provide a scalable tool for studying electronic structure in complex moiré materials.

title: Observation Of An Amplitudelike Mode In The Excitonic Insulator ${\mathrm{Ta}}_{2}{\mathrm{Pd}}_{3}{\mathrm{Te}}_{5}$
authors: Y.-S. Choi, Dirk Wulferding, Raju Kalaivanan, Rajesh Kumar Ulaganathan, Raman Sankar, And Kwang-Yong Choi
abstract:
Author(s): Y.-S. Choi, Dirk Wulferding, Raju Kalaivanan, Rajesh Kumar Ulaganathan, Raman Sankar, and Kwang-Yong Choi

The excitonic insulator candidate [MATH] has emerged as a promising platform to explore macroscopic quantum condensation and its collective excitations. Using polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy, we identify a symmetry-selective electronic mode tha…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023273] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Observation of an amplitudelike mode in the excitonic insulator Ta2Pd3Te5 using Raman spectroscopy.
motivation: Excitonic insulators are a platform for macroscopic quantum condensation, and understanding their collective excitations is important for condensed matter physics.
method: Polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy was used to identify a symmetry-selective electronic mode.
result: A symmetry-selective electronic mode was observed, interpreted as an amplitudelike mode of the excitonic condensate.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into collective excitations in excitonic insulators, but the paper is focused on condensed matter physics without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Frenkel Line And The Pseudogap: An Analogy Between Classical And Electronic Fluids
authors: J. Fournier, P.-O. Downey, O. Gingras, C.-D. Hébert, M. Charlebois, And A.-M. S. Tremblay
abstract:
Author(s): J. Fournier, P.-O. Downey, O. Gingras, C.-D. Hébert, M. Charlebois, and A.-M. S. Tremblay

Asymptotically close to critical end points of first-order transitions, maxima in thermodynamic quantities occur along a line called the Widom line, a concept first introduced in classical fluids. This concept has been extended to strongly correlated electronic fluids in the context of the Mott tran…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023278] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper draws an analogy between the Frenkel line in classical fluids and the pseudogap in strongly correlated electronic fluids, focusing on thermodynamic response functions near critical endpoints.
motivation: To extend the concept of the Widom line from classical fluids to electronic systems, specifically the Mott transition, and to explore the analogy between the Frenkel line and the pseudogap.
method: The authors analyze thermodynamic quantities and response functions near critical endpoints in both classical and electronic fluids, using theoretical models and possibly numerical simulations.
result: They identify a line analogous to the Frenkel line in the electronic system, associated with the pseudogap phase, and show similarities in the behavior of thermodynamic maxima.
conclusion: The analogy provides a unified perspective on critical phenomena in classical and quantum fluids, but the work is primarily focused on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:
Author(s): Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, and Cristian D. Batista

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains, showing they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and are detectable via neutron scattering.
motivation: To understand the quantum dynamics of chiral solitons in spin chains, which are topological excitations with potential relevance to low-dimensional magnetism.
method: A nonperturbative quantization approach is applied to chiral solitons in a spin chain model, analyzing their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid.
result: Chiral solitons appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and can be observed via inelastic neutron scattering.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for chiral soliton dynamics and suggests experimental detection methods.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To develop a non-perturbative method for studying strongly coupled conformal field theories using the fuzzy sphere as a regularization scheme.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative geometry, to discretize the sphere and simulate fermionic CFTs numerically, analyzing spectra and operator dimensions.
result: They find evidence for emergent supersymmetry in the interacting theory and compute scaling dimensions of primary operators.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere provides a viable numerical approach to study 3D fermionic CFTs, revealing emergent supersymmetry and enabling future studies of strongly coupled fixed points.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky
abstract:
Author(s): Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. DeBeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, and Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures, demonstrating three distinct magnetic phases in EuAg4Sb2 and establishing a design framework for spin-based vortex lattices.
motivation: To understand and control complex spin textures in moiré superlattices, which are of interest for information manipulation via spin-based vortex lattices.
method: The authors combine neutron scattering, magnetization measurements, and theoretical modeling to map the magnetic phase diagram of EuAg4Sb2 and identify three tunable magnetic phases.
result: Three distinct, tunable magnetic phases are revealed, providing a design framework for materials that manipulate information via spin-based vortex lattices.
conclusion: The work establishes a general approach to engineering spin moiré superstructures, with potential applications in spintronics and information storage.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, and Alexander Mook

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Theoretical study of topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature.
motivation: To understand the stability of topological magnon gaps at finite temperatures for spintronic applications.
method: Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions using many-body perturbation theory or similar techniques.
result: Topological magnon gaps remain stable near the Curie point.
conclusion: Provides a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices based on topological magnons.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: Understanding causal relationships in complex networks is crucial for predicting system behavior, but existing methods often lack a physical basis.
method: The authors develop a framework that incorporates physical principles to infer causal links from time-series data of network dynamics.
result: The framework accurately predicts physical links across various networked dynamical systems, outperforming standard causal inference methods.
conclusion: Physics-informed causal inference provides a powerful tool for network analysis, with potential applications in diverse fields.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, and Ashvin Vishwanath

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies anyon superfluidity of excitons in quantum Hall bilayers, focusing on topological criticality and exotic collective states.
motivation: To understand and engineer exotic quantum states in fractional quantum Hall systems, specifically anyonic exciton superfluids.
method: Theoretical analysis using topological field theory and mean-field approaches for quantum Hall bilayers.
result: Topological criticality enables the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids with robust properties.
conclusion: Quantum Hall bilayers provide a platform for realizing anyonic superfluidity, which may lead to new collective quantum phenomena.

title: Three-Dimensional Xy Universality And Nonlinear Magnetic Susceptibility In A Kagome Ice Compound
authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart
abstract:
Author(s): Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, and Philipp Gegenwart

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in a kagome spin ice compound, revealing hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.
motivation: To investigate the ground state properties and phase transitions in frustrated magnetic systems, specifically kagome spin ice HoAgGe.
method: Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements combined with neutron scattering and other techniques to probe symmetry breaking and critical behavior.
result: Observation of hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground state, with the transition belonging to the three-dimensional XY universality class.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the exotic magnetic phases of kagome spin ice and the nature of the phase transition.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the discovery of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature, characterized by angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Flat bands in strongly correlated materials can host exotic quantum phases, but many are only stable at low temperatures. The authors aim to find a room-temperature platform for studying such phenomena.
method: The authors synthesize layered transition-metal oxyhalides and use angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) to map the electronic band structure, revealing flat bands that are stable at room temperature.
result: They observe intrinsic flat bands that remain robust at room temperature, with orbital selectivity, providing a tunable platform for strongly correlated electron states.
conclusion: These materials offer a promising system for investigating flat-band physics and potentially correlated phases at accessible temperatures.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi
abstract:
Author(s): Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, and Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021037] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses magneto-optical spectroscopy to probe quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, demonstrating electric-field control of magnetic order.
motivation: To investigate the quantum anomalous Hall phase in twisted bilayer WSe2 and understand the interplay between topology and magnetism in moiré materials.
method: Magneto-optical spectroscopy, specifically attractive polaron spectroscopy, is used to probe the electronic structure and magnetic ordering under applied electric and magnetic fields.
result: The authors observe a spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase and demonstrate electric-field control over transitions between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders.
conclusion: Twisted bilayer WSe2 provides a platform for studying and controlling topological magnetic phases, with potential applications in quantum devices.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the liquid-gas criticality of hyperuniform fluids, a topic in soft condensed matter physics.
motivation: To understand the unusual critical behavior of hyperuniform fluids, which exhibit suppressed density fluctuations yet high susceptibility at the critical point.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and possibly simulations to characterize the critical properties of hyperuniform fluids composed of spinning particles.
result: Hyperuniform fluids show suppressed fluctuations but enhanced susceptibility at the liquid-vapor critical point, contrasting with ordinary fluids.
conclusion: The work reveals a new class of critical behavior in hyperuniform fluids, relevant to soft matter and statistical physics.

title: Stealthy-Hyperuniform Wave Dynamics In Two-Dimensional Photonic Crystals
authors: Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, and Mikael C. Rechtsman

While disordered stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be largely transparent within a particular range of wavelengths, new experiments on large-scale silicon photonic crystals reveal unexpected residual scattering driven by radiative loss.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021028] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wave dynamics in disordered stealthy hyperuniform photonic crystals, revealing unexpected residual scattering due to radiative loss.
motivation: Stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be transparent in certain wavelength ranges, but experiments show residual scattering that needs explanation.
method: Large-scale experiments on silicon photonic crystals combined with theoretical analysis of wave dynamics and radiative loss.
result: Unexpected residual scattering is driven by radiative loss, contradicting the expectation of near-complete transparency.
conclusion: The findings highlight the importance of radiative loss in disordered photonic crystals and may impact design of transparent materials.

title: Ballistic Spin Valve In Graphene Realized Via Electron Optics
authors: Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, And Ivan J. Vera-Marun
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, and Ivan J. Vera-Marun

Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport, providing a mechanism for coherent spin control through spin-dependent electron optics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021029] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates ballistic spin transport and spin valve behavior in graphene using transverse magnetic focusing, a condensed matter physics result with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To realize coherent spin control in graphene via electron optics, enabling gate-tunable ballistic spin transport.
method: Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene devices to observe spin-dependent electron trajectories.
result: Observation of gate-tunable ballistic spin transport and spin valve effect.
conclusion: Graphene can serve as a platform for spin-based electron optics, but the work is purely in condensed matter physics.

title: Excitations Across The Equilibrium And Photoinduced “Hidden” States Of Magnetoresistive Manganites
authors: Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, And Jonathan Pelliciari
abstract:
Author(s): Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, and Jonathan Pelliciari

Ultrafast photoexcitation in /3Ca1/3MnO3 generates a long-lived hidden phase with unique polaronic and phononic excitations that do not exist under standard equilibrium conditions.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021018] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies photoinduced hidden phases and excitations in magnetoresistive manganites using ultrafast spectroscopy and resonant inelastic X-ray scattering.
motivation: To understand the nature of photoinduced hidden phases in strongly correlated electron systems, which may have implications for controlling material properties.
method: Combines ultrafast optical pump-probe spectroscopy, resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS), and theoretical modeling to characterize excitations in equilibrium and hidden phases.
result: Identifies unique polaronic and phononic excitations in the hidden phase that are absent in equilibrium, revealing a distinct lattice and electronic structure.
conclusion: The hidden phase in manganites exhibits novel excitations, suggesting a new state of matter that can be accessed via photoexcitation.

title: More Is Less In Unpercolated Active Solids
authors: Jack Binysh, Guido Baardink, Jonas Veenstra, Corentin Coulais, And Anton Souslov
abstract:
Author(s): Jack Binysh, Guido Baardink, Jonas Veenstra, Corentin Coulais, and Anton Souslov

By combining experiments with robotic metamaterials and theory, this work shows that increasing microscopic activity can counterintuitively cause a solid’s macroscale active response to vanish when active units are too sparse for the active forces to percolate through the structure.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021012] Published Mon Apr 13, 2026.
tldr: Increasing microscopic activity in a sparse active solid can counterintuitively reduce its macroscopic active response due to lack of percolation.
motivation: To understand how the density of active units affects the collective mechanical response in active solids.
method: Combined experiments with robotic metamaterials and theoretical modeling.
result: When active units are too sparse, increasing activity does not percolate, causing the macroscopic active response to vanish.
conclusion: Sparsity can lead to a 'more is less' effect in active solids, highlighting the role of percolation in active matter.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a quantum algorithm for computing persistence in topological data analysis, claiming exponential speedup.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a powerful tool for understanding data shape, but classical algorithms are computationally expensive. Quantum computing may offer speedups.
method: The authors design a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and sampling techniques to compute persistence diagrams.
result: They prove a provable exponential quantum speedup over classical algorithms for certain problem instances.
conclusion: This work suggests that quantum computers could enable practical topological data analysis for large datasets, though practical implementation remains challenging.

title: Grand Challenge Of Quantum Applications
authors: Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. Mcclean, Thomas O’brien, And Nicholas C. Rubin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. McClean, Thomas O’Brien, and Nicholas C. Rubin

A proposed five-stage framework outlines the path to useful quantum computing, detailing the scientific milestones required to bridge the gap between theory and real-world utility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A high-level perspective piece proposing a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, focusing on scientific milestones rather than technical results.
motivation: To outline a roadmap bridging the gap between current quantum computing capabilities and real-world applications.
method: Conceptual framework based on expert opinion and analysis of the field's progress.
result: A five-stage framework with milestones for quantum utility.
conclusion: The framework provides a structured path but does not present new technical contributions.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, serving as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant with applications in knot theory and quantum gravity, and its approximation is a candidate for quantum advantage.
method: The authors design an end-to-end quantum algorithm that maps the Jones polynomial evaluation to a quantum circuit, including state preparation, unitary evolution, and measurement, and implement it on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: They demonstrate the algorithm on small knots and links, showing agreement with classical simulations and highlighting resource requirements for larger instances.
conclusion: The work provides a practical benchmark for near-term quantum devices and suggests that the Jones polynomial approximation may offer a quantum advantage, but the current implementation is limited to small problem sizes.

title: Photon Catalysis For General Multimode Multi-Photon Quantum State Preparation
authors: Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, And Massimo Frigerio
abstract:
Author(s): Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, and Massimo Frigerio

Using a procedure based on symmetric tensor decomposition, every photonic state can be prepared with realistic experimental tools and a predictable number of steps.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020323] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: A method for preparing arbitrary multimode multi-photon quantum states using symmetric tensor decomposition and photon catalysis.
motivation: Efficient preparation of complex photonic states is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are often limited to specific state families.
method: The authors propose a procedure based on symmetric tensor decomposition to decompose any photonic state into a sequence of elementary operations including photon catalysis, linear optics, and measurements.
result: They show that any multimode multi-photon state can be prepared with a predictable number of steps using realistic experimental tools.
conclusion: The work provides a general and systematic approach to photonic state preparation, potentially enabling new experiments in quantum optics and quantum information.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical studies on 2D van der Waals magnetic materials.
result: The field encompasses ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, spintronics, and multiferroics.
conclusion: 2D van der Waals magnets are a rapidly evolving field with potential for new physics and applications.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: A review of radiation forces and torques in optics and acoustics, focusing on wave-matter interactions and particle manipulation.
motivation: To provide a unified perspective on how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in wave fields induce forces and torques on particles.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on optical and acoustic radiation forces, including trapping, sorting, and pulling effects.
result: Summarizes key mechanisms and applications of radiation forces and torques in both optics and acoustics.
conclusion: The field has broad applications in particle manipulation, but the paper does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from geometric frustration and interference effects.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing findings from multiple studies.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic phenomena including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, unconventional superconductivity, and orbital antiferromagnetism.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for exploring correlated electron physics and may lead to new electronic states.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation, with broad applications to physical systems.
motivation: Spin glasses are a paradigmatic model for complex systems, and understanding their dynamics is crucial for many areas of physics.
method: The paper reviews experimental techniques, theoretical approaches (e.g., mean-field theory, replica method), and large-scale simulations (e.g., Monte Carlo).
result: It highlights the synergy between experiment, theory, and simulation in advancing the field, and identifies open questions.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich area for interdisciplinary research, with implications for other complex systems.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on material candidates and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in candidate materials, discussing their magnetic and topological properties.
result: Highlights key materials such as α-RuCl3 and their chiral edge modes, but does not present new experimental or theoretical results.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids remain an active area of research with promising candidates, but further work is needed to confirm their existence and properties.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to neural network data, but does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding coordinated activity in large neural networks is a key goal in neuroscience, and statistical physics offers tools to model such systems.
method: The review discusses maximum entropy models and renormalization group approaches applied to recordings of thousands of neurons.
result: These methods uncover reproducible collective behaviors in neural networks, bridging theory and experiment.
conclusion: Statistical physics principles can provide predictive power for neural network dynamics, similar to their role in other areas of physics.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of using massive quantum systems to probe gravity, including tests of quantum gravity effects and entanglement mediated by gravity.
motivation: To understand the interplay between quantum mechanics and gravity, which is poorly understood, and to explore whether gravity can cause decoherence or mediate entanglement.
method: Review of theoretical proposals and experimental efforts involving massive quantum systems (e.g., matter-wave interferometry, optomechanics) to test gravitational effects.
result: Summarizes current theoretical models and experimental progress, including tests of gravity-induced decoherence and entanglement generation between massive particles.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems are promising platforms for probing quantum gravity, but further theoretical and experimental work is needed to distinguish between classical and quantum gravity effects.

title: Ising Supercriticality And Universal Magnetocalorics In Spiral Antiferromagnet ${\mathrm{Nd}}_{3}{\mathrm{BWO}}_{9}$
authors: Xinyang Liu, Enze Lv, Xueling Cui, Han Ge, Fangyuan Song, Zhaoming Tian, Gang Su, Kan Zhao, Junsen Xiang, Peijie Sun, And Wei Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyang Liu, Enze Lv, Xueling Cui, Han Ge, Fangyuan Song, Zhaoming Tian, Gang Su, Kan Zhao, Junsen Xiang, Peijie Sun, and Wei Li

An emergent Ising supercritical regime in Nd
[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 246502] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports an Ising supercritical regime in a spiral antiferromagnet Nd3BWO9 with universal magnetocaloric behavior, suggesting potential for sub-Kelvin refrigeration.
motivation: To explore the liquid-gas analogy in magnetic systems and discover new magnetocaloric materials for low-temperature refrigeration.
method: Experimental measurements of magnetization, specific heat, and magnetocaloric effect on single crystals of Nd3BWO9, combined with theoretical modeling.
result: Observation of an Ising supercritical regime with universal scaling of magnetocaloric quantities, and a critical endpoint at low temperatures.
conclusion: The compound exhibits universal thermodynamic behavior analogous to a liquid-gas system and is promising for sub-Kelvin refrigeration applications.

title: Exciton Steering Via Potential Landscape Engineered By Excited Electron-Hole Phase Transition
authors: Yiling Yu, Yan Xu, Volodymyr Turkowski, Bo Liu, Sheng Liu, Yihan Xiang, Yaorong Liu, Chen Shen, Sheng Wang, Talat S. Rahman, Ting Yu, And Jun He
abstract:
Author(s): Yiling Yu, Yan Xu, Volodymyr Turkowski, Bo Liu, Sheng Liu, Yihan Xiang, Yaorong Liu, Chen Shen, Sheng Wang, Talat S. Rahman, Ting Yu, and Jun He

Controlling exciton transport—especially intralayer excitons with strong light-matter interactions—is challenging due to the lack of efficient, tunable driving mechanisms, hindering practical excitonic device development. In this Letter, we demonstrate all-optical steering of intralayer excitons in …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 246901] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates all-optical steering of intralayer excitons in a 2D material using a photoinduced exciton–electron–hole phase transition.
motivation: Controlling exciton transport is challenging due to lack of efficient driving mechanisms, hindering practical excitonic devices.
method: The authors use optical excitation to create a potential landscape via an excited electron-hole phase transition, steering intralayer excitons.
result: They achieve all-optical control of exciton motion, demonstrating steering over micrometer distances.
conclusion: This work provides a new mechanism for exciton manipulation, potentially enabling excitonic circuits and devices.

title: Duality Between Correlation Functions And Wilson Loops In Gauge Theory From Effective Field Theory
authors: Hao Chen, Pier Francesco Monni, Zhaoyan Pang, Gherardo Vita, And Hua Xing Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Chen, Pier Francesco Monni, Zhaoyan Pang, Gherardo Vita, and Hua Xing Zhu

In this Letter, we initiate a systematic study of the [MATH]-point correlation functions (CFs) in gauge theories in the sequential light-cone (SLC) limit. Focusing on QCD, we formulate a factorization theorem for the CF of four vector currents in this limit using tools from soft-collinear effective fie…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 241601] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies correlation functions and Wilson loops in gauge theories using effective field theory, focusing on QCD in the sequential light-cone limit.
motivation: To understand the structure of multi-point correlation functions in gauge theories and their relation to Wilson loops, which is important for high-energy physics but not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use soft-collinear effective field theory (SCET) to derive a factorization theorem for the four-point correlation function of vector currents in the sequential light-cone limit.
result: They establish a duality between correlation functions and Wilson loops in this limit, providing a systematic framework for computing such observables.
conclusion: The work advances the theoretical understanding of gauge theory correlation functions but has no direct application to the user's research interests.

title: Room-Temperature Intrinsic Nonlinear Planar Hall Effect In ${\mathrm{TaIrTe}}_{4}$
authors: Chang Jiang, Fan Yang, Yu Zhao, Jinshan Yang, Peng Yu, Huiying Liu, Yuda Zhang, Zehao Jia, Xiangyu Cao, Li Tian, Jingyi Yan, Zheng Liu, Zhongkai Liu, Xian-Lei Sheng, Cong Xiao, Shengyuan A. Yang, Shaoming Dong, And Faxian Xiu
abstract:
Author(s): Chang Jiang, Fan Yang, Yu Zhao, Jinshan Yang, Peng Yu, Huiying Liu, Yuda Zhang, Zehao Jia, Xiangyu Cao, Li Tian, Jingyi Yan, Zheng Liu, Zhongkai Liu, Xian-Lei Sheng, Cong Xiao, Shengyuan A. Yang, Shaoming Dong, and Faxian Xiu

A room-temperature intrinsic nonlinear planar Hall effect in the nonmagnetic topological semimetal TaIrTe
[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236302] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of an intrinsic nonlinear planar Hall effect in the topological semimetal TaIrTe4 at room temperature, driven by a Berry-connection-polarizability dipole.
motivation: To explore nonlinear transport phenomena in topological semimetals and understand the role of Berry curvature and orbital effects in generating nonlinear Hall signals.
method: Experimental measurement of the nonlinear planar Hall effect in TaIrTe4 under an in-plane magnetic field, combined with theoretical analysis based on Berry-connection polarizability.
result: A room-temperature intrinsic nonlinear planar Hall effect is observed, attributed to an orbital mechanism involving Berry-connection polarizability dipole.
conclusion: The findings reveal a new mechanism for nonlinear Hall effect and highlight TaIrTe4 as a platform for studying nonlinear transport in topological materials.

title: Observation Of Switchable Chiral Magnons In An Altermagnet
authors: Zheyuan Liu, Hodaka Kikuchi, Zijun Wei, Shinichiro Asai, Mechthild Enderle, Ursula B. Hansen, Vasile O. Garlea, Manh D. Le, Gøran J. Nilsen, Igor A. Zaliznyak, And Takatsugu Masuda
abstract:
Author(s): Zheyuan Liu, Hodaka Kikuchi, Zijun Wei, Shinichiro Asai, Mechthild Enderle, Ursula B. Hansen, Vasile O. Garlea, Manh D. Le, Gøran J. Nilsen, Igor A. Zaliznyak, and Takatsugu Masuda

Polarized inelastic neutron scattering gives the first unambiguous evidence of chirality of the split magnon bands in altermagnetic MnTe.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236705] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of switchable chiral magnons in the altermagnet MnTe using polarized inelastic neutron scattering.
motivation: Altermagnets are a newly discovered class of magnetic materials with unique spin-split band structures, and understanding their magnon chirality is important for spintronics.
method: Polarized inelastic neutron scattering was used to measure the magnon spectra of MnTe single crystals, revealing chirality of split magnon bands.
result: Unambiguous evidence of chiral magnons was obtained, and the chirality could be switched by an external magnetic field.
conclusion: The findings establish altermagnets as a platform for chiral magnonics, with potential applications in information processing.

[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062811] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies long-lived metastable states in the 4f13 5d 6s configuration of Yb+ ions using optical pumping and spectroscopy.
motivation: To identify and characterize metastable states in Yb+ that could be useful for precision measurements or quantum information applications.
method: Optical pumping of a single trapped Yb+ ion on a specific transition at 377.5 nm, followed by spectroscopy to probe the metastable states.
result: A wide range of metastable electronic states were prepared and their lifetimes measured.
conclusion: The identified metastable states may serve as resources for future experiments in quantum computing or atomic clocks.

authors: G. Ferioli, P. Lombardi, P. Sekhar, E. Solé Cardona, N. Preti, C. Drevon, N. Antolini, L. Tanzi, G. Modugno, C. Gabbanini, F. Robicheaux, And A. Fioretti

The authors report on the high-resolution spectroscopy of over 700 Rydberg states in
[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062807] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: High-resolution spectroscopy of over 700 Rydberg states in dysprosium using two-color trap depletion spectroscopy and multichannel quantum defect theory.
motivation: To characterize Rydberg states in dysprosium, which is important for applications in quantum simulation and sensing, but the paper focuses on atomic physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Two-color trap depletion spectroscopy in a magneto-optical trap combined with multichannel quantum defect theory analysis.
result: Measured and assigned over 700 Rydberg states, identified six perturbing states belonging to higher ionization limits.
conclusion: The work provides a benchmark for dysprosium Rydberg states, aiding future experiments in quantum simulation and sensing.

title: Bond-rigidity Heterogeneity Induced Anomalous Strong Bond–strong Anharmonicity And Coherent Phonon Transport In The Ultralow Lattice Thermal Conductivity Compounds $X\mathrm{Ag}Y (X=\mathrm{K},\mathrm{Rb},\mathrm{Cs};Y=\mathrm{S},\mathrm{Se},\mathrm{Te})$
authors: Xinrui Li, Yinchang Zhao, Pengfei Sui, Jun Ni, And Zhenhong Dai
abstract:
Author(s): Xinrui Li, Yinchang Zhao, Pengfei Sui, Jun Ni, and Zhenhong Dai

Understanding the microscopic origin of intrinsically low lattice thermal conductivity is crucial for the design of thermoelectric materials. Here, the lattice dynamics and thermal transport of layered [MATH] compou…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214316] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the microscopic origin of ultralow lattice thermal conductivity in layered XAgY compounds through bond-rigidity heterogeneity and anharmonic phonon transport.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic origin of intrinsically low lattice thermal conductivity is crucial for designing thermoelectric materials.
method: The authors perform lattice dynamics and thermal transport calculations, analyzing bond-rigidity heterogeneity and its effect on phonon anharmonicity and coherent transport.
result: They find that bond-rigidity heterogeneity induces anomalous strong bond–strong anharmonicity, leading to ultralow lattice thermal conductivity.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the design of thermoelectric materials with ultralow thermal conductivity.

title: Giant Anomalous Hall Conductivity And Magnetostriction In Heavy-element Substituted Co-based All-$d$ Heusler Alloys
authors: Pengju Wu, Tao Zhu, Chengwu Xie, Hang Li, And Wenhong Wang

Author(s): Pengju Wu, Tao Zhu, Chengwu Xie, Hang Li, and Wenhong Wang

All-[MATH] Heusler alloys are promising candidates for advanced spintronic and magnetoelastic applications, yet many lack the intrinsic large anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) and magnetostriction required for practical device integration. In this work, we systematically investigate the topological tra…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214441] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anomalous Hall conductivity and magnetostriction in heavy-element substituted Co-based Heusler alloys, focusing on topological transport and magnetoelastic properties.
motivation: To find materials with large anomalous Hall conductivity and magnetostriction for spintronic and magnetoelastic devices.
method: Systematic investigation of topological transport and magnetostriction in heavy-element substituted Co-based all-d Heusler alloys using experimental and theoretical methods.
result: The substituted alloys exhibit giant anomalous Hall conductivity and magnetostriction.
conclusion: These materials are promising for advanced spintronic and magnetoelastic applications.

title: Pressure-driven Superconductivity And Unexpected Semiconducting Behavior In Li-Pt Electrides
authors: Xinrui Jia, Yao Sun, Ailing Liu, Shoutao Zhang, Xin Zhong, And Hanyu Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Xinrui Jia, Yao Sun, Ailing Liu, Shoutao Zhang, Xin Zhong, and Hanyu Liu

Lithium-abundant electrides, characterized by the presence of interstitial anionic electrons, have attracted considerable attention owing to their extraordinary properties, including superconductivity. Here, we conduct comprehensive first-principles structure-prediction simulations to investigate th…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214515] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper predicts pressure-driven superconductivity and semiconducting behavior in Li-Pt electrides using first-principles structure prediction.
motivation: To explore the properties of lithium-abundant electrides, which are known for superconductivity, under high pressure.
method: First-principles structure-prediction simulations (e.g., evolutionary algorithms) combined with density functional theory calculations.
result: Identified new Li-Pt compounds with unexpected semiconducting behavior and pressure-induced superconductivity.
conclusion: Li-Pt electrides exhibit rich pressure-driven electronic transitions, offering insights into electride superconductivity.

title: Spin-orbit Torques In Bulk Collinear Antiferromagnets: Complete Classification And Induced Spin Dynamics
authors: Yizhuo Song, Jianting Dong, Jiahao Shentu, Chen Wang, Yurong Su, And Jia Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yizhuo Song, Jianting Dong, Jiahao Shentu, Chen Wang, Yurong Su, and Jia Zhang

Current-induced spin-orbit torques (SOTs) provide a crucial mechanism for the electrical control of antiferromagnetic order. However, SOTs in antiferromagnets (AFMs) and the resulting spin dynamics remain largely unexplored. Here we present a complete classifications of SOTs in bulk collinear AFMs b…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224432] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper classifies spin-orbit torques in bulk collinear antiferromagnets and studies induced spin dynamics.
motivation: Spin-orbit torques offer electrical control of antiferromagnetic order, but their classification and dynamics in antiferromagnets are largely unexplored.
method: The authors present a complete classification of spin-orbit torques in bulk collinear antiferromagnets using symmetry analysis and model the resulting spin dynamics.
result: They provide a full classification of SOTs and demonstrate how they drive spin dynamics in antiferromagnets.
conclusion: This work advances the understanding of electrical control of antiferromagnetic order, relevant for spintronics applications.

title: Probing Magnetic Field Sensitive Criticality In MnP Single Crystals: From Low-field Scaling To High-field Crossover
authors: Nguyen Thi My Duc, Nivarthana W. Y. A. Y. Mudiyanselage, Shirin Mozaffari, Hasitha Suriya Arachchige, Hari Srikanth, David Mandrus, And Manh-Huong Phan

In this study, MnP single crystals were synthesized and comprehensively characterized to elucidate their structural quality, magnetic behavior, magnetocaloric response, and field-dependent critical phenomena along the easy [MATH] axis. High-resolution x-ray diffraction confirmed the orthorhombic MnP-ty…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224433] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnetic field-sensitive criticality and magnetocaloric effects in MnP single crystals, focusing on scaling behavior and phase transitions.
motivation: To understand the critical phenomena and magnetocaloric response of MnP, a material with potential for magnetic refrigeration.
method: Single crystals were synthesized and characterized using X-ray diffraction, magnetization measurements, and analysis of critical exponents via scaling laws.
result: The study reveals low-field scaling behavior and a high-field crossover in the magnetic phase diagram, with detailed critical exponents.
conclusion: MnP exhibits complex magnetic criticality that can be tuned by magnetic field, relevant for magnetocaloric applications.

title: Influence Of Lattice Anharmonicity And Structural Phase Transitions On The Fröhlich Interaction In $\mathrm{CsPbB}{\mathrm{r}}_{3}$: A First-principles Study
authors: Zeli Xu, Simon Thébaud, Marios Zacharias, Laurent Pedesseau, Claudine Katan, And Jacky Even

All-inorganic lead halide perovskites [MATH] (X = Cl, Br, I) exhibit rich structural dynamics, with vibrational properties and electron-lattice interactions still under active investigation due to strong lattice anharmonicity and structural phase transitions. Here we present…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235206] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study of lattice anharmonicity and structural phase transitions on the Fröhlich interaction in CsPbBr3.
motivation: To understand the influence of lattice dynamics and phase transitions on electron-phonon coupling in lead halide perovskites.
method: First-principles calculations using density functional theory and phonon calculations, analyzing anharmonic effects and phase transitions.
result: Lattice anharmonicity and structural phase transitions significantly modify the Fröhlich interaction strength and electron-phonon coupling.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the electron-lattice interactions in CsPbBr3, relevant for optoelectronic applications.

title: Valence Band Satellite, And Temperature-dependent Magnetic And Spectral Study Of $α\text{−}\mathrm{Fe}$
authors: Trishu Verma, Shivani Bhardwaj, And Sudhir K. Pandey

Author(s): Trishu Verma, Shivani Bhardwaj, and Sudhir K. Pandey

We investigate the influence of correlations and plasmonic excitation on the valence band satellite of [MATH]-Fe, along with magnetic and spectral properties as a function of temperature. Coulomb interaction parameters are obtained by systematically employing various schemes within the constrained rand…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245137] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the valence band satellite and temperature-dependent magnetic and spectral properties of α-Fe using DFT+DMFT.
motivation: To understand the role of correlations and plasmonic excitations in the electronic structure of iron.

result: Supratransmission is observed even without linear coupling, with energy propagation arising solely from nonlinear interactions.

result: Quantifies the effects of confinement and finite range, showing deviations from idealized models.
conclusion: The study provides benchmarks for quasi-2D fermionic dimer gases, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

result: Observation of successive transitions to two distinct metallic tetragonal phases, including a nonequilibrium structure with isotropic lattice expansion.
conclusion: Current can induce structural phase transitions that are inaccessible under thermal equilibrium, offering a new route to engineer material phases.

result: Efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, suggesting that such neural networks may be collision resistant.

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.

result: The review categorizes and compares different theoretical approaches, highlighting their strengths and limitations for describing internal conversion.

authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker

method: Review of theoretical models and experimental techniques for detecting spin-dependent exotic interactions.
result: Summarizes current constraints and experimental limits on various spin-dependent interactions.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain an active area of research with potential implications for fundamental physics.

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on the role of surface defects and plasma formation.
motivation: Vacuum breakdown limits the performance of particle accelerators and other high-voltage devices; understanding its mechanism is crucial for improving reliability.
method: The authors synthesize experimental observations and computer simulations to build a coherent mechanistic picture of the breakdown process.
result: They identify that tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact to trigger breakdowns.
conclusion: These insights can help improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational waves and X-ray pulse profiles.
motivation: To understand the behavior of matter at extreme densities found in neutron stars, which is key for nuclear physics and astrophysics.
method: Summarizes recent gravitational-wave detections from binary neutron star mergers and X-ray pulse profile measurements, comparing them to theoretical nuclear equation of state models.
result: Provides constraints on neutron star masses, radii, and central densities, and compares them to predictions from nuclear theory.
conclusion: Neutron star observations offer unique insights into dense matter, but further data are needed to discriminate between equation of state models.
